FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r3.speaker: علي بن نصر وهارون الأعور وعبيد بن عقيل
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r3.claim: These transmitters read with gemination from Abū ʿAmr.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r3.anchor: وروى علي بن نصر وهارون الأعور وعبيد بن عقيل عن أبي عمرو ولتكملوا العدة مشددة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r4.claim: Abū Zayd reports both geminated and light readings from Abū ʿAmr.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r4.anchor: وقال أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو كلاهما: مشددة ومخففة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r5.speaker: اليزيدي وعبد الوارث
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r5.claim: They report that Abū ʿAmr first read with gemination, then returned to the light reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r5.anchor: وقال اليزيدي وعبد الوارث عنه: إنه كان يثقلها، ثم رجع إلى التخفيف

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r6.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r6.claim: These readers use the light form with sukūn on the kāf.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: ولتكملوا العدة بإسكان الكاف خفيفة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r7.claim: Al-Fārisī supports the form from akmala by citing ‘I have completed your religion’ and Aws’s poetry.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r7.anchor: حجة من قرأ: ولتكملوا: قوله : اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r8.claim: He supports the competing form because faʿala and afʿala can substitute for one another, citing waṣṣā/awṣā and al-Nābigha’s ‘fa-kamilat’.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p274/r8.anchor: ومن قال: ولتكملوا العدة فلأن فعل وأفعل كثيرا ما يستعمل أحدهما موضع الآخر

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p93/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p93/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p93/r1.claim: The doubled form presents fasting as repeated through the month until its count is completed.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p93/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن شدد تكرير فعل الصيام في الشهر إلى اتمام عدته

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p93/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p93/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p93/r2.claim: The light form treats Ramadan as one complete unit, supported by the wording about God's completion of the religion.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p93/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن خفف أنه جعل عقد شهر رمضان عقدا واحدا

NASHR:v1p21#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p21#2/r1.claim: The seven modes ease recitation for the community, showing mercy, honor, latitude, and a special favor in response to the Prophet's repeated request.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r1.anchor: فللتخفيف على هذه الأمة وإرادة اليسر بها، والتهوين عليها شرفا لها وتوسعة ورحمة وخصوصية لفضلها

NASHR:v1p21#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASHR:v1p21#2/r2.claim: Gabriel conveyed God's command to recite on one mode; the Prophet repeatedly asked for relief until the allowance reached seven modes, a report found in the Sahih.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r2.anchor: أتاه جبريل فقال له: إن الله يأمرك أن تقرأ أمتك القرآن على حرف فقال: أسأل الله معافاته ومعونته

NASHR:v1p21#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p21#2/r3.claim: An authenticated report says the Quran descended through seven doors on seven modes, whereas earlier scriptures descended through one door on one mode.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r3.anchor: إن القرآن نزل من سبعة أبواب على سبعة أحرف، وإن الكتاب قبله كان ينزل من باب واحد على حرف واحد

NASHR:v1p21#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p21#2/r4.claim: Earlier prophets addressed their own peoples, while Muhammad was sent to all peoples; Arab dialects differed and shifting dialects could be difficult or impossible, especially for the elderly, women, and the unlettered.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r4.anchor: وكانت العرب الذين نزل القرآن بلغتهم لغاتهم مختلفة وألسنتهم شتى ويعسر على أحدهم الانتقال من لغته إلى غيرها

NASHR:v1p21#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r5.speaker: العلماء
NASHR:v1p21#2/r5.claim: Scholars differed on reciting in a non-Arabic language; one reported position permits it only for someone unable to recite Arabic, and the author leaves adjudication to another place.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r5.anchor: اختلف العلماء في جواز القراءة بلغة أخرى غير العربي على أقوال، ثالثها إن عجز عن العربي جاز وإلا فلا

NASHR:v1p21#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r6.speaker: أبو محمد عبد الله بن قتيبة
NASHR:v1p21#2/r6.claim: Ibn Qutaybah explains the modes as God's accommodation of each community's habitual dialect, illustrating dialectal consonant and vowel variation.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r6.anchor: فكان من تيسير الله تعالى أن أمر نبيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بأن يقرئ كل أمة بلغتهم

NASHR:v1p21#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r7.speaker: الهذلي
NASHR:v1p21#2/r7.claim: The Hudhayli dialect says ʿattā ḥīn where other Arabs say ḥattā ḥīn.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r7.anchor: فالهذلي يقرأ (عتى حين) يريد (حتى) هكذا يلفظ بها ويستعملها

NASHR:v1p21#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r8.speaker: الأسدي
NASHR:v1p21#2/r8.claim: The Asadi dialect has the cited forms تعلمون وتعلم وتسود وألم إعهد إليكم.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r8.anchor: والأسدي يقرأ (تعلمون وتعلم وتسود وألم إعهد إليكم)

NASHR:v1p21#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r9.speaker: التميمي والقرشي
NASHR:v1p21#2/r9.claim: Tamim pronounces hamza, while Quraysh does not.

NASHR:v1p21#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21#2/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p21#2/r10.claim: Ibn Qutaybah also cites ishmaam in قيل لهم and غيض الماء, and the beginning of an example for بضاعتنا ردت.
NASHR:v1p21#2/r10.anchor: والآخر يقرأ قيل لهم، وغيض الماء بإشمام الضم مع الكسر، وبضاعتنا ردت بإشمام الكسر

NASHR:v1p90/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p90/r1.claim: The correct transmission chain for al-Misbah goes through al-Zanjani; the claim that Ibn Abi al-Afiyah received it directly from the compiler omits al-Zanjani and is an error noted by Abu Hayyan and Ibn Musdi.
NASHR:v1p90/r1.anchor: هذا هو الصواب في هذا الإسناد، وإن وقع في أن ابن أبي العافية رواه سماعا وقراءة عن المصنف، فإنه وهم سقط منه ذكر الزنجاني

NASHR:v1p209/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p209/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NASHR:v1p209/r1.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Masud urges beautifying the Quran with fine voices and clear Arabic articulation; no grading is stated.
NASHR:v1p209/r1.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: جودوا القرآن وزينوه بأحسن الأصوات وأعربوه، فإنه عربي والله يحب أن يعرب به

NASHR:v1p209/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p209/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p209/r2.claim: Tajwid is the verbal noun of jawwada and quality opposite to poor quality; technically it means accurate, beautiful recitation free of faulty pronunciation.
NASHR:v1p209/r2.anchor: فالتجويد مصدر من جود تجويدا والاسم منه الجودة ضد الرداءة

NASHR:v1p209/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p209/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p209/r3.claim: The community is charged both with understanding the Quran and observing its limits, and with preserving its letters in the transmitted Prophetic Arabic form; ability determines whether a reciter is rewarded, sinful, or excused.
NASHR:v1p209/r3.anchor: متعبدون بتصحيح ألفاظه وإقامة حروفه على الصفة المتلقاة من أئمة القراءة المتصلة بالحضرة النبوية

NASHR:v2p215/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p215/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p215/r5.claim: Abu Amr makes the sin damma in al-yusr and al-ʿusr, including ذو عسرة and the paired al-ʿusra/al-yusra forms.
NASHR:v2p215/r5.anchor: وضم السين من اليسر والعسر أبو عمرو، وكذا ما جاء منه نحو وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى

NASHR:v2p225#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p225#2/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p225#2/r11.claim: Abu Jafar's damma on the sin of اليسر and العسر is cross-referenced, including the related forms in this verse and elsewhere.
NASHR:v2p225#2/r11.anchor: وتقدم مذهب أبي جعفر في ضم سين (اليسر) و (العسر)

NASHR:v2p225#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p225#2/r12.speaker: يعقوب وأبو بكر
NASHR:v2p225#2/r12.claim: Yaqub and Abu Bakr geminate the mim in ولتكملوا العدة; the other readers do not.
NASHR:v2p225#2/r12.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب وأبو بكر بتشديد الميم، وقرأ الباقون بالتخفيف.

QIRAAT-ER:2:185:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:6#1/r1.speaker: Ibn Kathīr
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:6#1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the Qurʾān without hamza, softening the glottal stop in a canonical pronunciation.
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:6#1/r1.anchor: Without hamza — softening of the glottal stop, a well-attested canonical reading (Ibn Kathīr)

QIRAAT-ER:2:185:39#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:39#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:39#1/r1.claim: The ten-reader variant has ḍamma on the sīn in al-yusura instead of sukūn; it is a fuller phonetic form without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:39#1/r1.anchor: With ḍamma on sīn instead of sukūn — fuller phonetic form, no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:2:185:45#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:45#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:45#1/r1.claim: A parallel ḍamma on the sīn in al-ʿusura creates a symmetrical fuller phonetic variant alongside al-yusura.
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:45#1/r1.anchor: With ḍamma on sīn — fuller phonetic form paralleling al-yusura; symmetric variant

QIRAAT-ER:2:185:48#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:48#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:48#1/r1.claim: Form II tukammilū rather than Form IV tukmilū emphasizes thorough, meticulous completion.
QIRAAT-ER:2:185:48#1/r1.anchor: Form II (tukammilū) instead of Form IV (tukmilū) — intensive completion

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r2.claim: A group assimilates the sounds in شهر رمضان; Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that Basran phonological principles disallow meeting the two quiescent consonants here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r2.anchor: وأدغمت فرقة شهر رمضان. قال ابن عطية: وذلك لا تقتضيه الأصول لاجتماع الساكنين فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects limiting Arabic to the majority Basran transmission or preference: soundly transmitted usage must be accepted, as in the cited lengthened form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r3.anchor: إذا صح النقل وجب المصير إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the whole Qur'an descended to the lowest heaven on Ramadan's twenty-fourth night, then was sent down to the Messenger piecemeal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r4.anchor: فعن ابن عباس أنه أنزل جميعه إلى سماء الدنيا ليلة أربع وعشرين من رمضان، ثم أنزل على رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r5.claim: One interpretation takes the descent as the beginning of revelation to the Messenger in Ramadan, with the whole Qur'an named while only part began descending.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r5.anchor: وقيل: الإنزال هنا هو على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فيكون القرآن مما عبر بكله عن بعضه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r6.claim: Another explanation treats the definite article as generic, like saying “I ate meat,” without intending every individual instance of the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r6.anchor: أو تكون الألف واللام فيه لتعريف الماهية، كما تقول: أكلت اللحم، لا تريد استغراق الأفراد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r7.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī explains the descent as Gabriel's Ramadan review of what had been revealed to the Messenger, with God erasing or confirming what He wills.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r7.anchor: وقيل معنى: أنزل فيه القرآن أن جبريل كان يعارض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في رمضان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r8.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r8.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the verse means that the Qur'an was revealed concerning the obligation of fasting, namely “Believers, fasting is prescribed for you.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r8.anchor: والقرآن الذي نزل هو قوله: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم الصيام قاله مجاهد، والضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r9.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r9.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna takes “the Qur'an was sent down in it” to mean that it was sent down concerning Ramadan's merit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r9.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: في فضله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r10.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r10.claim: Muqātil says the Qur'an descended from the Preserved Tablet to the heavenly scribes in the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, and Gabriel brought it down over twenty years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p195/r10.anchor: في ليلة القدر من عشرين شهرا، ونزل به جبريل في عشرين سنة. قاله مقاتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r1.claim: Most readers give the imperative lām in فليصمه sukūn, treating it like a verb form and lightening it, though its underlying vowel is kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بسكون اللام في: فليصمه، أجروا ذلك مجرى: فعل، فخففوا، وأصلها الكسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن والزهري وأبو حيوة وعيسى الثقفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r2.claim: These readers use kasra on the imperative lām here and throughout the Qur'an; Abū Ḥayyān calls this a well-known Arabic usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي، والحسن، والزهري، وأبو حيوة، وعيسى الثقفي، وكذلك قرؤا لام الأمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r3.claim: A report from al-Farrāʾ allows an open imperative lām as an Arabic dialect; his son specifies Banū Sulaym, while another report restricts opening to a following fatḥa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r3.anchor: عن الفراء أن من العرب من يفتح هذه اللام لفتحة الياء بعدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r4.claim: The repeated sick-or-traveling rule had already been explained; if the prior “counted days” refers to Ramadan, that statement made repeating it unnecessary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r4.anchor: وذكر فائدة تكرارها على تقدير: أن شهر رمضان هو قوله: أياما معدودات، فأغنى ذلك عن إعادته هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r5.speaker: صاحب المنتخب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r5.claim: On the literal-will reading, al-Muntakhab supplies an omitted complement: God intends to command what contains ease for you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r5.anchor: يريد الله أن يأمركم بما فيه يسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r6.claim: Alternatively, “intends” can be figurative for “requests”: God requests ease from you, since request and will are distinct in Abū Ḥayyān's doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r6.anchor: وإما أن يتجوز بها عن الطلب، أي: يطلب الله منكم اليسر، والطلب عندنا غير الإرادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r7.claim: The two readings are motivated because, for Sunnis, what God wills must occur although hardship does occur; the Muʿtazilites can retain the verse's apparent sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r7.anchor: لأن ما أراده الله كائن لا محالة، على مذهب أهل السنة، وعلى ظاهر الكلام لم يكن ليقع عسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r8.claim: The verb يَرِيدُ takes physical objects with ب and verbal nouns directly, and can also take the reverse constructions; the cited verse illustrates the ب construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r8.anchor: كالآية. ويأتي أيضا متعديا إلى الأجرام بنفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r9.claim: Rather than treating yurid as past-tense intent, Abū Ḥayyān reads it as an enduring state: the imperfect is ongoing, and divine will is an eternal attribute of essence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r9.anchor: والأولى أن يراد به الحالة الدائمة هنا، لأن المضارع هو الموضوع لما هو كائن لم ينقطع، والإرادة صفة ذات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r10.claim: Ease and hardship are stated generally, covering worldly and otherworldly circumstances.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p198/r10.anchor: وظاهر اليسر والعسر العموم في جميع الأحوال الدنيوية والأخروية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r1.claim: The passage cites the hadith “God's religion is ease, so make things easy, not difficult,” and reports that the Prophet chose the easier of two options when offered them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r1.anchor: دين الله يسر يسر ولا تعسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r2.claim: The ease principle is also linked to the declarations that religion has no hardship and that burdens and shackles were removed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r2.anchor: وفي القرآن: ما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التي كانت عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r3.claim: The general ease includes the sick and traveler being allowed to break the fast; the general hardship includes their fasting amid illness or travel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r3.anchor: فيندرج في العموم في اليسر فطر المريض والمسافر اللذين ذكر حكمهما قبل هذه الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r4.speaker: علي وابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r4.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify ease as breaking the fast while traveling and hardship as fasting then; Abū Ḥayyān treats these as examples within the general rule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r4.anchor: وروي عن علي، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك: أن اليسر الفطر في السفر، والعسر الصوم فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r5.speaker: صاحب المنتخب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r5.claim: Al-Muntakhab says the statement that God intends ease already conveys that He does not intend hardship; the second clause is emphatic repetition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r5.anchor: وفي (المنتخب) يريد الله بكم اليسر كاف عن قوله: ولا يريد بكم العسر وإنما كرر توكيدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ويحيى بن وثاب وابن هرمذ وعيسى بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, Ibn Hurmuz, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read al-yusr and al-ʿusr with ḍamma on the sīn; others use sukūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر، ويحيى بن وثاب، وابن هرمذ، وعيسى بن عمر: اليسر والعسر، بضم السين فيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r7.speaker: أبو بكر وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r7.claim: Abū Bakr and, in one transmission, Abū ʿAmr read with a doubled mīm and fatḥa on kāf; the remaining readers lighten mīm and give kāf sukūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر، وأبو عمرو بخلاف عنهما، وروي: مشدد الميم مفتوح الكاف، والباقون بالتخفيف وإسكان الكاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya analyzes the lām as introducing the delayed object, with an implicit أن: God intends completion of the count; he compares it with a poetic example.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هي اللام الداخلة على المفعول، كالتي في قولك: ضربت لزيد، المعنى، ويريد إكمال العدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī likewise construes “and that you complete” as an object of “He intends,” citing يريدون ليطفئوا as a parallel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r9.anchor: كأنه قيل: يريد الله بكم اليسر، ويريد لتكملوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the delayed-object analysis is rare or poetic; separation from the verb may strengthen the lām, but the proposed insertion of أن after a lām called “extra” is problematic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r10.anchor: أن اللام جاءت في المفعول المؤخر عن الفعل، وهو مما نصوا على أنه قليل، أو ضرورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r11.claim: He corrects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's wording: أن is suppressed after the preposition lām; it is not that the verb itself is estimated with أن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p199/r11.anchor: وفي كلام ابن عطية تتبع، وهو في قوله: وهي، يعني باللام مع الفعل، يعني تكملوا مقدرة بأن، وليس كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1.claim: “The month of Ramadan” may be the subject, with the relative clause as predicate, introducing the obligation by the month’s merit.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1.anchor: رمضان ) مبتدأ خبره الموصول بعده ويكون ذكر الجملة مقدمة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, “whoever witnesses the month” is the predicate, with fā licensed by its conditional sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2.anchor: والفاء لتضمنه معنى الشرط لكونه موصوفا بالموصول

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3.claim: It may predicate an omitted “that is the time when fasting was prescribed,” or identify the prescribed month.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره ذلكم الوقت الذي كتب عليكم الصيام فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4.claim: It may be whole-apposition to fasting, estimating “fasting the month of Ramadan”; the intervening words still relate to “was prescribed.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4.anchor: بدل كل بتقدير مضاف أي كتب عليكم الصيام صيام شهر رمضان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5.claim: An inclusion-apposition avoids estimating a genitive, but is less fitting because the previous fasting ruling is the main point and does not anticipate an apposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5.anchor: وإن اعتبرته بدل اشتمال استغنيت عن التقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6.claim: A reading with “month” in the accusative construes it as the object of an omitted “fast.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6.anchor: وقريء ( شهر ) بالنصب على أنه مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r7.claim: Another accusative parse makes it object of “that you fast,” but this separates parts of the verbal noun construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r7.anchor: مفعول ( وأن تصوموا ) وفيه لزوم الفصل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8.claim: It is also parsed as object of “you know,” estimating the month’s merit; a literal reading means knowing the month itself, which al-Alusi rejects.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8.anchor: وجوز أن يكون مفعول ( تعلمون ) بتقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9.claim: A month is a period beginning with sighting the new moon; “ashhur” is the plural for a few and “shuhur” for many.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9.anchor: المدة المعينة التي ابتداؤها رؤية الهلال ويجمع في القلة على أشهر وفي الكثرة على شهور

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r10.claim: “Month” derives from a root meaning that something appeared, as months mark worship and transactions and become publicly known.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11.claim: Al-Alusi accepts Ramadan as a verbal noun from “to burn”; he faults al-Bahr for denying verbal nouns from intransitive verbs.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11.anchor: فما في البحر من أن كونه مصدرا يحتاج إلى نقل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12.claim: Al-Khalil derives Ramadan from “ramad,” a pre-autumn rain that cleans the earth of dust.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12.anchor: والخليل يقول : إنه من الرمضمسكن الميموهو مطر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13.claim: Al-Alusi says the compound month-name conventionally applies to Ramadan and the two Rabi months.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13.anchor: وبالجملة فقد أطبقوا على أن العلم في ثلاثة أشهر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14.claim: A mnemonic says “month” is added only before names beginning with rāʾ, except Rajab, where that usage was not heard.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14.anchor: وقد نظم ذلك بعضهم فقال : ولا تضف شهرا إلى اسم شهر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r15.claim: The compound analysis derives rules for declension and the article from the second element.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r15.anchor: في الإضافة يعتبر في أسباب منع الصرف وإمتناع اللام

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r16.claim: On that account, bare “Ramadan” in “whoever fasts Ramadan” drops one element of the compound to avoid ambiguity.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r16.anchor: فنحو من صام رمضان من حذف جزء العلم لعدم الإلباس

ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r17.claim: Acceptability of adding a generic noun to a specific one depends on usage and taste, not an absolute rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p59#2/r17.anchor: ولهذا تحسن تارة كشجر الأراك وتقبح أخرى كإنسان زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r1.speaker: أكثر النحويين
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r1.claim: Most grammarians allow “month” to be added to every month-name, contrary to the claim that only three such forms are attested.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r1.anchor: شرح التسهيل جواز إضافة ( شهر ) إلى جميع أسماء الشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r2.speaker: أدب الكاتب
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r2.claim: Adab al-Katib describes the limited forms as a scribal convention from Umar’s calendar, not a rule of language.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r2.anchor: من أنه أصطلاح الكتاب قال : لأنهم لما

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r3.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r3.claim: Sibawayh allows “month” with all month-names: including it is non-generic, while omitting it gives the generic sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r3.anchor: وفرق بين ذكره وعدمه بأنه حيث ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r4.speaker: النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r4.claim: Grammarians report both declinable and indeclinable “Ibn Dayah”; a cited verse illustrates the form, with competing compound analyses.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r4.anchor: ولما رأيت النسر عزإبن داية وعشش في وكريه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r5.claim: Al-Alusi concludes that Ramadan alone is a generic proper name for the known month.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r5.anchor: المعول عليه أن ( رمضان ) وحده علم وهو علم جنس

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r6.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra, both attributed to the Prophet and stopped at the Companion, forbids saying “Ramadan” because it is a divine name; say “month of Ramadan.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا وموقوفا لا تقولوا : رمضان فإن رمضان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r7.claim: Mujahid adopts the prohibition on saying “Ramadan” alone.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r8.claim: Al-Alusi’s correct view permits “Ramadan” alone, citing its use in sound hadith, while acknowledging caution.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r8.anchor: الجوازفقد روى ذلك في الصحيح والإحتياط لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r9.speaker: ابن عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r9.claim: Ibn Amr explains the name by saying sins are burned away in that month.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r9.anchor: لأن الذنوب ترمض فيهقاله إبن عمرو

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r10.speaker: أنس وعائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r10.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet through Anas and Aisha also explains the name by sins burning in Ramadan.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r10.anchor: وروى ذلك أنس وعائشة مرفوعا إلى النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r11.claim: Another explanation is that the month fell during burning heat when ancient month-names were transferred; its old name was Natiq.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r11.anchor: لوقوعه أيام رمض الحر حيث نقلوا أسماء الشهور عن اللغة القديمة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r12.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r12.claim: Ibn Ishaq says revelation of the Qur’an began in Ramadan on the Night of Power.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r12.anchor: وكان ذلك ليلة القدرقاله إبن إسحاق وروي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r13.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Hasan say the Qur’an descended all at once to the lowest heaven, then gradually to earth over twenty-three years.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p60/r13.anchor: عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وإبن جبير والحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r1.claim: Another view understands the Qur’an’s descent in Ramadan as the revelation about Ramadan, namely the command to fast.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r1.anchor: أنزل في شأنه القرآن وهو قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r2.claim: A report from Wathila says Abraham’s scrolls descended on Ramadan’s first night, the Torah on the sixth, the Gospel on the thirteenth, and the Qur’an on the twenty-fourth; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r2.anchor: من حديث وائلة بن الأسقع عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r3.claim: Fasting is a great sign of servitude and removes human attachments that block divine illumination, so the month of revealed scriptures is suited to fasting.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r3.anchor: بين الصوم ونزول الكتب الإلهية مناسبة عظيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r4.claim: “Guidance” and “clear proofs” are circumstantial clauses describing the Qur’an, governed by “was sent down.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r4.anchor: هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان حالان لازمان من القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r5.claim: The Qur’an guides people through its uniquely inimitable character.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r5.anchor: هداية للناس بإعجازه المختص به كما يشعر بذلك التنكير

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r6.claim: It also contains clear signs shared with other revealed books, guiding to truth and distinguishing it from falsehood through divine knowledge and practical rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r6.anchor: آيات واضحات من جملة الكتب الإلهية الهادية إلى الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r7.claim: Another view repeats “guidance” for glorification and emphasis, like saying “a learned expert.”

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r8.claim: “Whoever” may be conditional or relative; the fā is either the conditional answer or extra in the predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r8.anchor: من شرطية أو موصولة والفاء إما جواب الشرط أو زائدة في الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r9.claim: “Among you” is circumstantial to the implicit subject of “witnessed,” excluding children and the insane.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r9.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من المستكن في ( شهد )

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r10.claim: “Witnessed” can mean physical presence or knowledge of the month; both senses are proposed.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r10.anchor: من الشهود والتركيب يدل على الحضور إما ذاتا أو علما

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r11.claim: On physical presence, “the month” is a temporal adverb and the direct object is omitted as irrelevant, not supplied as a town or country.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r11.anchor: على الأول مفعول فيه والمفعول به متروك لعدم تعلق الغرض به

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r12.claim: On the knowledge reading, it is the object with “crescent of” understood; the definite article refers to the known crescent.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r12.anchor: وعلى الثاني مفعول به بحذف المضاف أي هلال الشهر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r13.claim: The explicit noun replaces a pronoun to honor the month.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r14.claim: The attached pronoun is accusative by extended usage although “to fast” is normally intransitive.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r15.claim: On the presence reading, a non-traveler present during Ramadan must fast; on the knowledge reading, whoever knows the crescent with certainty must fast.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r15.anchor: فمن حضر في الشهر ولم يكن مسافرا فليصم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r16.claim: The knowledge reading implies that fasting is not obligatory when the new moon is uncertain.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r16.anchor: عدم وجوب الصوم على من شك في الهلال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r17.claim: Witnessing the whole month would occur only after it ended, motivating the estimate “crescent” on the knowledge reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r17.anchor: إنما قدر المضاف لأن شهود الشهر بتمامه إنما يكون بعد انقضائه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r18.claim: The sick-and-traveler concession specifies both groups on the knowledge reading, but only the sick on the presence reading because travelers were already excluded.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r18.anchor: وعلى الأول مخصص بالنظر إلى الأول دون الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r19.claim: The repeated concession serves that specification or prevents an assumption of abrogation, linking back to the earlier fasting verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r19.anchor: لئلا يتوهم نسخه كما نسخ قرينه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r20.claim: Al-Alusi prefers physical presence because it needs no estimated word and places the fā as expected, detailing the earlier general command.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p61/r20.anchor: ورجح المعنى الأول من المعنيين بعدم الاحتياج إلى التقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r1.claim: The month’s obligation entails honoring it through fasting for everyone who reaches it, whether resident or traveling; a resident’s ruling is to fast.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r1.anchor: من وجوب التعظيم المستفاد مما في أثره على كل من أدركه ومدركه إما حاضر أو مسافر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r2.claim: Witnessing the month means reaching or experiencing it; it is not well paraphrased as merely knowing that the crescent appeared.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r2.anchor: ولا يحسن أن يقال من علم الهلال فليصم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r3.claim: One objection says the detailed coordinating conjunction makes the sick and traveling a category distinct from those who witnessed the month.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r3.anchor: والعاطف التفصيلي يقتضي المغايرة بينهما كذا قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r4.speaker: أكثر النحويين
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r4.claim: Mention of the sick supports treating them as a specification of those who witnessed; most grammarians parse “the month” as object, making the fa causal or sequential rather than explanatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r4.anchor: أكثر النحويين إلى أن الشهر مفعول به

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r5.claim: God’s ease-giving and rejection of hardship express His abundant mercy and compassion in making this exception.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r6.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer that a person can do what God does not will: a sick or traveling person who fasts to exhaustion acts against the ease God wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r6.anchor: وأستدل المعتزلة بالآية على أنه قد يقع من العبد ما لا يريده الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r7.claim: The rebuttal is that God wills ease by permitting the sick and traveler to break the fast; the permission is fulfilled by the command to make up the days.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r7.anchor: ورد بأن الله تعالى أراد التيسير وعدم التعسير في حقهما بإباحة الفطر وقد حصل بمجرد الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r8.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r8.claim: Al-Baḥr interprets divine willing here as demanding; al-Alusi says this entails the Muʿtazilite view that God’s will concerning human acts is command.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r8.anchor: وفي البحر تفسير الإرادة هنا بالطلب وفيه إلتزام لمذهب الإعتزال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r9.claim: The lām clauses can be attached to an implied “He legislated,” signaled by the fasting command: complete the month’s count by fasting it when present and making up excused missed days without loss.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r9.anchor: فعل محذوف دل عليه ( فمن شهد منكم الشهر ) إلخ أي وشرع لكم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r10.claim: Completing the count preserves the month’s blessings and rewards whether the month has fewer days or is complete.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r10.anchor: فتحصلوا خيراته ولا يفوتكم شيء من بركاته نقصت أيامه أو كملت

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r11.claim: Another analysis treats each lām as the reason for its own implied act: God obligated make-up days, taught their method, and granted the exemption.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r11.anchor: وجوز أن تكون عللا لأفعال مقدرة كل فعل مع علة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r12.claim: He links takbīr to the make-up ruling and gratitude to the concession; shifting to “perhaps” subtly presents gratitude as hoped-for despite strong grounds for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p62/r12.anchor: علة الترخيص والتيسير وتغيير الأسلوب للإشارة إلى هذا المطلوب بمنزلة المرجو

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r1.claim: The clauses may instead depend on an implied “so it is easy for you” or “so you may know what to do”; some are rationale by way of making the preceding rulings clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r1.anchor: ليسهل أو لتعلموا علة لما سبق بإعتبار الإعلام

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r2.claim: A further option attaches the lām clauses to “ease” after “God wills,” taking the lām as purposive and possibly extra after a verb of willing.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r2.anchor: واللام زائدة مقدرة بعدها أن وزيدت كما قيل : بعد فعل الإرادة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r3.claim: A reported analysis takes the lām as equivalent to “that,” but then gratitude must coordinate with “He wills,” producing an incoherent construction and disconnected clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r3.anchor: إنها بمعنى أن كما في الرضى إلا أنه يلزم على هذا الوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r4.claim: Some avoid the earlier parses by understanding an ellipsis: God granted the concession because He wills ease, while completing the count and gratitude explain the rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r4.anchor: عدل بعضهم عن الجميع وجعل الكلام من الميل مع المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r5.claim: “Takbīr” here figuratively means praise and glorification, of which declaring God greatest is one kind; the preposition “upon” fits this meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r5.anchor: والمراد من التكبير الحمد والثناء مجازا لكونه فردا منه ولذلك عدى بعلي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that the takbīr is the glorification on the day of Eid.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r6.anchor: وأخرج إبن المنذر وغيره عن زيد بن أسلم أن المراد به التكبير يوم العيد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r7.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to say that the takbīr is made on sighting the crescent of Shawwāl.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r8.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Muslims should glorify God upon seeing Shawwāl’s crescent until Eid ends, citing the verse; al-Alusi notes this reading does not explain the prior rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r8.anchor: حق على المسلمين إذا نظروا إلى هلال شوال أن يكبروا الله تعالى حتى يفرعوا من عيدهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r9.claim: The particle “mā” may be a verbal noun (“for His guiding you”) or a relative pronoun (“that to which He guided you”).
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r9.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون مصدرية وأن تكون موصولة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r10.claim: Gratitude includes more than verbal praise, making it an apt rationale for the practical gift of the concession.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r10.anchor: والمراد من الشكر ما هو أعم من الثناء ولذا ناسب أن يجعل طلبه تعليلا للترخيص

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r11.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r11.claim: Abū Bakr’s transmission from ʿĀṣim reads “litukammilū” with a doubled mīm.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63/r11.anchor: أبو بكر عن عاصم ( ولتكملوا ) بالتشديد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r1.claim: The nominative شهر رمضان is parsed as an implied هو شهر رمضان, while al-Kisa’i supplies كتب عليكم شهر رمضان.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r1.anchor: رفعه على معنى هو شهر رمضان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r2.claim: The word شهر is linked to شهرة, because the month is well known.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r3.claim: Mujahid says Ramadan is one of God’s names, as in calling it the month of God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: هو اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r4.claim: Baghawī prefers that Ramadan names the month from الرمضاء, the scorching stones, since people fasted in intense heat and the stones grew hot.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r4.anchor: والصحيح أنه اسم للشهر سمي به من الرمضاء وهي الحجارة المحماة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r5.claim: The Qur’an is so named because it gathers its chapters, verses, and letters, as well as narratives, commands, prohibitions, promises, and warnings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r5.anchor: سمي القرآن قرآنا لأنه يجمع السور والآي والحروف وجمع فيه القصص والأمر والنهي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r6.claim: The root قرء means gathering; the idiom قريت الماء describes gathering water in a basin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r6.anchor: وأصل القرء الجمع وقد يحذف الهمز منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r7.speaker: ابن كثير والشافعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads القران without hamza and with fatḥa on rā’; al-Shāfiʿī also read it so and considered it the book’s proper name, like Torah and Gospel, rather than a derivative of recitation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير: القران بفتح الراء غير مهموز، وكذلك كان يقرأ الشافعي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the whole Qur’an descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven’s Bayt al-ʿIzza on Laylat al-Qadr, then Gabriel delivered it to Muhammad in stages over twenty-three years.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r8.anchor: ابن عباس: أنه سئل عن قوله عز وجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r9.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r9.claim: Al-Shaʿbī explains the Ramadan wording by saying Gabriel reviewed with Muhammad during Ramadan what had already been revealed, while God confirms, erases, or causes what He wills to be forgotten.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198/r9.anchor: قلت للشعبي: {شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن} أما كان ينزل في سائر الشهور؟ قال: بلى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r1.claim: A report from Abū Dharr dates the scriptures’ descents to Ramadan: Abraham’s pages on the third night (also said the first), Torah on the sixth, Gospel on the thirteenth, Psalms on the eighteenth, and the Furqān on the twenty-fourth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r1.anchor: وروي عن أبي ذر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أنزلت صحف إبراهيم عليه السلام في ثلاث ليال مضين من رمضان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r2.claim: The Qur’an guides people away from error; grammatically, hudan is accusative by way of القطع because القرآن is definite and هدى indefinite.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r2.anchor: {هدى للناس} من الضلالة، وهدى في محل نصب على القطع لأن القرآن معرفة وهدى نكرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r3.claim: The clear signs are explanations of the lawful and unlawful, the legal limits, and rulings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r3.anchor: {وبينات من الهدى} أي دلالات واضحات من الحلال والحرام والحدود والأحكام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p198#2/r4.claim: Al-Furqān is that which distinguishes truth from falsehood.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r1.claim: The phrase initially concerns someone resident in town when the month begins and who encounters it there.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r1.anchor: أي فمن كان مقيما في الحضر فأدركه الشهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r2.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r2.claim: ʿAlī, joined by ʿUbayda al-Salmānī, says one who entered Ramadan resident may not break the fast after starting a journey, since he witnessed the month and must fast it all.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r2.anchor: روي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لا يجوز له الفطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r3.speaker: أكثر الصحابة والفقهاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r3.claim: Most Companions and jurists permit breaking the fast when a person begins a journey during Ramadan; the verse means to fast the whole month if all of it was witnessed, and otherwise to fast the days witnessed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r3.anchor: وذهب أكثر الصحابة والفقهاء إلى أنه إذا أنشأ السفر في شهر رمضان جاز له أن يفطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet fasted on the conquest journey to Mecca until al-Kadīd, then broke his fast and the people did too; people followed the Prophet’s later action.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج إلى مكة عام الفتح في رمضان فصام حتى بلغ الكديد ثم أفطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r1.claim: Illness and travel permit postponing the fast and making up the same number of days; the repeated wording shows this ruling remains established in both the abrogating and abrogated rulings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r1.anchor: أباح الفطر لعذر المرض والسفر وأعاد هذا الكلام ليعلم أن هذا الحكم ثابت في الناسخ ثبوته في المنسوخ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r2.speaker: أهل الظاهر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r2.claim: The Ẓāhirīs, as did Ibn Sīrīn, hold that any condition called an illness permits breaking the fast.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r2.anchor: فذهب أهل الظاهر إلى أن ما يطلق عليه اسم المرض يبيح الفطر وهو قول ابن سيرين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r3.speaker: طريف بن تمام العطاردي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r3.claim: Ṭarīf ibn Tammām says he found Ibn Sīrīn eating in Ramadan because his finger hurt, illustrating the broad illness threshold.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r3.anchor: قال طريف بن تمام العطاردي دخلت على محمد بن سيرين. في رمضان، وهو يأكل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r4.speaker: الحسن وإبراهيم النخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī define the relevant illness as one that permits praying while seated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن وإبراهيم النخعي هو المرض الذي تجوز معه الصلاة قاعدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r5.claim: Most scholars require a fear that fasting will cause an intolerable worsening of illness; one who is strained by fasting may break it, but one not strained is like a healthy person.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r5.anchor: وذهب الأكثرون إلى أنه مرض يخاف معه من الصوم زيادة علة غير محتملة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r6.speaker: عامة أهل العلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r6.claim: The generality of scholars permit travel fasting and regard it as valid.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r6.anchor: فالفطر فيه مباح والصوم جائز عند عامة أهل العلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة وعروة بن الزبير وعلي بن الحسين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayra, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn say fasting while travelling is impermissible and requires making up the day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r7.anchor: إلا ما روي عن ابن عباس وأبي هريرة وعروة بن الزبير وعلي بن الحسين أنهم قالوا لا يجوز الصوم في السفر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r8.claim: The Prophet’s statement that fasting in travel is not righteousness is cited by those forbidding it; Baghawī explains it as addressing a traveller whom fasting exhausts, for whom breaking the fast is better.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r8.anchor: واحتجوا بقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ليس من البر الصوم في السفر"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r9.claim: A report describes the Prophet seeing a crowd and a man shaded during a journey; when told he was fasting, he said fasting in travel was not righteousness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r9.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفر فرأى زحاما ورجلا قد ظلل عليه فقال ما هذا؟ قالوا هذا صائم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r10.claim: Baghawī reconciles the prohibition report with permissibility by applying it to a traveller burdened by fasting, who is better off breaking the fast.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r10.anchor: وذلك عند الآخرين في حق من يجهده الصوم فالأولى له أن يفطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r11.speaker: أبو سعيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r11.claim: Abū Saʿīd says the Prophet’s travelling party included both fasters and non-fasters, and neither group criticized the other.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p199#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: "كنا نسافر مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في رمضان فمنا الصائم ومنا المفطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r1.speaker: ابن عمر وسعيد بن المسيب والشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, and al-Shaʿbī hold that breaking the fast is better than fasting on a journey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r1.anchor: فقالت طائفة: الفطر في السفر أفضل من الصوم، روي ذلك عن ابن عمر وإليه ذهب سعيد بن المسيب والشعبي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل وأنس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r2.claim: A group, including Muʿādh ibn Jabal and Anas, prefer fasting while travelling; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr also hold this view.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r2.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن الصوم أفضل وروي ذلك عن معاذ بن جبل وأنس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وعمر بن عبد العزيز
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r3.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz say the better option is whichever is easier for the traveller.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r3.anchor: أيسرهما عليه لقوله تعالى: {يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر} وهو قول مجاهد وقتادة وعمر بن عبد العزيز

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r4.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r4.claim: Most scholars say someone who began the day resident and fasting may not break that day after travelling.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r4.anchor: ومن أصبح مقيما صائما ثم سافر في أثناء النهار لا يجوز له أن يفطر ذلك اليوم عند أكثر أهل العلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r5.speaker: الشعبي وأحمد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and Aḥmad permit the person who began fasting as a resident to break the fast after setting out during the day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r5.anchor: وقالت طائفة: له أن يفطر، وهو قول الشعبي وبه قال أحمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r6.claim: Scholars agree that a traveller who began the day fasting may break the fast later that day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r6.anchor: أما المسافر إذا أصبح صائما فيجوز له أن يفطر بالاتفاق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r7.claim: On the conquest journey, the Prophet drank water after the afternoon at Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm when fasting had become hard for the people; some followed suit and some kept fasting, and he called those who continued disobedient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r7.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج إلى مكة عام الفتح في رمضان، فصام حتى بلغ كراع الغميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r8.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r8.claim: Some set the journey that permits breaking the fast at one day’s travel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r8.anchor: واختلفوا في السفر الذي يبيح الفطر، فقال قوم: مسيرة يوم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r9.speaker: الشافعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r9.claim: A group, including al-Shāfiʿī, sets the travel threshold at two days’ journey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r9.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى مسيرة يومين، وهو قول الشافعي رحمه الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r10.speaker: سفيان الثوري وأصحاب الرأي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r10.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī and the jurists of opinion set the threshold at three days’ travel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p200/r10.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى مسيرة ثلاثة أيام، وهو قول سفيان الثوري وأصحاب الرأي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r1.claim: God’s intention of ease is shown by permitting the sick and traveller to break the fast.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r1.anchor: اليسر} بإباحة الفطر في المرض والسفر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads al-ʿusr and al-yusr, and similar words, with ḍamma on sīn; other readers use sukūn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر: العسر واليسر ونحوهما بضم السين، وقرأ الآخرون بالسكون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r3.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says that whenever a person chooses the easier of two options, it is the one God loves more.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r3.anchor: وقال الشعبي: ما خير رجل بين أمرين فاختار أيسرهما إلا كان ذلك أحبهما إلى الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r4.claim: Abū Bakr reads tukmilū with a doubled mīm; the other readers read it lightly, which Baghawī prefers by analogy with 5:3.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر بتشديد الميم وقرأ الآخرون بالتخفيف، وهو الاختيار لقوله تعالى: "اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r5.claim: The wāw coordinates the clause and the lām marks purpose: God wills that people complete the count by making up days missed through illness or travel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r5.anchor: واو النسق، واللام لام كي، تقديره: ويريد لكي تكملوا العدة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r6.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets completing the count as completing the number of days in the month.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء: {ولتكملوا العدة} أي عدد أيام الشهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet’s instruction that the month can be twenty-nine days; begin and end fasting by sighting the crescent, and complete thirty if it is obscured.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "الشهر تسع وعشرون فلا تصوموا حتى تروا الهلال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r8.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that one should not begin Ramadan one or two days early except for a habitual fast, and should complete thirty days if the crescent is obscured.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تقدموا الشهر بصوم يوم ولا يومين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r1.claim: Takbīr here means magnifying and exalting God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r2.claim: The guidance is God’s direction to the approved practice of Ramadan fasting, a privilege distinguishing this community from other religious communities.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r2.anchor: أرشدكم إلى ما رضي به من صوم شهر رمضان وخصكم به دون سائر أهل الملل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the takbīrs as those of the night of Eid al-Fiṭr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو تكبيرات ليلة الفطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r4.speaker: الشافعي وابن المسيب وعروة وأبو سلمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwa, and Abū Salama are reported to proclaim takbīr aloud on Eid night; the night is likened to Eid al-Aḍḥā, except that pilgrims say the talbiya.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن الشافعي وعن ابن المسيب وعروة وأبي سلمة أنهم كانوا يكبرون ليلة الفطر يجهرون بالتكبير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r5.claim: The verse calls people to thank God for His blessings.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that at Ramadan the devils are chained, the gates of Paradise opened, and the gates of Hell closed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا دخل رمضان صفدت الشياطين، وفتحت أبواب الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r7.claim: A second Abū Hurayra report says that on Ramadan’s first night devils and rebellious jinn are chained, Hell’s gates shut, Paradise’s gates open, a caller summons good and restrains evil, and people are freed from the Fire nightly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا كان أول ليلة في شهر رمضان صفدت الشياطين ومردة الجن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r8.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that whoever fasts Ramadan, prays during it, or stands on Laylat al-Qadr in faith and expectation of reward is forgiven past sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p201#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من صام رمضان إيمانا واحتسابا غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r1.claim: Shahr Ramadan is a subject whose predicate follows; the sentence highlights the month’s virtue and explains why its fast was prescribed.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r1.anchor: مبتدأ خبره ما بعده فيكون المقصود من ذكر هذه الجملة المنبهة على فضله ومنزلته

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r2.claim: The fast of Ramadan is obligatory for whoever witnesses the month, as stated in the verse’s following command.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r2.anchor: ثم أوجب صومه بقوله : {فمن شهد منكم الشهر}

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r3.claim: The Arabic word for month is shahr because the month is widely known; Ramadan is a verbal noun from ramida, to burn, and the compound is a proper name made diptote by its ending.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r3.anchor: ورمضان مصدر رمض إذا احترق فأضيف إليه الشهر وجعل المجموع علما

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r4.claim: Ramadan may be named for livers burning from hunger and thirst, sins burning away through fasting, or the month’s occurrence during intense heat.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r4.anchor: وإنما سمي بذلك إما لارتماض الأكباد واحتراقها من الجوع والعطش وإما لارتماض الذنوب بالصيام فيه أو لوقوعه أيام رمض الحر

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r5.claim: One account says month names were borrowed from an older language and assigned according to the season at naming, as with Ramadan’s hot days, spring, and frozen water in Jumada.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r5.anchor: قيل : إنهم نقلوا أسماء الشهور من اللغة القديمة فسموها بالأزمنة التي وقعت هي فيها وقت التسمية

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r6.claim: An alternative view holds that Ramadan is one of God’s names; a Prophetic report therefore advises saying “the month of Ramadan,” not “Ramadan came” or “Ramadan went.”
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r6.anchor: أو رمضان اسم من أسماء الله تعالى والشهر مضاف إليه

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r7.claim: The Qur’an first descended to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brought it down in portions over twenty-three years according to divine will.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r7.anchor: جملة إلى بيت العزة في السماء الدنيا ثم نزل به جبريل نجوما في ثلاث وعشرين سنة حسبما تقتضيه المشيئة الربانية

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r8.claim: A Prophetic report dates the Scrolls of Abraham to Ramadan’s first night, the Torah to its sixth day, the Gospel to its thirteenth, and the Qur’an to its twenty-fourth.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r8.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام : "نزلت صحف إبراهيم أول ليلة من رمضان وأنزلت التوراة لست مضين منه

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r9.claim: Qur’an derives from qarʾ, gathering, because it brings together the knowledge of earlier and later people.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r9.anchor: والقرآن من القرء وهو الجمع لأنه مجمع علم الأولين والآخرين

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r10.claim: The Qur’an was sent as guidance for people to the straight path, through its inimitability and other features.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r10.anchor: أي : أنزل حال كونه هداية للناس إلى سواء الصراط بما فيه من الإعجاز وغيره

BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r11.claim: The Qur’an also contains clear signs guiding to truth and distinguishing it from falsehood through its wisdom and rulings; guidance has more than one category.
BURSEVI:v1p238#2/r11.anchor: أي : وحال كونه آيات واضحات مما يهدي إلى الحق

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r1.claim: “Month of Ramadan” may be a subject followed by its predicate, the predicate of an omitted subject, or an appositive to fasting with “fast of” understood; the accusative reading supplies an imperative or object analysis, though that is weak, or apposition to the numbered days.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r1.anchor: { شهر رمضان } مبتدأ خبره ما بعده، أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r2.claim: Month derives from being renowned; Ramadan is a verbal noun from burning, made the month’s proper name and diptote because it is a name ending in alif and nūn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r2.anchor: والشهر: من الشهرة، ورمضان: مصدر رمض إذا احترق

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r3.claim: The name may refer to fasting in heat, burning away sins, or the hot days when month names were transferred from the old calendar.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r3.anchor: إما لارتماضهم فيه من حر الجوع والعطش، أو لارتماض الذنوب فيه،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r4.claim: The Prophetic phrase “fasted Ramadan” omits the word “month,” since the meaning is unambiguous.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r4.anchor: " من صام رمضان " فعلى حذف المضاف لأمن الالتباس

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r5.claim: One explanation is that revelation of the Qur’an began in Ramadan on the Night of Decree.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r5.anchor: أي ابتدىء فيه إنزاله، وكان ذلك ليلة القدر،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r6.claim: Another explanation is that the Qur’an descended all at once to the lowest heaven in Ramadan, then came down piecemeal to earth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r6.anchor: أو أنزل فيه جملة إلى سماء الدنيا ثم نزل منجما إلى الأرض،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r7.claim: A third explanation is that the Qur’an was revealed concerning Ramadan, namely the command to fast.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r7.anchor: أو أنزل في شأنه القرآن وهو قوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r8.claim: A report from the Prophet dates Abraham’s scrolls to Ramadan’s first night, the Torah to its sixth, the Gospel to its thirteenth, and the Qur’an to its twenty-fourth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r8.anchor: " نزلت صحف إبراهيم عليه السلام أول ليلة من رمضان،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r9.claim: The relative clause is either the predicate or an adjective of the subject; the predicate is then “whoever witnesses,” with fa signaling its conditional sense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r9.anchor: والموصول بصلته خبر المبتدأ أو صفته والخبر فمن شهد،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r10.claim: That the Qur’an was revealed in Ramadan suggests revelation is why this month was singled out for obligatory fasting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r10.anchor: وفيه إشعار بأن الإنزال فيه سبب اختصاصه بوجوب الصوم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r11.claim: The Qur’an is guidance through its inimitability, clear proofs that guide to truth, and judgments and rulings distinguishing truth from falsehood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r11.anchor: حالان من القرآن، أن أنزل وهو هداية للناس بإعجازه وآيات واضحات

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r12.claim: Whoever is present during the month and is not traveling must fast then; explicit mention of the month magnifies it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r12.anchor: فمن حضر في الشهر ولم يكن مسافرا فليصم فيه،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r13.claim: In the main reading, “the month” is an adverb with an omitted preposition, while the second pronoun is accusative by expanded usage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r13.anchor: لكن وضع المظهر موضع المضمر الأول للتعظيم، ونصب على الظرف

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r14.claim: Alternatively, witnessing means seeing the crescent, with the month as a direct object, like witnessing Friday’s prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r14.anchor: وقيل: { فمن شهد منكم } هلال الشهر فليصمه، على أنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r15.claim: The make-up rule specifies the crescent interpretation, since the ill and traveler also witness the month; repetition may prevent assuming abrogation with its counterpart.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r15.anchor: مخصصا له، لأن المسافر والمريض ممن شهد الشهر ولعل تكريره لذلك،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r16.claim: God intends ease rather than hardship, so He permits breaking the fast during travel or illness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r16.anchor: أي يريد أن ييسر عليكم ولا يعسر، فلذلك أباح الفطر في السفر والمرض.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r17.claim: The purpose clauses may explain an omitted verb for the whole ruling: completing the count concerns observing it, takbīr concerns making up missed days, and gratitude concerns the dispensation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r17.anchor: علل لفعل محذوف دل عليه ما سبق، أي وشرع جملة ما ذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r18.claim: Alternatively, each purpose clause may attach to its own action, to an implied rationale such as ease, or to “ease” itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r18.anchor: أو الأفعال كل لفعله، أو معطوفة على علة مقدرة مثل ليسهل عليكم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r19.claim: The purpose phrase may coordinate with “ease,” meaning God intends ease so that you complete the count, as in the cited verse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185/r19.anchor: ويجوز أن يعطف على اليسر أي ويريد بكم لتكملوا كقوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r1.claim: The coordination with ease is compared with the verse “They wish to extinguish God’s light,” cited as a parallel construction.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r2.claim: Takbīr means magnifying God with praise and commendation; “upon” fits this sense.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r3.claim: One alternative takes the takbīr to be the takbīr on Eid al-Fitr.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r4.claim: Another alternative takes it to be the takbīr when the new moon is sighted.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r5.claim: The clause may be construed as a verbal noun, with its predicate meaning what God guided you to.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r5.anchor: وما يحتمل المصدر، والخبر أي الذي هداكم إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r6.speaker: عاصم برواية أبي بكر
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:185#2/r6.claim: In Abū Bakr’s transmission from ʿĀṣim, tukmilū is read with a doubled mīm.

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r1.claim: The verse first names guidance as a genus, then singles out its clear kinds; this honorific coordination intensifies the description through three levels, and the clear mode is the superior division.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r1.anchor: والأول أفضل القسمين فذكر الجنس أولا ثم أردفه

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r2.claim: Witnessing the month here means being present at one's place of residence, whether a town or village.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r2.anchor: حضر موضع الإقامة من المصر أو القرية

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r3.claim: Al-shahr is accusative as a temporal adverb, not an object, because both residents and travelers witness the month.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r3.anchor: منصوب على الظرف أي : في الشهر دون المفعول به

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r4.claim: The phrase means let him fast in it: a preposition is omitted and the verb is extended directly to the governed noun.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r4.anchor: فليصم فيه بحذف الجار وإيصال الفعل إلى المجرور اتساعا

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r5.claim: The resident who must fast is a rational, mature, healthy person; children and the insane may be present in town but are not obligated.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r5.anchor: والمراد بالشاهد العاقل البالغ الصحيح لأن كل واحد

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r6.claim: This binding command abrogates the resident's former choice between fasting, breaking the fast, and paying fidya.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r6.anchor: ينسخ التخيير بين الصوم والإفطار والفداء

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r7.claim: The illness concession applies even to a resident, and the travel concession even to a healthy person; ʿalā here means fī.

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r8.claim: A sick person or traveler who breaks the fast must make up the missed days later.

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r9.claim: The earlier verse allowed residents able to fast, travelers, and the sick to choose; this verse removes the resident's choice, so the concession is restated to show it remains for the sick and traveler.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r9.anchor: وأعاد تخيير المريض والمسافر وترخيصهما في الإفطار

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r10.claim: God intends ease by permitting breaking the fast during travel or illness; yusr means what is made easy.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r10.anchor: حيث أباح الفطر بالسفر والمرض واليسر ما تسهل

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r11.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r11.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reads ease as Paradise and hardship as Hell: fasting is intended to bring the servant into Paradise and spare him entry into Hell.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r11.anchor: قال محمد بن علي الترمذي قدس سره : اليسر اسم الجنة

BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r12.speaker: الفضلي
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r12.claim: Al-Faḍlī says fasting brings ease in both abodes: worldly spiritual ascent and wakefulness toward knowledge, then Paradise, blessing, nearness, union, and vision; hardship is worldly animal and ego-bound life, then Hell and its torments.
BURSEVI:v1p238#3/r12.anchor: قال شيخنا العلامة الفضلي قدس سره في الآية أن مراده تعالى بأن يأمركم بالصوم

BURSEVI:v1p239/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r1.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v1p239/r1.claim: Najm al-Dīn says to attend to the ease that accompanies hardship while obeying a command; like a patient taking bitter medicine for health, the wise focus on its benefit and drink with resolve.
BURSEVI:v1p239/r1.anchor: وقال نجم الدين في "تأويلاته" : يعني يريد الله بكم

BURSEVI:v1p239/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r2.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p239/r2.claim: Saʿdī's couplet illustrates that a wise physician's bitter medicine is beneficial, like sugar given to a sick person.
BURSEVI:v1p239/r2.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : وبالست دادن برنجور قند

BURSEVI:v1p239/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p239/r3.claim: Completing the prescribed total means making up the days missed because of illness or travel after Ramadan's fast was imposed.
BURSEVI:v1p239/r3.anchor: فعليكم عدة ما أفطرتم لتكملوا عدد أيام الشهر

BURSEVI:v1p239/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p239/r4.claim: The instruction to make up fasts on later days leaves their arrangement unrestricted, so they may be consecutive or separated; magnifying God means praising Him.

BURSEVI:v1p239/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p239/r5.claim: Mā is a verbal noun: the phrase means praising God for guiding you to a way of discharging the duty.
BURSEVI:v1p239/r5.anchor: ما مصدرية أي : على هدايته إياكم إلى طريق الخروج

BURSEVI:v1p239/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p239/r6.claim: The fast-breaking concession is granted so that people thank God for this blessing with tongue, heart, and body.
BURSEVI:v1p239/r6.anchor: إنما رخصنا لكم بالإفطار لكي تشكروا الله

BURSEVI:v1p239/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p239/r7.claim: A hadith says whoever keeps three things is truly God's friend, and whoever neglects them is truly God's enemy: prayer, fasting, and the bath after major ritual impurity; no grading is given.

BURSEVI:v1p239/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
