BURSEVI:v1p239/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p239/r8.claim: A report says Paradise longs for four groups: Ramadan fasters, Qurʾan reciters, those who guard their tongues, and those who feed neighbors; no grading is given.
BURSEVI:v1p239/r8.anchor: إن الجنان يشتقن إلى أربعة نفر صائمي رمضان

BURSEVI:v1p239/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p239/r9.claim: A report says God forgives the Muslim at iftar for the sins of the limbs and thoughts his body and heart have engaged in; no grading is given.
BURSEVI:v1p239/r9.anchor: وإن الله يغفر للعبد المسلم عند إفطاره ما مشت إليه رجلاه

BURSEVI:v1p239/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p239/r10.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p239/r10.claim: The Prophet reports seeing at the Lote Tree a vast, radiant angel assigned to glorify God on behalf of him and his community for Ramadan; two locked chests before the angel hold the community's deliverance from Hell, and no grading is stated.
BURSEVI:v1p239/r10.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال

DURR-FULL:v1p429/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p429/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p429/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says fasting began as three days each month, with permission for residents or travelers to break the fast and feed a poor person; the Ramadan regime removed that ransom, made the month obligatory, and allowed travelers who break the fast to make up other days as the intended ease.
DURR-FULL:v1p429/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {كتب عليكم الصيام} قال: كان ثلاثة أيام من كل شهر ثم نسخ بالذي أنزل الله من صيام شهر رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p455/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r1.claim: An unnamed response explains tightening one's waist as abstaining from sexual relations during those nights.
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r1.anchor: قيل: وما شد المئزر قال: كان يعتزل النساء فيهن

DURR-FULL:v1p455/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra asked Ka'b whether they found Ramadan in their scripture; Ka'b answered that they found it as redemption.
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r2.anchor: عن اسحق بن أبي اسحق أن أبا هريرة قال لكعب: تجدون رمضان عندكم قال: نجده حطة

DURR-FULL:v1p455/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r3.speaker: عمرو بن مرة الجهني
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r3.claim: The Prophet tells a man who affirms faith, prayer, Ramadan fasting and night worship, and almsgiving that he will join the prophets, truthful, and martyrs if he dies thus, provided he does not disobey his parents.
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن مرة الجهني قال جاء رجل من قضاعة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أرأيت إن شهدت أن لا إله إلا الله وأنك رسول الله وصليت الصلوات الخمس وصمت رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p455/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r4.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r4.claim: Ali says Ramadan fasting is obligatory but its night vigil is not, and says fasting requires avoiding lies, falsehood, and idle talk; begin and end by crescent sighting and complete the count if obscured.
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r4.anchor: عن علي أنه كان يخطب إذا حضر رمضان ثم يقول: هذا الشهر المبارك الذي فرض الله صيامه ولم يفرض قيامه

DURR-FULL:v1p455/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r5.speaker: وائلة بن الأسقع
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r5.claim: Wathila reports revelation dates: Abraham's scrolls on Ramadan's first night, Torah on the sixth, Gospel on the thirteenth, Psalms on the eighteenth, and Quran on the twenty-fourth.
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r5.anchor: عن وائلة بن الأسقع أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أنزلت صحف إبراهيم في أول ليلة من رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p455/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r6.claim: Jabir gives another chronology: scrolls on the first night, Torah on day six, Psalms on day twelve, Gospel on day eighteen, and Quran on day twenty-four.
DURR-FULL:v1p455/r6.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: أنزل الله صحف إبراهيم أول ليلة من رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p456/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r1.speaker: أبو الجلد
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r1.claim: Abu al-Jald says Abraham's scrolls were sent down on Ramadan's first night, the Gospel on the eighteenth, and Quran on the twenty-fourth.
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r1.anchor: عن أبي الجلد قال: أنزل الله صحف إبراهيم عليه السلام في أول ليلة من رمضان وأنزل الإنجيل لثماني عشرة

DURR-FULL:v1p456/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r2.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the seven long chapters replaced the Torah, clear chapters the Gospel, oft-repeated verses the Psalms, and detailed chapters were a special distinction.
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r2.anchor: وذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أعطيت السبع الطوال مكان التوراة وأعطيت المبين مكان الانجيل

DURR-FULL:v1p456/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r3.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r3.claim: Aisha gives a different chronology: early scriptures on Ramadan's first day, Torah on the sixth, Gospel on the twelfth, Psalms on the eighteenth, and Quran on the twenty-fourth.
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r3.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أنزلت الصحف الأولى في أول يوم من رمضان وأنزلت التوراة في ست من رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p456/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r4.claim: Answering Atiyya's concern that Quran was revealed in several months, Ibn Abbas says the whole Quran descended on the Night of Decree in Ramadan and was then sent down gradually over the months and days.
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r4.anchor: سأل عطية بن الأسود ابن عباس فقال: إنه قد وقع في قلبي الشك في قوله الله {شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن}

DURR-FULL:v1p456/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Quran descended together on the twenty-fourth of Ramadan to the lowest heaven's Bayt al-Izza, then Gabriel brought it to the Prophet in measured recitation; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزل القرآن جملة

DURR-FULL:v1p456/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Ramadan's blessed night as the Night of Decree: Quran descended all at once from the Remembrance to the lowest heaven, then came to Muhammad in installments about commands, prohibitions, and battles.
DURR-FULL:v1p456/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: شهر رمضان والليلة المباركة وليلة القدر فإن ليلة القدر هي الليلة المباركة

DURR-FULL:v1p457/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the whole Quran descended on the Night of Decree in Ramadan to the lowest heaven, from which God sent it down to earth as events required.
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أنزل القرآن كله جملة واحدة في ليلة القدر في رمضان إلى السماء الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v1p457/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Quran descended all at once to Gabriel on the Night of Decree, who thereafter delivered only what he was commanded.
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزل القرآن جملة واحدة على جبريل في ليلة القدر فكان لا ينزل منه إلا ما أمر به

DURR-FULL:v1p457/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Quran descended in full to Bayt al-Izza in Ramadan, then came to the Prophet over twenty years in response to people's speech.
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: نزل القرآن جملة واحدة في رمضان في ليلة القدر فجعل في بيت العزة ثم أنزل على النبي

DURR-FULL:v1p457/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r4.speaker: الحسن بن علي
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r4.claim: In a sermon after Ali was killed, al-Hasan ibn Ali says he was killed on a night when Quran descended, Jesus was raised, Joshua was killed, and the Children of Israel repented.
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r4.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي أنه لما قتل علي قام خطيبا فقال: والله لقد قتلتم الليلة رجلا في ليلة نزل فيها القرآن

DURR-FULL:v1p457/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that each year's Quranic revelation was sent on the Night of Decree from the seventh heaven to Gabriel in the lowest heaven, who conveyed only what God ordered until revelation ceased.
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: بلغني أنه كان ينزل فيه من القرآن حتى انقطع الوحي وحتى مات محمد

DURR-FULL:v1p457/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r6.speaker: عامر الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r6.claim: Al-Sha'bi says Quran was also revealed during the rest of the year; Gabriel reviewed that year's revelation with Muhammad in Ramadan, when God confirmed, abrogated, or caused verses to be forgotten.
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r6.anchor: عن داود بن أبي هند قال: قلت لعامر الشعبي: شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن

DURR-FULL:v1p457/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r7.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the phrase as the month in which the Quran's fasting obligation was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك {شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن} يقول: الذي أنزل صومه في القرآن

DURR-FULL:v1p457/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says people find guidance through the Quran, which contains the lawful and unlawful and prescribed penalties.
DURR-FULL:v1p457/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {هدى للناس} قال: يهتدون به {وبينات من الهدى} قال: فيه الحلال والحرام والحدود

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r1.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the proofs of guidance and criterion as proofs distinguishing the lawful from the unlawful.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r1.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {وبينات من الهدى والفرقان}

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says people fasted Ashura before Ramadan was revealed, then left the Ashura fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: كان يوم عاشوراء يصام قبل أن ينزل شهر رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r3.speaker: جابر بن سمرة
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r3.claim: Jabir b. Samura says the Prophet urged and checked on their Ashura fast; after Ramadan became obligatory he neither ordered nor forbade it nor checked on them.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r3.anchor: عن جابر بن سمرة قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يأمر بصيام يوم عاشوراء

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains witnessing the month as the month appearing to a person in his home town.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه} قال: هو هلاكه بالدار

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r5.claim: Mujahid says a traveler who is resident in a town must fast when the month comes.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد {فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه} قال: من كان مسافرا

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r6.claim: Said b. Jubayr glosses the command as applying when one is resident.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه} قال: إذا كان مقيما

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r7.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r7.claim: Ali holds that whoever meets Ramadan while resident and then travels is bound to keep fasting, citing this command.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r7.anchor: عن علي قال: من أدركه رمضان وهو مقيم ثم سافر فقد لزمه الصوم

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r8.claim: Ibn Umar says a person who meets Ramadan at home and then intends to travel must fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر في قوله {فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه} قال: من أدركه رمضان في أهله

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r9.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r9.claim: A weak Prophetic report says someone who breaks a Ramadan fast while resident owes a camel sacrifice, or thirty measures of dates for the poor if unable.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r9.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من أفطر يوما من شهر رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r10.speaker: الحسن وإبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r10.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi say a sick person unable to pray standing may break the fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r10.anchor: عن الحسن وإبراهيم النخعي قالا: إذا لم يستطع المريض أن يصلي قائما أفطر

DURR-FULL:v1p458/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r11.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r11.claim: Ata compares fasting while traveling to prayer: the traveler may break the fast and fast when prayer is completed in full.
DURR-FULL:v1p458/r11.anchor: عن عطاء قال: الصيام في السفر مثل الصلاة تقصر

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r1.claim: When Khaythama asks why the verse permits making up travel fasts, Anas says travel was then hungry and unsated, unlike their well-fed travel later.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r1.anchor: عن خيثمة قال: سألت أنس بن مالك عن الصوم في السفر فقال: يصوم

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r2.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r2.claim: Anas says breaking the fast while traveling is a concession, while fasting is better.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r2.anchor: عن أنس قال: من أفطر فهي رخصة ومن صام فهو أفضل

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r3.speaker: إبراهيم وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r3.claim: Ibrahim, Said b. Jubayr, and Mujahid say the traveler may either fast or break the fast, and fasting is better.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد أنهم قالوا في الصوم في السفر: إن شئت

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r4.claim: Mujahid reports that the Prophet both fasted and broke his fast on journeys, told companions to eat, and said God sustained him; Mujahid says Ramadan fasting is better than fasting outside Ramadan.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصوم ويفطر في السفر

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r5.speaker: عبيدة
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r5.claim: Ubayda says one who travels after beginning a Ramadan fast must continue fasting.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r5.anchor: من طريق أبي البختري قال: قال عبيدة: إذا سافر الرجل وقد صام في رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the traveler may choose either to fast or to break the fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r6.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: من شاء صام ومن شاء أفطر

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r7.speaker: عبيدة
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r7.claim: Asked whether he may travel in Ramadan, Ubayda tells Ibn Sirin not to.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين سألت عبيدة قلت: أسافر في رمضان قال: لا

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r8.claim: Ibrahim advises not to set out once Ramadan begins; one who has fasted some days and then travels should keep fasting, since making them up during Ramadan is preferable.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r8.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: إذا أدرك الرجل رمضان فلا يخرج فإن خرج وقد صام شيئا منه

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r9.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r9.claim: Abu Majliz says not to travel once Ramadan begins, but if a man insists on traveling he should fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r9.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال: إذا دخل شهر رمضان فلا يسافرن الرجل

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r10.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r10.claim: Aisha tells Ibrahim b. Muhammad not to travel after Ramadan has begun, and says he should recall his companions and stay until breaking the fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r10.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم أن إبراهيم بن محمد جاء إلى عائشة يسلم عليها وهو في رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p461/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r11.speaker: أم درة
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r11.claim: Umm Durra reports that in Ramadan she asks Aisha about a messenger seeking to take them away; Aisha's response continues in the next segment.
DURR-FULL:v1p461/r11.anchor: عن أم درة قالت: كنت عند عائشة فجاء رسول الي وذلك في رمضان فقالت لي عائشة: ما هذا

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says a man may travel in Ramadan and break the fast if he wishes.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قال: لا بأس أن يسافر الرجل في رمضان ويفطر

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says God did not make Ramadan a restraint on travel.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال: لم يجعل الله رمضان قيدا

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r3.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r3.claim: Ata says a person may travel after Ramadan begins and then break the fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r3.anchor: عن عطاء قال: من أدركه شهر رمضان فلا بأس أن يسافر ثم يفطر

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r4.speaker: سنان بن سلمة
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r4.claim: A Prophetic report from his father says a traveler with enough provisions to reach food should fast Ramadan wherever it finds him.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r4.anchor: عن سنان بن سلمة بن محبق الهذلي عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r5.claim: Aisha reports that God granted the sick and traveling members of the Prophet's community the charity of breaking the Ramadan fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r5.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تصدق بفطر رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r6.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says God waived half of prayer for the traveler and waived fasting for the traveler, sick person, and pregnant woman.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r6.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك عن رجل من كعب قال أغارت علينا خيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r7.claim: Umm Durra reports that Aisha told her not to leave before Ramadan ended, adding that she herself would stay if Ramadan caught her on the road.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r7.anchor: قالت: لا تخرجي حتى ينقضي الشهر فإن رمضان لو أدركني وأنا في الطريق لأقمت

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r8.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r8.claim: Ikrima says missed Ramadan days may be made up consecutively or separately.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة {فعدة من أيام أخر} قال: إن شاء وصل وإن شاء فرق

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says make-up fasts may be consecutive or separated, since the verse requires only a count of other days.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قضاء رمضان قال: إن شاء تابع وإن شاء فرق

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says one may make up the fast however one wishes.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قضاء رمضان صم كيف شئت

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r11.claim: Ibn Umar says one should make up fasts in the same pattern in which they were missed.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: صمه كما أفطرته

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r12.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r12.claim: Ibn Umar says a person who missed Ramadan through illness or travel should make it up consecutively.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r12.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: يصوم شهر رمضان متتابعا من أفطره من مرض أو سفر

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r13.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r13.claim: Anas says the make-up requirement is satisfied once the count is completed, so the days may be separated.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r13.anchor: عن أنس أنه سئل عن قضاء رمضان فقال: إنما قال الله {فعدة من أيام أخر}

DURR-FULL:v1p462/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن الجراح
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r14.claim: Abu Ubayda says God did not permit breaking the fast only to make its later repayment burdensome; complete the count in any pattern.
DURR-FULL:v1p462/r14.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة بن الجراح أنه سئل عن قضاء رمضان متفرقا فقال: إن الله لم يرخص لكم في فطره

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r1.speaker: رافع بن خديج
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r1.claim: Rafi b. Khadij says to complete the count and fast the make-up days however one wishes.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r1.anchor: عن رافع بن خديج قال: احصر العدة وصم كيف شئت

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r2.claim: Muadh b. Jabal says to complete the count and fast the make-up days however one wishes.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r2.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل أنه سئل عن قضاء رمضان فقال: احصر العدة وصم كيف شئت

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r3.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r3.claim: Amr b. al-As permits separating make-up fasts because the verse says to fast a number of other days.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن العاص قال: فرق قضاء رمضان إنما قال الله {فعدة من أيام أخر}

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra tells a woman she may arrange make-up fasts as she wishes, provided she counts them, citing God's desire for ease.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن امرأة سألته: كيف تقضي رمضان فقال: صومي كيف شئت

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r5.claim: Aisha says the verse was first revealed with the word 'consecutive' and that word later fell away; al-Bayhaqi explains it was abrogated.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r5.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: نزلت / فعدة من أيام أخر متتابعات / فسقطت متتابعات

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r6.speaker: البيهقي
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqi explains Aisha's report about the dropped word 'consecutive' as an abrogation.

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r7.claim: A weak Prophetic report says anyone owing a Ramadan fast should make the days up consecutively rather than separately.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان عليه صوم من رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r8.claim: A weak report says the Prophet prescribed consecutive make-up fasts but also said separating them suffices.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r8.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قضاء رمضان فقال: يقضيه تباعا

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r9.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet allowed Ramadan make-up fasts either consecutively or separately.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r9.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: في قضاء رمضان إن شاء فرق

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to give the same Prophetic permission to make up fasts consecutively or separately.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r10.anchor: وأخرج الدارقطني من حديث ابن عباس مثله

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r11.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r11.claim: A mursal report al-Daraqutni calls hasan compares make-up fasting to paying a debt in installments; its alternate connected report from Jabir he weakens.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r11.anchor: عن محمد بن المنكدر قال بلغني عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن تقطيع قضاء صيام

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies ease as breaking the fast while traveling and hardship as fasting while traveling.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر} قال: الإفطار في السفر

DURR-FULL:v1p463/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r13.speaker: محجن بن الأدرع
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r13.claim: Mihjan reports that the Prophet watched a man praying and asked whether his prayer was sincere; Mihjan replied that he was among Medina's most prayerful people.
DURR-FULL:v1p463/r13.anchor: عن محجن بن الأدرع أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلا يصلي فتراءاه ببصره

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r1.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet let her watch the Ethiopians dance until she tired, saying the Jews should know their religion has latitude and that he was sent with tolerant monotheism.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت وضع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذقني على منكبه لأنظر زفن الحبشة

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says God's religion is set below excess and above shortcoming.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال: إن دين الله وضع دون الغلو وفوق التقصير

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says there is no blame on a traveler for either fasting or breaking the fast; choose whichever is easier.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لا تعب على من صام في السفر ولا على من أفطر

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r4.claim: Mujahid says to choose whichever of fasting and breaking the fast is easier, since God intends only ease.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: خذ بأيسرهما عليك فإن الله لم يرد إلا اليسر

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r5.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r5.claim: Al-Rabi says completing the number means completing the Ramadan count.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r5.anchor: عن الربيع في قوله {ولتكملوا العدة} قال: عدة رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r6.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r6.claim: Hudhayfa reports that one should begin and end fasting only after sighting the crescent or completing thirty days.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r6.anchor: عن حذيفة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تقدموا الشهر حتى تروا الهلال

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports not fasting one or two days before the month unless it is one's habitual fast, and completing thirty days if clouds obscure the crescent.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تقدموا الشهر بصيام يوم ولا يومين

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophetic instruction to fast and break on sighting the crescent, and complete the month's count when cloudy.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: صوموا لرؤيته وافطروا لرؤيته

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r9.speaker: رافع بن خديج
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r9.claim: Rafi b. Khadij reports counting Shaʿban, avoiding a pre-month fast, and completing thirty days if cloudy; the Prophet showed a twenty-nine-day month by folding a finger.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r9.anchor: عن رافع بن خديج قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم احصوا عدة شعبان لرمضان ولا تقدموا الشهر بصوم

DURR-FULL:v1p466/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r10.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r10.claim: Abd al-Rahman b. Zayd says the Companions reported completing thirty days if cloudy; two upright witnesses allow fasting, breaking, and sacrifice.
DURR-FULL:v1p466/r10.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن الخطاب قال: إنا اصطحبنا أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r1.speaker: أبو مسعود الأنصاري
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r1.claim: Abu Masud reports that after the Prophet fasted a thirtieth day of Ramadan, two Bedouins testified to seeing the crescent the previous evening, so he ordered people to break the fast.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r1.anchor: عن أبي مسعود الأنصاري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أصبح صائما لتمام الثلاثين من رمضان

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the completed count is the number of days the sick person or traveler missed.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {ولتكملوا العدة} قال: عدة ما أفطر المريض والمسافر

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r3.claim: Zayd b. Aslam interprets magnifying God as saying takbir on Eid al-Fitr.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله {ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم} قال: لتكبروا يوم الفطر

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muslims should say takbir from seeing the Shawwal crescent until the Eid celebration ends.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: حق على المسلمين إذا نظروا إلى هلال شوال أن يكبروا الله

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r5.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction to adorn the Eids with takbir.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r5.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زينوا أعيادكم بالتكبير

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r6.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami says people were more emphatic about takbir on Eid al-Fitr than Eid al-Adha.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r6.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال: كانوا في الفطر أشد منهم في الأضحى

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r7.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r7.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that the Prophet went out on Eid al-Fitr saying takbir until reaching the prayer ground, then stopped after prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r7.anchor: عن الزهري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخرج يوم الفطر فيكبر حتى يأتي المصلى

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r8.claim: A second chain from al-Zuhri through Salim to Ibn Umar transmits the report, but al-Bayhaqi grades this route weak.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r8.anchor: وأخرجه البيهقي من وجه آخر موصولا عن الزهري عن سالم عن ابن عمر وضعفه

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r9.speaker: عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r9.claim: Nafi reports that the Prophet went out to the two Eids raising his voice with tahlil and takbir.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r9.anchor: من طريق نافع عن عبد الله أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخرج إلى العيدين

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r10.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r10.claim: Ata says it is Sunnah to say takbir on Eid.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r10.anchor: عن عطاء قال: إن من السنة أن تكبر يوم العيد

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r11.claim: Ibn Masud's takbir formula magnifies God, affirms His oneness, and ends with praise to God.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه كان يكبر الله أكبر الله أكبر لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas's takbir formula magnifies God and praises Him for guiding the believers.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يكبر الله أكبر كبيرا الله أكبر كبيرا

DURR-FULL:v1p467/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r13.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r13.claim: Abu Uthman says Uthman taught a takbir formula magnifying God and denying that He has a consort, child, partner, or humiliated ally.
DURR-FULL:v1p467/r13.anchor: عن أبي عثمان النهدي قال: كان عثمان يعلمنا التكبير الله أكبر الله أكبر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي، سعيد بن أبي هريرة، مجاهد، محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r1.claim: These authorities say not to say Ramadan by itself because Ramadan is one of God's names; say the month of Ramadan.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي وسعيد بن أبي هريرة قالا : لا تقولوا رمضان فان رمضان اسم من اسماء الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، زيد بن ثابت
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Thabit permitted saying Ramadan without the word month.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r2.anchor: ورخص فيه ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت

IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r3.claim: The Prophet's report dates the revealed scriptures to Ramadan: Abraham's scrolls on its first night, Torah on the sixth, Gospel on the thirteenth, Zabur on the eighteenth, and Quran on the twenty-fourth.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r3.anchor: عن واثلة ان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : نزل صحف ابراهيم في اول ليلة من رمضان وانزل التوراة لست مضين من رمضان

IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas answered Atiyya's doubt by saying the Quran descended all at once in Ramadan, on the Night of Power and a blessed night, then was sent down in stages at the stars' settings.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس : انما نزل في رمضان وفي ليلة القدر وفي ليلة مباركة جملة واحدة ثم انزل على مواقع النجوم من الشهور والايام .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr's parallel account adds that the Quran's all-at-once descent was to a heavenly house called Bayt al-Izza.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r5.anchor: وروى عن سعيد بن جبير نحوه وذكر فيه إلى بيت في السماء يقال له : بيت العزة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the Quran as the revelation that prescribed Ramadan's fast.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك شهر رمضان الذي انزل فيه القران يقول : الذي انزل صومه القران .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says people are guided by the Quran.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج هدى للناس قال : يهتدون به .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r8.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r8.claim: A report Ibn Abi Najih says had reached him describes Quranic revelation continuing through Muhammad's life; each year's portion descended on Laylat al-Qadr from the seventh heaven to the lowest heaven and then to the Prophet as God commanded.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p310/r8.anchor: عن ابن نجيح شهر رمضان الذي انزل فيه القران قال بلغني انه كان ينزل فيه القران حتى انقطع الوحي وحتى مات محمد

IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r1.claim: Al-Suddi explains the clear signs of guidance as clear explanations of the lawful and the unlawful.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r1.anchor: عن السدى هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان اما وبينات من الهدى فبينات من الحلال والحرام .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r2.claim: Abu Salih identifies al-Furqan here as the Torah.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r2.anchor: عن أبي صالح الفرقان قال : التوراة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r3.speaker: علي، عائشة، ابن عمر، ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، عبيدة بن الحنفية، خيثمة، سويد بن غفلة، علي بن الحسين، إبراهيم النخعي، مجاهد، الشعبي، أبو مجلز، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r3.claim: Ali and the listed authorities hold that someone who encounters Ramadan while resident must continue fasting even if he travels afterward.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r3.anchor: عن عبيدة السلماني عن علي قال : من ادركه رمضان وهو مقيم ثم سافر بعد لزمه الصوم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet left Medina fasting in Ramadan, broke his fast at Qudayd, and remained a nonfasting traveler until he entered Mecca.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس , قال : خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من المدينة وهو صائم في شهر رمضان , فلما اتى قديدا , افطر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r5.speaker: سلمة بن الأكوع
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r5.claim: Salama says that before this verse descended, people in the Prophet's time could either fast Ramadan or break the fast and feed a poor person.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r5.anchor: عن سلمة ابن الاكوع انه قال : كنا في رمضان في عهد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم من شاء صام ومن شاء افطر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r6.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r6.claim: The commentary says the explanation of the illness and travel concession and making up missed days was already given at 2:184.

IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r7.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r7.claim: Al-Sha'bi advises choosing the easier of two matters when uncertain, as nearer the truth, because God wills ease for this community.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p311/r7.anchor: عن الشعبي قال : اذا اختلف عليك امران فانظر ايسرهما فانه اقرب إلى الحق ان الله اراد بهذه الامة اليسر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك، عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains God's willing ease as allowing a traveler to break the fast; al-Dahhak and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر قال : اليسر : الافطار في السفر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r2.claim: Asked how a woman should make up Ramadan, Abu Hurayra reportedly answered that she should separate the make-up days and cited God's willing ease.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r2.anchor: قالت : ارسلت إلى أبي هريرة كيف تقضي المرأة رمضان فقال : فرقي ثم قال : يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak includes pregnant and nursing women, as well as travelers, among those permitted to break the fast.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله يريد الله بكم اليسر قال : تفطر الحامل والمرضع والافطار في السفر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r4.speaker: جابر بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r4.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd says that in battle one may pray riding or walking, facing whichever direction one can, as an instance of divine ease.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r4.anchor: سئل جابر بن زيد عن الصلاة عند القتال فقال : يصلي الرجل راكبا وماشيا حيث كان وجهه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، عمر بن عبد العزيز، الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains hardship as fasting while traveling; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and al-Dahhak are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ولا يريد بكم العسر قال : العسر الصيام في السفر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة، مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r6.claim: A woman asking about Ramadan make-up for menstrual days was told by Abu Hurayra to count the days and fast them whenever she wished; Mujahid is reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r6.anchor: انه يصيبني ما يصيب النساء من العلة في رمضان فما ترى في قضائه ؟ فقال أبو هريرة : احصى العدة وصومي كيف شئت

IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r7.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas explains completing the count as completing the number of Ramadan days.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p313/r7.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس قوله ولتكملوا العدة عدة رمضان .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p314/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the commanded takbir as the takbir on Eid al-Fitr.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم في قوله ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم قال : التكبير يوم الفطر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r1.claim: على originally signals elevation, then figuratively indicates being in a state; Arabic usage makes على سفر explicit for actually traveling, not merely intending to travel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r1.anchor: وأصل ( على ) الدلالة على الاستعلاء ثم استعملت مجازا في التمكن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r2.claim: The wording means a traveler breaks the fast only after beginning the journey, rather than on mere intention; whether one who travels after dawn may break that day is disputed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r2.anchor: على أن المسافر لا يفطر حتى يأخذ في السير في السفر دون مجرد النية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r3.claim: Anas intended to travel in Ramadan, had his mount readied and wore travel clothes near sunset, ate, then mounted and called this the Sunna; al-Daraqutni transmits the report, and al-Hasan al-Basri shares this view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r3.anchor: فعن أنس بن مالك أنه أراد السفر في رمضان فرحلت دابته ولبس ثياب السفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r4.speaker: الزهري ومالك والشافعي والأوزاعي وأبو حنيفة وأبو ثور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r4.claim: These authorities say that someone who began the day resident cannot break the fast after traveling later that day; if he does, he owes make-up days but no expiation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r4.anchor: وقال جماعة : إذا أصبح مقيما ثم سافر بعد ذلك فلا يفطر يومه ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r5.speaker: ابن كنانة والمخزومي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r5.claim: Some Malikis, including Ibn Kinanah and al-Makhzumi, require expiation if a person breaks the fast after traveling later in a day begun at home; Ibn al-Arabi chose this view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r5.anchor: وبالغ بعض المالكية فقال : عليه الكفارة وهو قول ابن كنانة والمخزومي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r6.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r6.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr rejects that expiation view: God explicitly allowed the traveler to break the fast; Ibn Ashur says Ibn Abd al-Barr was right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عمر بن عبد البر : ليس هذا بشيء لأن الله أباح له الفطر بنص الكتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r7.speaker: أحمد وإسحاق والشعبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r7.claim: Ahmad, Ishaq, and al-Sha'bi allow a person who travels after dawn to break that day's fast; they also transmit this from Ibn Umar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r7.anchor: وقال أحمد وإسحاق والشعبي : يفطر إذا سافر بعد الصبح ورووه عن ابن عمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports in Bukhari and Muslim that the Prophet traveled from Medina to Mecca fasting, then at Usfan called for water, displayed it, broke the fast, and remained unfasted until Mecca.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r8.anchor: حديث ابن عباس في ( صحيحي البخاري ومسلم ) ( خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من المدينة إلى مكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r9.claim: Ibn Ashur favors allowing a traveler to break the fast after departing after dawn, supported by Ibn Abbas's report; al-Qurtubi calls that report explicit and says the contrary view falls away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r9.anchor: قال القرطبي : وهذا نص في الباب فسقط ما يخالفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r10.claim: The wording عدّة, rather than صيام, explicitly requires a number of make-up fasting days equal to the days missed through illness or travel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r10.anchor: تنصيصا على وجوب صوم أيام بعدد أيام الفطر في المرض والسفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r11.claim: من is partitive if الأيام means days of the year or era; alternatively it classifies the count, as in five thousand angels in 3:125.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p163/r11.anchor: فمن للتبعيض إن اعتبر أيام أعم من أيام العدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r1.claim: أخر is the plural of أخرى, matching the plural days because Arabic treats every plural as feminine; the author connects it with أياما معدودات earlier in the passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r1.anchor: ووصف الأيام بأخر وهو جمع الأخرى اعتبارا بتأنيث الجمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says the plural أخر was selected instead of أخرى to prevent readers taking it as an adjective of عدّة.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r2.anchor: قال أبو حيان : واختير في الوصف صيغة الجمع دون أن يقال أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur says Abu Hayyan's concern about confusion is unconvincing; عدّة الأيام already means days, so plural agreement and lighter wording better explain the form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r3.anchor: فالظاهر أن العدول عن أخرى لمراعاة صيغة الجمع في الموصوف مع طلب خفة اللفظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r4.speaker: جمهور النحويين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r4.claim: Most grammarians explain أخر as diptote because it is an adjective and is deflected from the masculine singular form expected of an unqualified أفعل; Ibn Ashur questions aspects of their account.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r4.anchor: وعلل جمهور النحويين منعه من الصرف على أصولهم بأن فيه الوصفية والعدل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r5.claim: The verse leaves three make-up rules unspecified: whether days must be consecutive, whether make-up must begin promptly, and whether deliberate interruption incurs expiation; unrestricted wording competes with analogy to the original worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r5.anchor: فأطلقت ( عدة من أيام أخر ) ، فلم تبين أتكون متتابعة أم يجوز تفريقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r6.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r6.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits with a sound chain Aisha's report that متتابعات was revealed after the make-up-days phrase and later dropped; she means it was abrogated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r6.anchor: فروى الدارقطني بسند صحيح قالت عائشة نزلت { فعدة من أيام أخر متتابعات } متتابعات فسقطت متتابعات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r7.speaker: الأئمة الأربعة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r7.claim: The four imams and Companions Abu Hurayra, Abu Ubayda, Muadh ibn Jabal, and Ibn Abbas hold that make-up days need not be consecutive; the unrestricted wording is a divine concession, unlike expiation fasts specified as consecutive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r7.anchor: وهو قول الأئمة الأربعة وبه قال من الصحابة أبو هريرة ، وأبو عبيدة ، ومعاذ بن جبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r8.claim: Ibn Umar says make-up days for Ramadan missed through illness or travel should be consecutive; al-Baji says he may intend obligation or recommendation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p164/r8.anchor: وفي ( الموطأ ) عن ابن عمر أنه يقول : يصوم قضاء رمضان متتابعا من أفطره من مرض أو سفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r1.claim: Neither Qur'an nor Sunna requires prompt make-up; the command does not entail immediacy, and practice allows make-up until Sha'ban before the next Ramadan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r1.anchor: وأما المبادرة بالقضاء ، فليس في الكتاب ولا في السنة ما يقتضيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r2.claim: Aisha says she could not make up her missed Ramadan fasts until Sha'ban; Ibn Ashur treats this as clear evidence against an immediate duty and notes the majority agree.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r2.anchor: وفي ( الصحيح ) عن عائشة قالت : يكون علي الصوم من رمضان فما أستطيع أن أقضيه إلا في شعبان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r3.speaker: داود الظاهري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r3.claim: Dawud al-Zahiri dissents from the majority and says make-up should begin on the day after the Eid of Ramadan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r3.anchor: وشذ داود الظاهري فقال : يشرع في قضاء رمضان ثاني يوم من شوال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r4.claim: The majority say deliberately breaking a make-up fast incurs no expiation, since expiation protects Ramadan's sanctity and make-up days do not share that sanctity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r4.anchor: وأما من أفطر متعمدا في يوم من أيام قضاء رمضان فالجمهور على أنه لا كفارة عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r5.claim: Qatada requires expiation for deliberately breaking a make-up fast, reasoning that the replacement worship has the same rule as its original.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p165/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة : تجب عليه الكفارة بناء على أن قضاء العبادة يساوي أصله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r2.claim: These verses continue the preceding fasting verses, and there is no abrogation among them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r2.anchor: قد علمت أن هذه الآيات تكملة للآيات السابقة وأن لا نسخ في خلال هاته الآيات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r3.claim: The phrase predicates Ramadan of an omitted subject, meaning the specified counted days are Ramadan; it resumes the discussion to answer the question raised by “counted days.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r3.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره هي أي الأيام المعدودات شهر رمضان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r4.claim: Mujahid reads شهرا in the accusative as a detailed apposition to أيامًا, supporting the omitted-subject analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r4.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك قراءة مجاهد { شهرا } بالنصب على البدلية من { أياما } : بدل تفصيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r5.claim: If this verse abrogated the preceding rule, Ramadan could instead be the subject, with the following clause as its predicate; the conditional-like relative licenses its فاء, or the فاء is extra as in Sibawayh’s poetic example. Both analyses are weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r5.anchor: أنشده سيبويه ، وكلا هذين الوجهين ضعيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r6.claim: A month is one of twelve divisions of the year, running from one new crescent to the next; it is named from شهرة because the visible crescent is publicized. The verse on twelve months is linked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p168/r6.anchor: والشهر جزء من اثني عشر جزءا من تقسيم السنة قال تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r1.claim: Ramadan is the recurring lunar month assigned for the obligatory fast; because the time recurs each year, the obligation recurs annually and is not limited to one particular Ramadan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r1.anchor: فكلما حل الوقت المعين من السنة المسمى بشهر رمضان فقد وجب على المسلمين أداء فريضة الصوم فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r2.claim: The relative clause may recall a great virtue the audience already knows, since the Quran’s descent is a major religious event unlikely to be obscure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r2.anchor: أن المخاطبين يعلمون أن نزول القرآن وقع في شهر رمضان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r3.claim: Alternatively, the clause can inform the audience of Ramadan’s virtue and identify it through this unique attribute; familiarity with a relative clause’s content is usual, not required.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r3.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون إعلاما بهذا الفضل وأجري الكلام على طريقة الوصف بالموصول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r4.claim: The sentence is not simply reporting that Ramadan is the month of Quranic revelation: شهر رمضان is a predicate, not the subject, in this construction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r4.anchor: وليس المقصود الإخبار عن شهر رمضان بأنه أنزل فيه القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r5.claim: The Quran’s descent means its beginning was revealed to the Prophet in year forty-one of the Elephant era; the first portion stands for the whole whose completion was destined to follow, as in 6:92.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r5.anchor: فإن فيه ابتداء النزول من عام واحد وأربعين من الفيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r6.claim: “In it” means in a corresponding Ramadan of another year: the actual month of first revelation had passed years before fasting became obligatory in the second year after the Hijra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p171/r6.anchor: ومعنى { الذي أنزل فيه } أنزل في مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r1.claim: The two descriptions are circumstantial clauses referring to the Quran; they show why the month is favored because guidance and distinction were revealed in it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r1.anchor: حالان من ( القرآن ) إشارة بهما إلى وجه تفضيل الشهر بسبب ما نزل فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r2.claim: The first guidance is the Quran’s direction toward public and private interests that do not conflict with the common good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r2.anchor: ما في القرآن من الإرشاد إلى المصالح العامة والخاصة التي لا تنافي العامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r3.claim: The clear proofs establish less visible guidance that many reject, including arguments for divine oneness, the Messenger’s truth, and other Quranic proofs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r3.anchor: ما في القرآن من الاستدلال على الهدى الخفي الذي ينكره كثير من الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r4.claim: Furqan means the Quran’s public distinction between truth from God and the falsehood people followed before Islam; the two kinds of guidance are therefore not repetitive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r4.anchor: والفرقان مصدر فرق وقد شاع في الفرق بين الحق والباطل أي إعلان التفرقة بين الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r5.claim: The verse returns to explaining the fasting command after an interlude that reassured listeners, praised fasting’s benefit for piety, and noted the easing of hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r5.anchor: فهو رجوع إلى التبيين بعد الفصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r6.claim: “Among you” refers back to the believers addressed in the fasting command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r6.anchor: عائد إلى { الذين أمنوا } ( البقرة : 183 ) مثل الضمائر التي قبله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r7.claim: If شهد means attended, الشهر is an adverbial object: whoever is present during the month, rather than traveling, must fast it; anyone present for only part fasts those days.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r7.anchor: { شهد } يجوز أن يكون بمعنى حضر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r8.claim: شهد may instead mean knew the month had arrived, with an understood word for its arrival; it does not mean saw, nor does الشهر here mean the crescent as al-Zajjaj reports from usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p173/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { شهد } بمعنى علم كقوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r1.speaker: قالوا
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r1.claim: On the view that 2:185 abrogates the earlier choice of fasting or feeding, the repeated exemption preserves make-up fasting for the sick and traveler while abrogating feeding for healthy residents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r1.anchor: أنه لما كان صوم رمضان واجبا على التخيير بينه وبين الفدية بالإطعام بالآية الأولى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r2.claim: If both passages were revealed together, the exemption is repeated where it best fits, after the fasting days are specified; the earlier mention gave listeners advance reassurance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r2.anchor: كان الوجه في إعادة هذا الحكم هو هذا الموضع الجدير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r3.claim: The repetition can also prevent readers from thinking the first exemption was abrogated by شهد, if understood as knowing the month; it reinforces and clarifies the concession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p174#2/r3.anchor: شهد بمعنى تحقق وعلم ، مع زيادة في تأكيد حكم الرخصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r1.claim: This explanatory resumption gives the reason for the exemption: God legislates making up missed fasts to provide ease when hardship occurs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r1.anchor: بين به حكمة الرخصة أي شرع لكم القضاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r2.claim: A single restriction to ease could have expressed the meaning, but affirmation comes first as the reason for the concession, then negation emphasizes it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r2.anchor: لكنه عدل عن جملة القصر إلى جملتي إثبات ونفي لأن المقصود ابتداء هو جملة الإثبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r3.claim: The phrase may explain all the preceding legislation: fasting may look difficult, yet its benefits make it an easy form of self-discipline, unlike other religions’ self-imposed strain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r3.anchor: إيماء إلى أن مشروعية الصيام وإن كانت تلوح في صورة المشقة والعسر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r4.claim: The majority read اليسر and العسر with a still س; Abu Jaafar reads both with a damma by vowel harmony.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r4.anchor: بسكون السين فيهما ، وقرأه أبو جعفر بضم السين ضمة إتباع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r5.claim: The lām in ولتكبروا is شبه زائدة: after wanting or commanding, a مصدر clause normally takes no preposition, though the lām is common; its verb is subjunctive after explicit or understood أن. Al-Kashshaf cites 61:8 and 39:12.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r5.anchor: تسمى شبه الزائدة وهي اللام التي يكثر وقوعها بعد فعل الإرادة وفعل الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r6.claim: The conjunction continues the explanation: all four clauses from witnessing the month through making up missed days explain the preceding command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p175/r6.anchor: فإن مجموع هذه الجمل الأربع تعليل لما قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r1.claim: Completing the count means making up days missed by those required to fast, preserving the wisdom of a complete Ramadan; the concession for an excuse supplies mercy and relief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r1.anchor: وإكمال العدة يحصل بقضاء الأيام التي أفطرها من وجب عليه الصوم ليأتي بعدة أيام شهر رمضان كاملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r2.claim: Most read ولتكملوا with a still ك and light م from أكمل; Abu Bakr from Asim and Yaqub read it with a fatḥa and doubled م from كمل.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r2.anchor: مضارع أكمل وقرأه أبو بكر عن عاصم ويعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r3.claim: Takbir verbally attributes greatness to God: say الله أكبر, declaring divine majesty and transcendence from every deficiency; the verb is coined from the phrase, like basmala and hamdala.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r3.anchor: والتكبير تفعيل مراد به النسبة والتوصيف أي أن تنسبوا الله إلى الكبر والنسبة هنا نسبة بالقول اللساني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r4.claim: God is greater than every actual or imagined power; affirming this entails His unique divinity, since whatever else is deficient cannot deserve worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r4.anchor: لأن التفضيل يستلزم نقصان من عداه والناقص غير مستحق للإلهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r5.claim: Takbir was prescribed in prayer to end prostration to other than God and when sacrificing in pilgrimage to end offerings to idols; this verse also grounds takbir at the end of fasting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r5.anchor: عند نحر البدن في الحج لإبطال ما كانوا يتقربون به إلى أصنامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r6.claim: The verse grounds the established practice of Muslims saying takbir while setting out for Eid prayer and the imam saying it in the Eid sermon.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p176/r6.anchor: فمن أجل ذلك مضت السنة بأن يكبر المسلمون عند الخروج إلى صلاة العيد ويكبر الإمام في خطبة العيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r1.claim: Eid takbir counters the idolaters’ attempts to approach their gods through food and blood: Muslims’ takbir signals that God is worshipped through fasting and is above idol worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الله يعبد بالصوم وأنه متنزه عن ضراوة الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r2.claim: Gratitude is a broader rationale than takbir: it includes spoken glorification, charitable acts during fasting and Eid, and wearing fine clothes on Eid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r2.anchor: لأنه يكون بالأقوال التي فيها تعظيم لله تعالى ويكون بفعل القرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r3.claim: The verse commands takbir but leaves its wording, timing, and number unspecified; Prophetic practice clarifies these, with juristic differences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r3.anchor: وهو غير مفصل في لفظ التكبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r4.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r4.claim: The famous Sunnah formula repeats الله أكبر three times, and Malik, Abu Hanifa, and al-Shafii adopt it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r4.anchor: والمشهور في السنة أنه يكرر الله أكبر ثلاثا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r5.speaker: مالك والشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r5.claim: Malik and al-Shafii permit added tahlil and praise after two takbirs; Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas are cited for saying لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ولله الحمد.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r5.anchor: وقال مالك والشافعي : إذا شاء المرء زاد على التكبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r6.speaker: أحمد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r6.claim: Ahmad holds that the formula is flexible.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that fewer or other than three takbirs do not suffice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : لا يجزىء غير ثلاث تكبيرات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r8.claim: Eid takbir begins when worshippers and imam leave home for the prayer place and stops when they arrive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r8.anchor: فتكبير الفطر يبتدىء من وقت خروج المصلي من بيته إلى محل الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r9.claim: The strongest practice is seven extra takbirs in the first Eid rakah and six in the second, supported by reports and Medinan practice from the Prophet onward; many disputes exist, but the matter is broad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r9.anchor: هذا هو الأصح مما ثبت في الأخبار وعمل به أهل المدينة من عهد النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r10.claim: After prayer, the imam says takbir in the Eid sermon; congregants repeat during his takbir and listen to the sermon otherwise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p177/r10.anchor: ثم يكبر الإمام في خطبة صلاة العيد بعد الصلاة ويكبر معه المصلون حين تكبيره وينصتون للخطبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r1.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash reads shahr in the nominative as an explanation of the previously mentioned ‘few days’: those days are the month of Ramadan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش شهر رمضان بالرفع على تفسير الأيام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r2.speaker: مجاهد ومعاوية والحسن وزيد بن علي وعكرمة ويحيى بن يعمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r2.claim: Mujāhid reads shahr in the accusative as an exhortation: ‘Ramadan is prescribed for you, so fast it’; Muʿāwiya, al-Hasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿIkrima, and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar also read it accusatively.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r2.anchor: وأراه نصبه على معنى الإغراء عليكم شهر رمضان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r3.claim: Ibn Fāris connects Ramaḍān with intense heat of sun-heated stones; the month was named when transferred from the old calendar because it coincided with hot weather.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r3.anchor: قال ابن فارس الرمض حر الحجارة من شدة حر الشمس ويقال شهر رمضان من شدة الحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r4.claim: One view says the whole Quran descended in Ramadan on the Night of Power to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r4.anchor: أحدها أنه أنزل القرآن فيه جملة واحدة وذلك في ليلة القدر إلى بيت العزة من السماء الدنيا قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r5.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r5.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain its being sent down in Ramadan as the establishment of the fast as an obligation then.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r5.anchor: والثاني أن معناه أنه انزل القرآن بفرض صيامه روي عن مجاهد والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق وأبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq and Abū Sulaymān al-Dimashqī say the Quran’s revelation to the Prophet began in Ramadan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r6.anchor: والثالث أن معناه إن القرآن ابتدىء بنزوله فيه على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قاله ابن إسحاق وابو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r7.claim: Muqātil glosses al-furqān as a way out of religious doubt and error.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل والفرقان المخرج في الدين من الشبهة والضلالة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r1.claim: Whoever witnesses the month means whoever is resident and not traveling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r1.anchor: أي من كان حاضرا غير مسافر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r2.claim: The sickness and travel exemption is repeated because the earlier verse included an abrogated ruling; repeating it prevents the exemption from being attached to that abrogated material.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r2.anchor: لأن في الآية المتقدمة منسوخا فأعاده لئلا يكون مقرونا بالمنسوخ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r3.claim: They interpret ease as breaking the fast while traveling and hardship as fasting during travel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r3.anchor: اليسر الإفطار في السفر والعسر الصوم فيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r4.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz says to choose whichever is easier for oneself, fasting or breaking the fast on a journey.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r4.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز أي ذلك كان أيسر عليك فافعل الصوم في السفر أو الفطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the kāf lightly; Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads the mīm doubled, like waṣṣā and awṣā.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r5.anchor: باسكان الكاف خفيفة وقرا أبو بكر عن عاصم بتشديد الميم وذلك مثل وصى و أوصى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this means completing the number of days missed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ولتكملوا عدة ما افطرتم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r7.claim: Another explanation says not to exceed what was prescribed, as Christians did, or move it from its proper time.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم المراد به لا تزيدوا على ما افترض كما فعلت النصارى ولا تنقلوه عن زمانه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Muslims should begin glorifying God upon seeing the Shawwāl crescent and continue until the end of their Eid.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس حق على المسلمين إذا نظروا إلى هلال شوال أن يكبروا لله حتى يفرغوا من عيدهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the lām clauses coordinate with an omitted lām: God wills ease, not hardship, and [wills] that people complete the count; the first lām is omitted because its sense is clear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r9.anchor: أن هذه الواو عطفت اللام التي بعدها على لام محذوفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r10.claim: The Sunna is to proclaim takbīr on the nights of Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā and while going to the prayer ground.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r10.anchor: ومن السنة إظهار التكبير ليلة الفطر وليلة النحر وإذا غدوا إلى المصلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r11.speaker: حنبل عن أحمد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r11.claim: In one report from Aḥmad, the takbīr for Eid al-Fiṭr ends after the imam finishes the sermon.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r11.anchor: واختلفت الرواية عن أحمد رضي الله عنه متى يقطع في عيد الفطر فنقل عنه حنبل يقطع بعد فراغ الإمام من الخطبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r12.speaker: الأثرم عن أحمد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r12.claim: Another report from Aḥmad says it ends upon reaching the prayer ground; al-Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā explains this as reaching the ground when the imam comes out.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p187#2/r12.anchor: ونقل الأثرم إذا جاء المصلى قطع قال القاضي أبو يعلى يعني إذا جاء المصلى وخرج الإمام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r1.claim: God praises Ramadan above the other months because He chose it for the descent of the great Qur’an; revelation of earlier divine books also occurred in this month.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r1.anchor: يمدح تعالى شهر الصيام من بين سائر الشهور، بأن اختاره من بينهن لإنزال القرآن العظيم فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r2.claim: A report transmitted by Ahmad says Abraham’s scrolls came down on Ramadan’s first night, the Torah on its sixth, the Gospel on its thirteenth, and the Qur’an on its twenty-fourth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أنزلت صحف إبراهيم في أول ليلة من رمضان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r3.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits from Jabir that the Zabur descended on Ramadan’s twelfth night and the Gospel on its eighteenth, with the remaining dates as in the preceding report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r3.anchor: وقد روي من حديث جابر بن عبد الله وفيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r4.claim: The earlier scriptures each descended all at once to their respective prophets, whereas the Qur’an first descended whole to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then piecemeal to Muhammad according to events.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r4.anchor: وأما القرآن فإنما نزل جملة واحدة إلى بيت العزة من السماء الدنيا، وكان ذلك في شهر رمضان، في ليلة القدر منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r5.claim: Replying to ʿAtiyya al-Aswad’s concern that revelation occurred in other months, Ibn ʿAbbas said the Qur’an descended whole in Ramadan on the blessed Night of Decree, then gradually across months and days.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p501/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: إنه أنزل في رمضان، في ليلة القدر وفي ليلة مباركة جملة واحدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r1.claim: In Saʿid ibn Jubayr’s report, Ibn ʿAbbas says the Qur’an descended to the lowest heaven and Bayt al-ʿIzza midway through Ramadan, then came to the Prophet over twenty years in response to people’s words.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r1.anchor: وفي رواية سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: أنزل القرآن في النصف من شهر رمضان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r2.claim: In ʿIkrima’s report, Ibn ʿAbbas says the Qur’an descended whole to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr; God then supplied the Prophet’s responses whenever the polytheists raised an argument.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r2.anchor: وفي رواية عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: نزل القرآن في شهر رمضان في ليلة القدر إلى هذه السماء الدنيا جملة واحدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r3.claim: These reports connect the gradual replies to the Qur’an’s statement that disbelievers asked why it was not revealed all at once and that God answered their challenges with truth and the best explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r3.anchor: ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r4.speaker: فخر الدين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r4.claim: Fakhr al-Din allows another possibility: on each Night of Decree, the amount people needed was sent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أنه كان ينزل في كل ليلة قدر ما يحتاج الناس إلى إنزاله إلى مثله من اللوح إلى سماء الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r5.speaker: فخر الدين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r5.claim: Fakhr al-Din leaves undecided whether this annual partial descent or the earlier account of a single descent is more likely.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r5.anchor: وتوقف، هل هذا أولى أو الأول؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r6.speaker: القرطبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi attributes the annual-descent possibility to Muqatil ibn Hayyan and reports consensus that the Qur’an descended whole from the Preserved Tablet to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r6.anchor: وحكى الإجماع على أن القرآن نزل جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ إلى بيت العزة في السماء الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r7.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r7.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna and others are reported to interpret the verse as referring to the Qur’an’s virtue or to the obligation of fasting in Ramadan; Ibn Kathir calls this very strange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502/r7.anchor: أي: في فضله أو وجوب صومه، وهذا غريب جدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r1.claim: The Qur’an guides the hearts of those who believe, affirm, and follow it; its clear proofs are understood by reflection, validate its guidance, oppose error, and distinguish truth from falsehood and lawful from unlawful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r1.anchor: هدى لقلوب العباد ممن آمن به وصدقه واتبعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r2.claim: A report says not to say simply “Ramadan,” because Ramadan is one of God’s names, but to say “the month of Ramadan”; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits it through Abu Maʿshar from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb and Saʿid al-Maqburi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: لا تقولوا: رمضان، فإن رمضان اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد، ومحمد بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim says similar disapproval of saying “Ramadan” alone was also reported from Mujahid and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r3.anchor: وقد روي عن مجاهد، ومحمد بن كعب نحو ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn Thabit allowed saying “Ramadan” without the word “month.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r4.anchor: ورخص فيه ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Abu Maʿshar Nujayh was an authority in campaigns and biographies but weak as a transmitter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r5.anchor: أبو معشر هو نجيح بن عبد الرحمن المدني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r6.claim: Abu Maʿshar’s son made the report Prophetic, but Ibn ʿAdi rejected that attribution; Ibn Kathir agrees, calling the son abandoned and his elevation of the report an error.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r6.anchor: وقد أنكره عليه الحافظ ابن عدي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r7.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r7.claim: Al-Bukhari supports using “Ramadan” alone by titling a chapter “It is said Ramadan” and citing reports such as the promise that fasting Ramadan with faith and seeking reward brings forgiveness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p502#2/r7.anchor: وقد انتصر البخاري، رحمه الله، في كتابه لهذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r1.claim: Witnessing Ramadan means being healthy and resident in one’s locality when the month begins; such a person is required to fast.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r1.anchor: إيجاب حتم على من شهد استهلال الشهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r2.speaker: author
