IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r2.claim: This verse abrogated the earlier permission for a healthy resident to skip the fast and feed one poor person for each missed day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r2.anchor: ونسخت هذه الآية الإباحة المتقدمة لمن كان صحيحا مقيما أن يفطر ويفدي بإطعام مسكين عن كل يوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r3.claim: A person whose illness makes fasting burdensome or harmful, or who is traveling, may break the fast and must make up the same number of days later.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r3.anchor: ومن كان به مرض في بدنه يشق عليه الصيام معه، أو يؤذيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r4.claim: The concessions for illness and travel, while fasting remains binding on the healthy resident, express divine ease and mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r4.anchor: إنما رخص لكم في الفطر في حال المرض وفي السفر، مع تحتمه في حق المقيم الصحيح، تيسيرا عليكم ورحمة بكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r5.speaker: طائفة من السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r5.claim: A group of early authorities held that someone resident when Ramadan began could not break the fast after traveling mid-month; travel only excused one who entered Ramadan already traveling.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r5.anchor: ذهب طائفة من السلف إلى أن من كان مقيما في أول الشهر ثم سافر في أثنائه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r6.speaker: ابن حزم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r6.claim: Ibn Hazm attributes the resident-then-travels position to a group of Companions and Successors, though Ibn Kathir questions the accuracy of that attribution.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r6.anchor: نقله أبو محمد بن حزم في كتابه المحلى، عن جماعة من الصحابة والتابعين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r7.claim: The Prophet set out during Ramadan for the conquest of Mecca, traveled as far as al-Kadid, then broke his fast and ordered the people to break theirs; both canonical compilers report it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r7.anchor: خرج في شهر رمضان لغزوة الفتح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r8.speaker: طائفة من الصحابة والتابعين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r8.claim: Some Companions and Successors considered breaking the fast obligatory for a traveler, taking “a number of other days” as a command to break and make up.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r8.anchor: ذهب آخرون من الصحابة والتابعين إلى وجوب الإفطار في السفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the majority view that travelers may choose to fast or break; reports say the Prophet’s companions did both without blaming one another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r9.anchor: والصحيح قول الجمهور، أن الأمر في ذلك على التخيير، وليس بحتم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r10.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r10.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that on a very hot Ramadan journey with the Prophet, no one fasted except the Prophet and ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503/r10.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء [قال] (6) خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and a group hold that fasting while traveling is preferable, based on the Prophet’s own practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.anchor: قالت طائفة منهم الشافعي: الصيام في السفر أفضل من الإفطار، لفعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.speaker: طائفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.claim: Another group prefers breaking the fast to accept the concession, citing the Prophet’s answer that either breaking or fasting is good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.anchor: وقالت طائفة: بل الإفطار أفضل، أخذا بالرخصة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.claim: When asked about fasting during travel, the Prophet said that the one who breaks the fast does well and there is no blame on the one who fasts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه سئل عن الصوم في السفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r4.claim: A separate Prophetic report urges travelers to take the concession God has granted them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r4.anchor: عليكم برخصة الله التي رخص لكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r5.speaker: طائفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r5.claim: A third group treats fasting and breaking the fast during travel as equally permissible.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r5.anchor: وقالت طائفة: هما سواء لحديث عائشة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r6.claim: When Hamza ibn ʿAmr al-Aslami asked whether to fast while traveling because he fasted often, the Prophet let him choose either course; the two canonical compilers report it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r6.anchor: إن شئت فصم، وإن شئت فأفطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r7.speaker: طائفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r7.claim: Some hold that breaking the fast is better when fasting is difficult, relying on the Prophet’s rebuke of fasting under hardship on a journey.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r7.anchor: قيل: إن شق الصيام فالإفطار أفضل لحديث جابر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r8.claim: Seeing a man shaded while fasting on a journey, the Prophet said that fasting while traveling was not righteousness; al-Bukhari and Muslim report it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r8.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلا قد ظلل عليه، فقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r9.claim: If a traveler is averse to God’s concession and regards breaking the fast as detestable, Ibn Kathir says he must break the fast and fasting is forbidden for him in that state.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r9.anchor: فهذا يتعين عليه الإفطار، ويحرم عليه الصيام، والحالة هذه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r10.speaker: ابن عمر وجابر وغيرهما
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r10.claim: Reports from Ibn ʿUmar, Jabir, and others say that one who refuses God’s concession bears sin like the mountains of ʿArafat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r10.anchor: من لم يقبل رخصة الله كان عليه من الإثم مثل جبال عرفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r11.speaker: قول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r11.claim: One legal view requires make-up fasts to be consecutive because the make-up should mirror the original performance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r11.anchor: أحدهما: أنه يجب التتابع، لأن القضاء يحكي الأداء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r12.speaker: جمهور السلف والخلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r12.claim: The majority of early and later scholars allow make-up fasts to be consecutive or separated; the sequence in Ramadan was required by the month’s fixed performance window, while afterward only the number of missed days is due.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r12.anchor: لا يجب التتابع، بل إن شاء فرق، وإن شاء تابع. وهذا قول جمهور السلف والخلف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r13.claim: A Bedouin who heard the Prophet reported that the best religion is the easiest religion, repeated twice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p503#2/r13.anchor: عن الأعرابي الذي سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r1.speaker: عروة بن الفقيمي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r1.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Fuqaymi reports that after the Prophet prayed with his head dripping from ablution or a bath, he answered questions about possible blame by repeating three times that God’s religion is ease.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r1.anchor: حدثني أبي عروة، قال: كنا ننتظر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r2.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s instruction to make matters easy rather than difficult, and to reassure people rather than drive them away; both canonical collections include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r2.anchor: يسروا، ولا تعسروا، وسكنوا ولا تنفروا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r3.claim: When sending Muʿadh and Abu Musa to Yemen, the Prophet told them to give good news, ease matters, cooperate, and avoid disagreement; both canonical collections report it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r3.anchor: بشرا ولا تنفرا، ويسرا ولا تعسرا، وتطاوعا ولا تختلفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r4.claim: Reports in the Sunan and Musnads say that the Prophet was sent with the upright, lenient religion.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r5.speaker: محجن بن الأدرع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r5.claim: Mahjan ibn al-Adraʿ reports that the Prophet cautioned him not to praise a man’s abundant prayer where the man could hear, lest he ruin him, and said God intended ease for this community.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r5.anchor: عن محجن بن الأدرع: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلا يصلي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r6.claim: God granted permission to break the fast for illness, travel, and similar excuses to provide ease, then required make-up fasting so the month’s full count would be completed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p504/r6.anchor: والسفر ونحوهما من الأعذار لإرادته بكم اليسر، وإنما أمركم بالقضاء لتكملوا عدة شهركم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r1.claim: The command to magnify God means remembering Him when worship is completed.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links remembrance after worship to commands to remember God after pilgrimage, prayer, Friday prayer, before sunset, and at night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r2.anchor: فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r3.claim: The Prophetic practice establishes the recommendation to glorify, praise, and magnify God after the obligatory prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r3.anchor: جاءت السنة باستحباب التسبيح، والتحميد والتكبير بعد الصلوات المكتوبات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they recognized that the Prophet had finished his prayer only by hearing him say the takbir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r4.anchor: ما كنا نعرف انقضاء صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا بالتكبير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says many scholars infer from this verse that takbir is prescribed at Eid al-Fitr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r5.anchor: أخذ كثير من العلماء مشروعية التكبير في عيد الفطر من هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r6.speaker: داود بن علي الأصبهاني الظاهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r6.claim: Dawud al-Zahiri holds that Eid al-Fitr takbir is obligatory, based on the apparent command in the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r6.anchor: إلى وجوبه في عيد الفطر؛ لظاهر الأمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that takbir is not prescribed at Eid al-Fitr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r7.anchor: أنه لا يشرع التكبير في عيد الفطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r8.speaker: الباقون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r8.claim: The remaining scholars recommend Eid al-Fitr takbir, though they differ over details of subsidiary rulings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505/r8.anchor: والباقون على استحبابه، على اختلاف في تفاصيل بعض الفروع بينهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#2/r1.claim: By obeying God’s commands, performing obligations, avoiding prohibitions, and guarding His limits, people may become thankful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#2/r1.anchor: إذا قمتم بما أمركم الله من طاعته بأداء فرائضه، وترك محارمه، وحفظ حدوده

JISHUMI:v1p764/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v1p764/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir reads Qur’an without hamza wherever the word occurs; the other readers pronounce the hamza, and both are linguistic forms.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحده القران بغير همز حيث كان، والباقون بالهمز، وهما لغتان.

JISHUMI:v1p764/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v1p764/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads al-yusr and al-ʿusr with gemination; the other readers lighten them, with no difference in meaning.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر اليسر والعسر بالتثقيل فيهما، والباقون بالتخفيف، والمعنى واحد.

JISHUMI:v1p764/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r5.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v1p764/r5.claim: Abu Bakr from ʿAsim geminates the m in wa-li-tukammilu; the others do not, and Abu al-ʿAbbas says akmala and kamala mean the same.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم: (ولتكملوا) بتشديد الميم، والباقون بالتخفيف،

JISHUMI:v1p764/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p764/r6.claim: The transmitted reading has damma on the rāʾ of Ramadan; readings attributed to Mujahid with fatḥa and Hasan with sukūn are not allowed because they lack widely transmitted support.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r6.anchor: وحكى أبو القاسم عن مجاهد بفتح الراء، وروي عن الحسن بسكون الراء، ولا تجوز القراءة بهما؛ لأنه خلاف النقل المستفيض.

JISHUMI:v1p764/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p764/r7.claim: A lunar month is twenty-nine or thirty days; legal month reckonings follow the crescents, except the impotent man’s waiting period, reckoned by a solar year according to the commentator’s school.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r7.anchor: والاعتبار في الشهر في أحكام الشرع بالأهلة إلا في مدة العنين، فعندنا يعتبر سنة شمسية لا قمرية.

JISHUMI:v1p764/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p764/r8.claim: The root of shahr means appearing: a report is made public and fame is the emergence of a notorious matter.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r8.anchor: وأصله من الظهور، يقال: شهرت الحديث أظهرته، والشهرة ظهور الأمر في شنعة.

JISHUMI:v1p764/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p764/r9.claim: Ramad means severe heat, and months were named for the seasons in which they fell; Ramadan coincided with hot weather. Its plural is ramadانات.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r9.anchor: رمضان أصل الرمض شدة الحر، وكانوا يسمون الشهور باسم الأزمنة التي فيها وقعت فوافق رمضان أيام الحر،

JISHUMI:v1p764/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p764/r10.claim: The name is variously said to be one of God’s names (making Ramadan “God’s month”), to refer to stones heated by the sun, or to burning away sins.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r10.anchor: واختلفوا، فقيل: سمي رمضان؛ لأن رمضان اسم من أسماء الله تعالى، كأنه قيل: شهر الله،

JISHUMI:v1p764/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p764/r11.claim: Qur’an derives from gathering, as recitation gathers letters.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r11.anchor: والقرآن: أصله الجمع، ومنه سمي القراءة؛ لأنها تجمع الحروف.

JISHUMI:v1p764/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p764/r12.claim: ʿUsr is difficulty and yusr is its opposite, ease.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r12.anchor: والعسر: الصعوبة، ونقيضه اليسر، وهو السهولة.

JISHUMI:v1p764/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p764/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p764/r13.claim: Ikmal means completing or bringing something to perfection; takbir means magnification.
JISHUMI:v1p764/r13.anchor: والإكمال من الكمال وهو التمام. والتكبير: التعظيم.

JISHUMI:v1p768/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r1.speaker: المجبرة
JISHUMI:v1p768/r1.claim: The commentator rejects the claim that guidance is identical to faith: God describes the Qur’an as guidance.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r1.anchor: فتدل على أن الهدى ليس هو نفس الإيمان كما تزعمه المجبرة؛ لأنه تعالى جعل القرآن هدى.

JISHUMI:v1p768/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r2.speaker: أصحاب المعارف
JISHUMI:v1p768/r2.claim: The commentator rejects the claim that knowledge is necessary: if it were necessary, calling the Qur’an guidance would add no benefit.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r2.anchor: وتدل على بطلان قول أصحاب المعارف؛ إذ لو كانت ضرورية لما أفاد وصفه بأنه هدى.

JISHUMI:v1p768/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r3.speaker: المجبرة
JISHUMI:v1p768/r3.claim: The ease God wills and hardship he does not will contradict the Mujbira claim that God wills every hardship for his servants.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r3.anchor: وهذا خلاف قولهم، فإنهم يزعمون أنه يريد كل عسر بعباده.

JISHUMI:v1p768/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r4.speaker: المجبرة
JISHUMI:v1p768/r4.claim: If God does not will hardship for people, he is even less likely to will imposing what they cannot bear or accomplish.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r4.anchor: لأنه إذا كان لا يريد بهم العسر فلأن لا يريد تكليف ما لا يطاق أولى.

JISHUMI:v1p768/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r5.speaker: المجبرة
JISHUMI:v1p768/r5.claim: The commentator rejects their doctrine of created acts because the verse attributes making ease and hardship to the responsible people.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r5.anchor: لأنه أثبت أن لهم فعلا بتعسير وتيسير، وتدل على بطلان قولهم أيضا

JISHUMI:v1p768/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r6.speaker: المجبرة
JISHUMI:v1p768/r6.claim: The command to complete the count shows God wills that all complete it, contrary to the Mujbira position.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r6.anchor: فبين أنه أراد من الجميع الإكمال، خلاف قول المجبرة.

JISHUMI:v1p768/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r7.speaker: المجبرة
JISHUMI:v1p768/r7.claim: The verse shows God wills gratitude from everyone; the commentator contrasts this with the Mujbira view that God wills neglect, gratitude, and disbelief according to each person’s act.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r7.anchor: أنه أراد من الجميع الشكر، وعندهم أراد الإهمال ممن فعله، والشكر ممن شكره، والكفر ممن كفره.

JISHUMI:v1p768/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p768/r8.claim: The verse shows that human welfare can depend on a particular place or time, which is why fasting is assigned to Ramadan.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r8.anchor: وتدل على أن المصالح قد تعلق بالمكان؛ والزمان لذلك أوجب صوم شهر رمضان.

JISHUMI:v1p768/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p768/r9.claim: The Qur’an was revealed on the Night of Decree; the commentator argues the statement is not merely a report about a past event and cites a past-form expression for a future event as an analogy.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r9.anchor: ولا يقال: إنه خبر عن الماضي؛ لأنه بمنزلة قوله: (ونادى أصحاب الجنة) يعني سينادي،

JISHUMI:v1p768/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p768/r10.claim: The Qur’an is guidance and evidence, and its meaning is intelligible; the commentator rejects claims that its apparent meaning cannot be known or that interpretation must be referred to an Imam, which would strip it of being guidance.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r10.anchor: وتدل على أن القرآن يفهم معناه، فيبطل قول من يخالف فيه، وقال: لا يعرف بظاهره،

JISHUMI:v1p768/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p768/r11.claim: The month-long fast is obligatory; all agree that a legally responsible person who witnesses the whole month must fast it, while a child reaching maturity or an unbeliever converting owes only the remaining days.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r11.anchor: ولا خلاف أن من شهد جميع الشهر وهو مكلف لزمه الصوم، واتفقوا أن الصبي إذا أدرك

JISHUMI:v1p768/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p768/r12.claim: Abu Hanifa requires a person recovering from insanity during the month to fast the entire month; al-Shafiʿi requires only the remaining days.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r12.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة يلزمه صوم الجميع، وقال الشافعي: لا يلزم إلا ما بقي،

JISHUMI:v1p768/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r13.speaker: الفقهاء
JISHUMI:v1p768/r13.claim: Jurists agree that the month is established by crescent sighting or by completing thirty days; the commentator rejects esoteric astronomical calculation as against consensus and an essential religious rule, and calls its adherents unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r13.anchor: الفقهاء كلهم على أنه يعتبر رؤية الأهلة، أو يكون بالعدد ثلاثين يوما، فأما الذي تزعمه الباطنية

JISHUMI:v1p768/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p768/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p768/r14.claim: The excerpt begins to distinguish evidentiary rules for sighting: fasting is established by one man’s testimony, but the following rule for breaking the fast is cut off.
JISHUMI:v1p768/r14.anchor: في الصوم بشهادة رجل واحد، وفي الفطر

JISHUMI:v1p765/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r1.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
JISHUMI:v1p765/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ and al-Akhfash analyze “month of Ramadan” as the predicate of an omitted subject, understood as “it is the month of Ramadan.”
JISHUMI:v1p765/r1.anchor: قال: شهر رمضان، عن الفراء والأخفش.

JISHUMI:v1p765/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r2.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p765/r2.claim: Al-Kisaʾi treats it as a nominative apposition to the passive subject of “fasting was prescribed upon you.”
JISHUMI:v1p765/r2.anchor: الثاني: على ما لم يسم فاعله بدلا من الصيام، كأنه قيل: كتب عليكم شهر رمضان، عن الكسائي.

JISHUMI:v1p765/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p765/r3.claim: A third nominative analysis makes “month of Ramadan” a subject whose predicate is “in which the Qur’an was sent down.”
JISHUMI:v1p765/r3.anchor: الثالث: الابتداء، وخبره الذي أنزل فيه القرآن.

JISHUMI:v1p765/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p765/r4.claim: Possible accusative analyses understand an imperative to fast Ramadan, make it an apposition to the numbered days, take it as an adverb according to al-Akhfash, or as an exhortation according to Abu ʿUbayda, like “God’s she-camel.”
JISHUMI:v1p765/r4.anchor: وفي نصبه وجوه: قيل: صوموا شهر رمضان، وقيل: بدلا من أيام معدودات.

JISHUMI:v1p765/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r5.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v1p765/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ connects wa-li-tukmilū to an omitted clause: the ordinance was given so that you complete the count.
JISHUMI:v1p765/r5.anchor: قيل: عطف على جملة؛ لأن بعده محذوفا، كأنه قيل: ولتكملوا العدة شرع ذلك، عن الفراء،

JISHUMI:v1p765/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r6.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p765/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead connects it to an implied clause indicated by what precedes: God made things easy for you so that you complete the count.
JISHUMI:v1p765/r6.anchor: وقيل: على تأويل محذوف دل عليه ما تقدم أن يسهل عليكم ولتكملوا العدة، عن الزجاج.

JISHUMI:v1p765/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p765/r7.claim: Huda is accusative as a circumstantial expression: the Qur’an was sent down as guidance.
JISHUMI:v1p765/r7.anchor: نصب على الحال، كأنه قيل: أنزل فيه القرآن هاديا.

JISHUMI:v1p765/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p765/r8.claim: The prepositional phrase “on a journey” coordinates with “ill” because it has the same meaning as “a traveler”; compare 10:12, where several states coordinate with “on his side.”
JISHUMI:v1p765/r8.anchor: لأنه بمعنى الاسم، كأنه قيل: أو مسافرا، ومثله: (دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما)

JISHUMI:v1p765/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p765/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p765/r9.claim: The passage next clarifies the time of fasting, its obligation, and the concession that applies to it.
JISHUMI:v1p765/r9.anchor: ثم بين تعالى وقت الصوم ووجوبه والرخصة فيه، فقال تعالى: (شهر رمضان)

JISHUMI:v1p760/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p760/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p760/r1.claim: If Ramadan fasting is said to abrogate every fast, this may mean obligatory fasts of earlier religious laws or a fast imposed on this community by another proof.
JISHUMI:v1p760/r1.anchor: قلنا: يحتمل كل صوم واجب في الشرائع المتقدمة، ويحتمل صياما وجب على هذه الأمة بغير الآية

JISHUMI:v1p760/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p760/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p760/r2.claim: The repeated illness-and-travel clause preserves the concession: residents initially chose fasting or ransom, while sick people and travelers could break fast; it clarifies they owe make-up days and reiterates their exemption after fasting became mandatory for residents.
JISHUMI:v1p760/r2.anchor: فلما نسخ التخيير في المقيم وحتم الصوم كان من الجائز أن يظن أن التضييق يعم المقيم والمسافر

JISHUMI:v1p760/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p760/r3.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p760/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the concession follows the labels: every sick person and traveler may break the fast.
JISHUMI:v1p760/r3.anchor: الرخصة تتبع الاسم فكل مريض ومسافر له أن يفطر، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v1p760/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p760/r4.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p760/r4.claim: Al-Aṣamm limits the concession to sick people and travelers who would suffer hardship by fasting.
JISHUMI:v1p760/r4.anchor: بل كل مريض ومسافر يلحقه الجهد إن صام، ومن لا جهد فلا رخصة، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v1p760/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p760/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p760/r5.claim: Jurists and most exegetes define qualifying illness as fasting causing harm or worsening illness; travel must reach a specified distance regardless of traveler’s effort.
JISHUMI:v1p760/r5.anchor: وفي السفر أن يكون قدرا مخصوصا، ولا اعتبار بحال المسافر وجهده، وعليه الفقهاء وأكثر المفسرين

JISHUMI:v1p760/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p760/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p760/r6.claim: A condition is omitted: if one breaks the fast, then an equal number of other days is due, as in the parallel head-injury rule in 2:196.
JISHUMI:v1p760/r6.anchor: لا بد من حذف وتقديره: فأفطر فعليه عدة ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r1.claim: Ramadan derives from رمض, to burn, associated with the heat of the hot ground; the month is attached to the word and the name is made proper.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r1.anchor: الرمضان مصدر رمض اذا احترق من الرمضاء فأضيف اليه الشهر وجعل علما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r2.claim: The proper name Ramadan is indeclinable here because it is definite and ends in alif and nun, like ابن داية for the crow.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r2.anchor: ومنع الصرف للتعريف والألف والنون كما قيل ( ابن داية ) للغراب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r3.claim: One explanation says the name reflects an ancient fasting practice: hunger's heat and hardship burned people, and the month was also called nātiq because its severity agitated them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r3.anchor: الصوم فيه عبادة قديمة فكأنهم سموه بذلك لارتماضهم فيه من حر الجوع ومقاساة شدته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r4.claim: Another explanation says the months were named for the seasons in which their names were transferred from the ancient language, and Ramadan coincided with hot days.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r4.anchor: وقيل لما نقلوا أسماء الشهور عن اللغة القديمة سموها بالأزمنة التى وقعت فيها فوافق هذا الشهر أيام رمض الحر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r5.claim: Hadiths that say simply Ramadan omit شهر because the meaning remains clear; the cited verse of poetry likewise omits ابن from Ibn Hudhaym.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r5.anchor: هو من باب الحذف لأمن الالباس كما قال ( بما أعيا النطاسي حذيما ) أراد ابن حذيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r6.claim: The nominative can make شهر رمضان a subject whose predicate is الذي أنزل فيه القرآن, a substitute for الصيام in 2:183, or the predicate of an omitted subject.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r7.claim: A reading in the accusative construes شهر رمضان as an imperative to fast, a substitute for أيام معدودات, or the object of أن تصوموا in 2:184.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r7.anchor: وقرىء بالنصب على صوموا شهر رمضان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r8.claim: The Qur'an's descent in Ramadan means its revelation began then, on Laylat al-Qadr.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r8.anchor: ومعنى ^ أنزل فيه القرآن ^ ابتدىء فيه إنزاله وكان ذلك في ليلة القدر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r9.claim: One view says the Qur'an descended all at once to the lowest heaven and then came down to earth gradually.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r9.anchor: وقيل أنزل جملة إلى سماء الدنيا ثم نزل إلى الأرض نجوما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r10.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r10.claim: Another view takes this as the Qur'an being revealed about Ramadan, namely the command that fasting was prescribed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r10.anchor: وقيل انزل في شأنه القرآن وهو قوله ^ كتب عليكم الصيام ^

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r11.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r11.claim: A report from the Prophet dates the scriptures: Abraham's pages on Ramadan's first night, the Torah after six days, the Gospel after thirteen, and the Qur'an after twenty-four.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p252#3/r11.anchor: وعن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام 91 ( نزلت صحف إبراهيم اول ليلة من رمضان وأنزلت التوراة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r1.claim: هُدى and بينات are accusatives of state: the Qur'an was sent as guidance to truth and as clear signs that guide and distinguish truth from falsehood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r1.anchor: نصب على الحال أي انزل وهو هداية للناس إلى الحق وهو آيات واضحات مكشوفات مما يهدي إلى الحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r2.claim: The wording first calls the Qur'an guidance generally, then specifies that it contains clear proofs among God's revealed guidance that distinguishes truth from error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r2.anchor: ذكر أولا انه هدى ثم ذكر أنه بينات من جملة ما هدى به الله وفرق به بين الحق والباطل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r3.claim: Whoever is present and resident during the month, rather than traveling, must fast and not break the fast.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r3.anchor: فمن كان شاهدا أي حاضرا مقيما غير مسافر في الشهر فليصم فيه ولا يفطر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r4.claim: الشهر and its pronoun are temporal accusatives, not direct objects as in شهدت الجمعة, since both residents and travelers witness the month.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r4.anchor: ولا يكون مفعولا به كقولك شهدت الجمعة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r5.claim: God intends ease, has removed religious hardship, and commands a tolerant, unburdened faith; the travel and illness concessions allowing a fast to be broken are examples.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r5.anchor: أن ييسر عليكم ولا يعسر وقد نفي عنكم الحرج في الدين وأمركم بالحنيفية السمحة التى لا إصر فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r6.speaker: من الناس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r6.claim: Some required the sick and travelers to break their fast and even claimed that if either group fasted, they had to repeat it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r6.anchor: ومن الناس من فرض الفطر على المريض والمسافر حتى زعم ان من صام منهما فعليه الاعادة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r7.claim: A reading pronounces both اليسر and العسر with a damma on the initial consonant.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r8.claim: The action whose purpose is expressed by ولتكملوا is omitted and supplied from what precedes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254/r8.anchor: الفعل المعلل محذوف مدلول عليه بما سبق تقديره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r1.claim: The legislation described—fasting for those present, making up missed days for those excused, and permission to break the fast—aims at completing the prescribed count.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r1.anchor: شرع ذلك يعني جملة ما ذكر من امر الشاهد بصوم الشهر وامر المرخص له بمراعاة عدة ما أفطر فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r2.claim: Completing the count is the purpose of keeping track of missed days; magnifying God is the purpose of the prescribed way of making them up; gratitude is the purpose of the concession and ease.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r2.anchor: علة ما علم من كيفية القضاء والخروج عن عهدة الفطر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r3.claim: This distribution of several purposes across the preceding rulings is a subtle form of لف that only a perceptive contemporary rhetorician readily detects.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r3.anchor: وهذا نوع من اللف لطيف المسلك لا يكاد يهتدي الي تبينه الا النقاب المحدث من علماء البيان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r4.claim: The verb تكبروا takes على because it includes the sense of praising: magnify God while praising Him for guiding you.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r4.anchor: وإنما عدى فعل التكبير بحرف الاستعلاء لكونه مضمنا معنى الحمد كانه قيل ولتكبروا الله حامدين على ما هداكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r5.claim: The phrase means that God intends for you to give thanks.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r6.claim: A reading has ولتكملوا with a doubled mīm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#2/r6.anchor: ولتكملوا ) بالتشديد فإن قلت هل يصح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r1.claim: It is possible to coordinate ولتكملوا with an omitted purpose or with اليسر, as in 61:8; the first analysis is stronger.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r1.anchor: قلت لا يبعد ذلك والأول اوجه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r2.claim: The takbir means exalting and praising God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r2.anchor: قلت ما المراد بالتكبير قلت تعظيم الله والثناء عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r3.claim: An alternative view identifies this takbir as the Eid al-Fitr takbir.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r3.anchor: وقيل هو تكبير يوم الفطر وقيل هو التكبير عند الإهلال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r4.claim: Another view identifies it as the takbir at the sighting of the new moon.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p254#3/r4.anchor: وقيل هو تكبير يوم الفطر وقيل هو التكبير عند الإهلال

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r1.claim: Shahr derives from notoriety or manifestation, as when someone draws and displays his sword.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r1.anchor: أما الشهر فمأخوذ من الشهرة , ومنه قيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r2.claim: Some linguists derive Ramadan from the severe heat that made young camels' feet burn; its naming is compared with Dhu al-Hijjah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r2.anchor: وأما رمضان فإن بعض أهل اللغة يزعم أنه سمي بذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r3.claim: Ramadan was called Natiq in pre-Islamic Arabia.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r3.anchor: وقد كان شهر رمضان يسمى في الجاهلية ناتقا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r4.claim: Mujahid disliked saying Ramadan, perhaps because he thought it might be one of God's names.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r4.anchor: وأما مجاهد فإنه كان يكره أن يقال رمضان

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r5.claim: One view says the whole Quran descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven on a Night of Decree in Ramadan, then was sent to the Prophet as God willed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r5.anchor: أن الله تعالى أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ إلى سماء الدنيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r6.claim: A report from the Prophet dates the scriptures: Abraham's scrolls on Ramadan's first night, Torah after six nights, Gospel after thirteen, and Quran after twenty-four.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r6.anchor: روى أبو مسلم عن وائلة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r7.claim: Mujahid interprets the Quran's descent in Ramadan as its revelation in connection with the obligation to fast Ramadan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r7.anchor: والثاني : أنه بمعنى أنزل القرآن في فرض صيامه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r8.claim: Hudā means guidance or right direction for people.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r9.claim: The clear signs explain lawful and unlawful matters, and the Criterion distinguishes truth from falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r9.anchor: أي بينات من الحلال والحرام , وفرقان بين الحق والباطل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r10.speaker: علي، ابن عباس، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r10.claim: One view requires a resident who witnesses the month's beginning to fast through its end and forbids breaking the remaining fast.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r10.anchor: أحدها : فمن شهد أول الشهر , وهو مقيم فعليه صيامه إلى آخره

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r11.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب، الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r11.claim: A second view requires fasting only the part of the month witnessed while resident, not the part spent away traveling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r11.anchor: والثاني : فمن شهد منكم الشهر , فليصم ما شهد منه وهو مقيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة وصاحباه
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r12.claim: A third view reads witnessing as being adult, sane, and legally responsible; becoming insane during the month does not cancel the duty for its remainder.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r12.anchor: والثالث : فمن شهد بالغا عاقلا مكلفا فليصمه , ولا يسقط صوم بقيته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r13.claim: The illness and travel concession is restated because its earlier mention belonged to an abrogated ruling; anyone who breaks the Ramadan fast for either reason must make up those days afterward.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r13.anchor: وإنما أعاد ذكر الفطر بالمرض والسفر مع قرب ذكره من قبل , لأنه في حكم تلك الآية منسوخا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r14.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r14.claim: Hasan al-Basri allows breaking the fast for any illness that prevents the person from praying while standing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r14.anchor: أحدها : أنه كل مرض لم يطق الصلاة معه قائما , وهذا قول الحسن البصري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r15.speaker: الشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r15.claim: Al-Shafi'i allows it when fasting is expected to worsen the illness by an intolerable amount.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r15.anchor: والثاني : أنه المرض الذي الأغلب من أمر صاحبه بالصوم الزيادة في علته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r16.speaker: ابن سيرين
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r16.claim: Ibn Sirin allows the concession for any condition that is called an illness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r16.anchor: والثالث : أنه كل مرض انطلق عليه اسم المرض , وهو قول ابن سيرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r17.speaker: داود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r17.claim: Dawud counts any journey, short or long, as travel for this concession.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r17.anchor: أحدها : أنه ما انطلق اسم السفر من طويل أو قصير , وهذا قول داود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r18.speaker: أبو حنيفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r18.claim: Abu Hanifa defines the relevant journey as a three-day journey.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r18.anchor: والثاني : أنه مسيرة ثلاثة أيام , وهو قول أبي حنيفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that breaking the fast while traveling is obligatory.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r19.anchor: أحدهما : أنه واجب وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r20.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r20.claim: The majority hold that breaking the fast while traveling is permitted rather than required.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r20.anchor: والثاني : أنه مباح , وهو قول الجمهور

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r21.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ease as breaking the fast and hardship as fasting while traveling; Mujahid and Qatada give a similar explanation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r21.anchor: قال ابن عباس : اليسر الإفطار , والعسر الصيام في السفر , ونحوه عن مجاهد وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r22.claim: Completing the count means making up the days missed from Ramadan by fasting them later.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r22.anchor: يعني عدة ما أفطر ثم في صيام شهر رمضان بالقضاء في غيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r23.claim: One explanation takes the command as the takbir of breaking the fast, beginning with the start of the month.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r23.anchor: قيل إنه تكبير الفطر من أول الشهر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r24.claim: One reading of the guidance is that it means guidance to the fast of Ramadan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r24.anchor: على ما هداكم } يعني من صيام شهر رمضان

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r25.claim: Māwardī also allows the phrase to refer generally to all the religion to which God guided people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r25.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون على عموم ما هدانا إليه من دينه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r26.claim: One possible object of gratitude is God's guidance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r27.claim: The other possible object of gratitude is the blessing of the reward granted for obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p239/r27.anchor: والثاني : على ما أنعم به من ثواب طاعته

MUQATIL:2:185/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:185/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:185/r1.claim: The Quran came down from the Preserved Tablet over twenty months, and Gabriel brought it down over twenty years.
MUQATIL:2:185/r1.anchor: من اللوح المحفوظ فى عشرين شهرا، وأنزل به جبريل، عليه السلام، عشرين سنة،

MUQATIL:2:185/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:185/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:185/r2.claim: The Quran guides in religion and gives clear proofs that distinguish guidance from doubt and misguidance; Muqatil glosses the criterion in 3:4 as an exit from doubts.
MUQATIL:2:185/r2.anchor: يعنى فى الدين من الشبهة والضلالة، نظيرها فى آل عمران [الآية: 4]:

MUQATIL:2:185/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:185/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:185/r3.claim: Anyone present for Ramadan must fast and not eat.
MUQATIL:2:185/r3.anchor: { فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه } ، فواجب عليه الصيام، ولا يطعم،

MUQATIL:2:185/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:185/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:185/r4.claim: A sick person who breaks the fast makes up the same number of days after recovery; the traveler does likewise, continuously or on separate days as desired.
MUQATIL:2:185/r4.anchor: { ومن كان } منكم { مريضا أو على سفر } ، فلم يصم، فإذا برئ المريض من مرضه، { فعدة } فليصم عدة { من أيام أخر }

MUQATIL:2:185/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:185/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:185/r5.claim: Ease means gentleness in religious duties through the concession allowing the sick and traveler to break the fast; without it, the duty would be hardship.
MUQATIL:2:185/r5.anchor: { يريد الله بكم اليسر } ، يعني الرفق فى أمر دينكم حين رخص للمريض والمسافر فى الفطر، { ولا يريد بكم العسر }

MUQATIL:2:185/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:185/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:185/r6.claim: Completing the count means making up the full number of counted days; takbir means magnifying God for His guidance in religion, and the verse calls people to thank Him for that blessing.
MUQATIL:2:185/r6.anchor: ثم قال عز وجل: { ولتكملوا العدة } ، يعنى تمام الأيام المعدودات، { ولتكبروا } ، يعني لكى تعظموا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r1.claim: شهر رمضان is a subject with the relative clause as predicate; alternatively it is an appositive to الصيام or a predicate after omitted هو.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r1.anchor: مبتدأ خبره ﴿ الذي أنزل فيه القرآن ﴾ أى ابتدى فيه إنزاله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s revelation began in Ramadan on the Night of Decree; alternatively the verse was revealed about the fasting duty in 2:183.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r2.anchor: وكان ذلك فى ليلة القدر أو أنزل فى شأنه القرآن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r3.claim: Ramadan derives from رمض, burning from hot ground; it became the month’s name and is indeclinable because it is definite and ends in ألف ونون. The name recalls hunger’s hardship or seasonal heat.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r3.anchor: والرمضان مصدر رمض إذا احترق من الرمضاء فأضيف إليه الشهر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r4.claim: In the hadith صام رمضان, شهر is omitted from شهر رمضان; the omission is understood from context and causes no ambiguity.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r4.anchor: هو من باب الحذف لا من الإلباس

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r5.speaker: مكي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r5.anchor: القرآن حيث كان غير مهموز مكى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r6.claim: هدى and بينات are circumstantial accusatives: the Qur’an was sent as guidance, with clear signs distinguishing truth from falsehood.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r6.anchor: على الحال أى أنزل وهو هداية للناس إلى الحق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r7.claim: These signs belong to God’s guidance through revelation and heavenly books, distinguishing truth from falsehood and guidance from error.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r7.anchor: ذكر أولا أنه هدى ثم ذكر أنه بينات من جملة ما هدى به الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r8.claim: Anyone present and resident during the month must fast it; a traveler need not fast while traveling.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r8.anchor: فمن كان شاهدا أى حاضرا مقيما غير مسافر فى الشهر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r9.claim: الشهر and the pronoun in ليصمه are temporal adverbials, not direct objects, since residents and travelers both witness the month.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r9.anchor: والشهر منصوب على الظرف وكذا الهاء فى ليصمه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r10.claim: The sick and traveler may defer fasting and make up an equal number of days later; عدة is a subject with its predicate omitted.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r10.anchor: فعدة مبتدأ والخبر محذوف أى فعليه عدة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r11.claim: Allowing the sick and traveler to break the fast expresses the intended ease.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r12.claim: The author rejects requiring sick people and travelers to break the fast and repeat it if they fast, since that contradicts the stated ease.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r12.anchor: ومن فرض الفطر على المريض والمسافر حتى لو صاما تجب عليهما الإعادة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r13.claim: The causal verb is omitted but supplied by the preceding clause; completing the count explains the instruction to make up missed days.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p90/r13.anchor: والفعل المعلل محذوف مدلول عليه بما سبق تقديره

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r1.claim: Completing the count is the reason to make up missed days.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r1.anchor: فقوله لتكملوا علة الأمر بمراعاة العدة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r2.claim: Magnifying God explains the way to discharge the missed-fast obligation through makeup.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r2.anchor: ولتكبروا علة ما علم من كيفية القضاء والخروج من عهدة الفطر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r3.claim: The hope of gratitude explains the concession to break the fast; this is a subtle form of لف.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r3.anchor: ولعلكم تشكرون علة الترخيص وهذا نوع من اللف اللطيف المسلك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r4.claim: على accompanies magnification because it carries the sense of praise: magnify God while praising Him for guidance.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r4.anchor: وعدى التكبير بعلى لتضمنه معنى الحمد كأنه قيل لتكبروا الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r5.speaker: أبو بكر
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91/r5.claim: Abu Bakr reads لتكملوا with a doubled mīm.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r1.speaker: عثمان بن أبي العاص الثقفي وأنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r1.claim: Uthman ibn Abi al-As and Anas, as well as Abu Hanifa and his companions, hold that fasting while traveling is better for one able to bear it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r1.anchor: روي عن عثمان بن أبي العاص الثقفي وأنس بن مالك صاحبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنهما قالا: الصوم في السفر أفضل لمن قدر عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r2.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r2.claim: Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, and the other listed authorities hold that taking the travel concession and breaking the fast is preferable, citing God's intent of ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r2.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر وابن عباس: الرخصة أفضل، وقال به سعيد بن المسيب والشعبي وعمر بن عبد العزيز

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r3.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r3.claim: The majority say that an ill resident unable to fast when the community fasted a 29-day Ramadan makes up 29 days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r3.anchor: والجمهور من العلماء على أن أهل البلد إذا صاموا تسعة وعشرين يوما وفي البلد رجل مريض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r4.speaker: الحسن بن صالح بن حي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r4.claim: Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy says the person makes up a whole month for a whole month, without matching the number of days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r4.anchor: وقال قوم منهم الحسن بن صالح بن حي: إنه يقضي شهرا بشهر من غير مراعاة عدد الأيام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r5.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r5.claim: Al-Kiya rejects making up a full month regardless of length: the verse requires a count of days, so missed days must be replaced day for day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r5.anchor: قال الكيا الطبري: وهذا بعيد لقوله تعالى: { فعدة من أيام أخر } ولم يقل فشهر من أيام أخر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r6.claim: The clause omits an understood condition: whoever among you is ill or traveling and breaks the fast must make it up.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r6.anchor: في الكلام حذف أي من يكن منكم مريضا أو مسافرا فأفطر فليقض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r7.claim: ʿIdda is nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, with the sense that the ruling or duty is a counted number of days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r7.anchor: ارتفع «عدة» على خبر الابتداء، تقديره فالحكم أو فالواجب عدة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r8.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r8.claim: Al-Kisa'i allows ʿidda to be read as an implied imperative: let the person fast a number of other days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r8.anchor: وقال الكسائي: ويجوز فعدة أي فليصم عدة من أيام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r9.claim: Another parse supplies the omitted noun ṣiyām, with ʿidda standing in its place.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r9.anchor: وقيل: المعنى فعليه صيام عدة فحذف المضاف وأقيمت العدة مقامه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r10.claim: ʿIdda is a count or counted amount, like ṭaḥn for what is ground; the same noun is used for a woman's waiting period.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r10.anchor: والعدة فعلة من العد، وهي بمعنى المعدود كالطحن بمعنى المطحون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r11.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r11.claim: Sibawayh says ukhar is indeclinable because it is an adjectival form shifted from the form normally used with the definite article.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r11.anchor: لم ينصرف «أخر» عند سيبويه، لأنها معدولة عن الألف واللام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r12.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r12.claim: Al-Kisa'i derives ukhar from akhar by analogy with ḥamrāʾ and ḥumr, explaining its indeclinability.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r12.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هي معدولة عن آخر، كما تقول: حمراء وحمر فلذلك لم تنصرف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r13.claim: One explanation is that ukhar is indeclinable because it has a plural pattern while describing days; ukhrā was avoided lest it seem to modify ʿidda.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r13.anchor: وقيل: منعت من الصرف لأنها على وزن جمع وهي صفة لأيام ولم تجىء أخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r14.claim: Another explanation derives ukhar as the plural of ukhrā, as in the expanded form ayyāmun ukhrā.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r14.anchor: وقيل: إن { أخر } جمع أخرى كأنه أيام أخرى ثم كثرت فقيل: أيام أخر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r15.claim: A further explanation says days take a feminine adjective, accounting for the form ukhar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r15.anchor: وقيل: إن نعت الأيام يكون مؤنثا فلذلك نعتت بأخر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r16.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r16.claim: Aisha reports that “consecutive” was revealed after “a number of other days” and later dropped; al-Daraqutni grades the chain sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185/r16.anchor: فروي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: نزلت «فعدة من أيام أخر متتابعات» فسقطت «متتابعات» قال هذا إسناد صحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#2/r1.claim: The earlier concession is removed by the command to fast, except for those unable to do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#2/r1.anchor: فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه [البقرة: 185] فزالت الرخصة إلا لمن عجز منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r1.speaker: أهل التاريخ
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r1.claim: Historians say Noah was the first to fast Ramadan, after leaving the Ark.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r1.anchor: قال أهل التاريخ: أول من صام رمضان نوح عليه السلام لما خرج من السفينة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r2.claim: Mujahid had said God prescribed Ramadan for every community; the author notes that communities existed before Noah and leaves the matter to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم قول مجاهد: كتب الله رمضان على كل أمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r3.claim: Shahr (month) derives from public visibility or renown, since a month is readily known to anyone seeking it; the same root is used for drawing a sword.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r3.anchor: والشهر مشتق من الإشهار لأنه مشتهر لا يتعذر علمه على أحد يريده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r4.claim: One derivation connects Ramadan with the fasting person's scorching thirst and severe heat called ramaḍāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r4.anchor: ورمضان مأخوذ من رمض الصائم يرمض إذا حر جوفه من شدة العطش

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r5.claim: The cited Muslim hadith says the prayer of the repentant is when the young camels' feet are scorched by hot ground and they crouch from its heat.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r5.anchor: والرمضاء ممدودة: شدة الحر ومنه الحديث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r6.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r6.claim: Al-Jawhari notes the plurals ramaḍānāt and armidāʾ and reports that ancient month names were drawn from the seasons in which they occurred; Ramadan coincided with scorching heat.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r6.anchor: قال الجوهري: وشهر رمضان يجمع على رمضانات وأرمضاء يقال إنهم لما نقلوا أسماء الشهور عن اللغة القديمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r7.claim: Another proposed derivation is that Ramadan burns away sins through good works.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: إنما سمي رمضان لأنه يرمض الذنوب أي يحرقها بالأعمال الصالحة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r8.claim: Another explanation likens hearts receiving the heat of admonition and reflection on the afterlife to sand and stones heated by the sun.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r8.anchor: وقيل: لأن القلوب تأخذ فيه من حرارة الموعظة والفكرة في أمر الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r9.speaker: ابن السكيت
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r9.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit connects the name to rubbing a blade between stones to thin it; weapons were prepared in Ramadan for fighting in Shawwal before the sacred months.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو من رمضت النصل أرمضه وأرمضه رمضا إذا دققته بين حجرين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r10.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r10.claim: Al-Mawardi reports that Ramadan was called Nātiq in pre-Islamic times and cites a poem using that name.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r10.anchor: وحكى الماوردي أن اسمه في الجاهلية «ناتق» وأنشد للمفضل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r11.claim: The common nominative reading makes shahr the subject and “in which the Qur'an was sent down” its predicate; alternatives supply an omitted subject such as the prescribed month of fasting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r11.anchor: و «شهر» بالرفع قراءة الجماعة على الابتداء، والخبر { الذي أنزل فيه القرآن }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r12.claim: A further parse makes shahr the subject, the relative phrase its adjective, and “whoever witnesses the month” the predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «شهر» مبتدأ، و { الذي أنزل فيه القرآن } صفة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r13.claim: Repeating the month gives emphasis, as in the cited wording about the Inevitable Hour.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#3/r13.anchor: وأعيد ذكر الشهر تعظيما، كقوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r1.speaker: أبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r1.claim: Abu Ali says the phrase can carry a conditional sense because Ramadan, though definite in form, does not designate one fixed month across years.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r1.anchor: وجاز أن يدخله معنى الجزاء، لأن شهر رمضان وإن كان معرفة فليس معرفة بعينها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r2.claim: Mujahid and Shahr ibn Hawshab, with Harun al-A'war transmitting from Abu Amr, read shahr in the accusative as an imperative to observe or fast Ramadan.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r2.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب نصب «شهر»، ورواها هارون الأعور عن أبي عمرو

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r3.claim: On the accusative reading the relative phrase modifies shahr; it cannot be governed by “you fast,” which would split the relative clause from its antecedent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز أن ينتصب بتصوموا لئلا يفرق بين الصلة والموصول بخبر أن وهو «خير لكم»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r4.speaker: الرماني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r4.claim: Al-Rummani allows the accusative shahr as an appositive to “numbered days” in 2:184.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r4.anchor: الرماني: يجوز نصبه على البدل من قوله أياماً معدودات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r5.claim: Mujahid disliked saying Ramadan without “month,” preferring the Qur'anic wording; he cited a report against the bare name and the claim that Ramadan is one of God's names.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r5.anchor: واختلف هل يقال «رمضان» دون أن يضاف إلى شهر فكره ذلك مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r6.claim: The report saying not to say Ramadan because it is a divine name is unsound: it comes through Abu Maʿshar Nujayh, whom the author calls weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r6.anchor: وهذا ليس بصحيح فإنه من حديث أبي معشر نجيح وهو ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r7.claim: It is sound and permissible to use “Ramadan” without adding “month,” as established in authentic collections.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r7.anchor: والصحيح جواز إطلاق رمضان من غير إضافة كما ثبت في الصحاح وغيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r8.claim: The Prophet said that when Ramadan comes, the gates of mercy open, Hell's gates close, and the devils are chained; Muslim transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r8.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r9.claim: Al-Busti transmits a similar report from Abu Hurayra: in Ramadan the gates of mercy and Hell are opened or closed respectively, and devils are chained.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r9.anchor: وفي صحيح البستي عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r10.speaker: أبو حاتم البستي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r10.claim: Al-Busti identifies Anas ibn Abi Anas as Malik ibn Anas's father, named Malik ibn Abi Amir and among Medina's trustworthy authorities.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r10.anchor: قال البستي: أنس بن أبي أنس هذا هو والد مالك بن أنس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r11.claim: The Prophet called Ramadan blessed, prescribed its fast, and said heaven's gates open, Hell's gates close, rebellious devils are fettered, and it contains a night better than a thousand months.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#4/r11.anchor: وروى النسائي عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r1.speaker: أبو حاتم البستي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r1.claim: Al-Busti explains that “rebellious devils” specifies which devils are meant by reports that devils are chained or fettered.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r1.anchor: وأخرجه أبو حاتم البستي أيضا وقال: فقوله «مردة الشياطين» تقييد لقوله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r2.claim: The Prophet told an Ansari woman to perform ʿumra in Ramadan, saying it is equivalent to a hajj; al-Nasa'i transmits it from Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r2.anchor: وروى النسائي أيضا عن ابن عباس قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r3.claim: The Prophet said God prescribed Ramadan fasting and the Prophet prescribed its night prayer; whoever fasts and prays in faith and hope is freed from sin as on the day of birth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r3.anchor: وروى النسائي أيضا عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r4.claim: Arabic may omit the word month before Ramadan, as in the cited reports; the month has great merit and reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r4.anchor: والآثار في هذا كثيرة، كلها بإسقاط شهر. وربما أسقطت العرب ذكر الشهر من رمضان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r5.claim: Ramadan's derivation as a month that burns away sins accords with its great reward and the cited hadiths.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r5.anchor: وفضل رمضان عظيم، وثوابه جسيم يدل على ذلك معنى الاشتقاق من كونه محرقا للذنوب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r6.claim: Fasting Ramadan means fasting for the lunar month indicated by its crescent; in the report “if the month is obscured,” month means crescent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r6.anchor: فرض الله صيام شهر رمضان أي مدة هلاله، وبه سمي الشهر كما جاء في الحديث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r7.claim: A cited poem likens the moon at the start of a month to a fingernail clipping and describes its growth into a full circle in a little over ten days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r7.anchor: والشهر مثل قلامة الظفر حتى تكامل في استدارته في أربع زادت على عشر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r8.claim: When the crescent is obscured, complete Shaʿban to thirty days before Ramadan and Ramadan to thirty before ending it, ensuring entry and exit from worship with certainty.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r8.anchor: وفرض علينا عند غمة الهلال إكمال عدة شعبان ثلاثين يوما وإكمال عدة رمضان ثلاثين يوما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r9.claim: God sent the Reminder to explain what was revealed to people, supporting this legal explanation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r9.anchor: وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r10.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r10.claim: Reports say to fast on sighting the crescent and break on sighting it; if obscured, complete the count, or count thirty days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r10.anchor: صوموا لرؤيته وأفطروا لرؤيته فإن غم عليكم فأكملوا العدد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r11.speaker: مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير وابن قتيبة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r11.claim: Mutarrif and Ibn Qutayba hold that when clouds hide the moon, Ramadan may be determined by calculating its lunar stations, such that a clear sky would have shown it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#5/r11.anchor: وقد ذهب مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير وهو من كبار التابعين وابن قتيبة من اللغويين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r1.speaker: مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير وابن قتيبة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r1.claim: They interpret “estimate it” as using the moon's stations to complete the month by calculation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r1.anchor: أي استدلوا عليه بمنازله، وقدروا إتمام الشهر بحسابه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r2.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r2.claim: The majority interpret “estimate it” as completing the count, as Abu Hurayra's report explains; the author says calculation is opposed by consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r2.anchor: وقال الجمهور: معنى «فاقدروا له» فأكملوا المقدار يفسره حديث أبي هريرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r3.speaker: الداودي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r3.claim: Al-Dawudi records an interpretation of “estimate it” as calculating the moon's stations.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r3.anchor: وذكر الداودي أنه قيل في معنى قوله «فاقدروا له»: أي قدروا المنازل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r4.speaker: ابن نافع عن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r4.claim: Ibn Nafiʿ reports Malik's ruling that an imam who starts and ends Ramadan by calculation rather than sighting is not to be followed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r4.anchor: وقد روى ابن نافع عن مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects as an error the claim by some associates that al-Shafiʿi relied on calculation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r5.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وقد زل بعض أصحابنا فحكى عن الشافعي أنه قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r6.claim: Malik requires two witnesses for Ramadan crescent testimony, by analogy with testimony for Shawwal and Dhu al-Hijja.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r6.anchor: فقال مالك: لا يقبل فيه شهادة الواحد لأنها شهادة على هلال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r7.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and Abu Hanifa accept one witness, relying on Ibn Umar's report that the Prophet fasted and ordered others to fast after Ibn Umar's sighting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r7.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأبو حنيفة: يقبل الواحد لما رواه أبو داود عن ابن عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r8.speaker: الدارقطني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r8.claim: Al-Daraqutni says the Ibn Umar report is uniquely transmitted by Marwan ibn Muhammad from Ibn Wahb and calls Marwan trustworthy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r8.anchor: وأخرجه الدارقطني وقال: تفرد به مروان بن محمد عن ابن وهب وهو ثقة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r9.claim: Al-Daraqutni reports a man testified before Ali to seeing Ramadan's crescent; Ali fasted and apparently ordered people to fast, preferring that over missing Ramadan.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r9.anchor: روى الدارقطني «أن رجلا شهد عند علي بن أبي طالب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r10.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r10.claim: Al-Shafiʿi first says he would accept one upright man's sighting if the public had not seen Ramadan's crescent, on the basis of the report and precaution.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r10.anchor: قال الشافعي: فإن لم تر العامة هلال شهر رمضان ورآه رجل عدل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r11.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r11.claim: Al-Shafiʿi later says Ramadan requires two witnesses; some associates also require two by analogy with other hidden matters.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r11.anchor: وقال الشافعي بعد: لا يجوز على رمضان إلا شاهدان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r12.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r12.claim: Al-Shafiʿi, as transmitted by al-Rabiʿ, says a lone witness to Ramadan should fast and one to Shawwal should end the fast discreetly.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#6/r12.anchor: فروى الربيع عن الشافعي: من رأى هلال رمضان وحده فليصمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r1.claim: Malik says a lone witness to Ramadan should fast, but one to Shawwal should not break fast, lest people falsely claim sighting to excuse breaking.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r1.anchor: وروى ابن وهب عن مالك في الذي يرى هلال رمضان وحده أنه يصوم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r2.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r2.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir attributes Malik's rule to al-Layth ibn Saʿd and Ahmad ibn Hanbal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r2.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وبهذا قال الليث بن سعد وأحمد بن حنبل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r3.speaker: عطاء وإسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r3.claim: Ata and Ishaq say the lone observer neither fasts on Ramadan nor breaks fast on Shawwal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء وإسحق: لا يصوم ولا يفطر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r4.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir's own view is that the lone observer both fasts and breaks fast according to what he saw.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r5.speaker: عكرمة والقاسم وسالم وابن عباس وإسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r5.claim: Nearby localities share a sighting; faraway localities follow their own, as reported from Ikrima, al-Qasim, Salim, Ibn Abbas, and Ishaq.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r5.anchor: فإن قرب فالحكم واحد، وإن بعد فلأهل كل بلد رؤيتهم روي هذا عن عكرمة والقاسم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r6.speaker: البخاري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r6.claim: Al-Bukhari signals the separate-locality view in his chapter heading, “Each locality has its own sighting.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r6.anchor: وإليه أشار البخاري حيث بوب: «لأهل كل بلد رؤيتهم»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r7.speaker: الليث بن سعد والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r7.claim: Al-Layth and al-Shafiʿi say that if a sighting is widely established in one locality, other localities must make up missed fasting days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r7.anchor: هكذا قال الليث بن سعد والشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r8.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r8.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says this is also the view of al-Muzani and the Iraqis.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r8.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: ولا أعلمه إلا قول المزني والكوفي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r9.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r9.claim: The Hanafis say that if one town fasted thirty days by sighting and another only twenty-nine, the latter must make up one day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r9.anchor: وأجمع أصحاب أبي حنيفة على أنه إذا صام أهل بلد ثلاثين يوما للرؤية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r10.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r10.claim: Shafiʿi authorities do not require the extra day because lunar horizons may differ between towns.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r10.anchor: وأصحاب الشافعي لا يرون ذلك إذ كانت المطالع في البلدان يجوز أن تختلف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r11.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r11.claim: The Hanafis argue that “complete the number” requires the town with evidence of a thirty-day month to complete thirty days as well.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r11.anchor: وحجة أصحاب أبي حنيفة قوله تعالى: { ولتكملوا العدة } وثبت برؤية أهل بلد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r12.speaker: مخالفو أصحاب أبي حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r12.claim: Their opponents cite the command to fast and break on sighting, which makes each locality's own practice relevant.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r12.anchor: ومخالفهم يحتج بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r13.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r13.claim: Abu Umar reports consensus that sightings do not govern distant lands such as al-Andalus and Khurasan: each has its own, except large cities and nearby districts.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r13.anchor: وحكى أبو عمر الإجماع على أنه لا تراعى الرؤية فيما بعد من البلدان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r14.claim: In Muslim's report from Kurayb, Ibn Abbas says Medina's Saturday sighting governs them despite Syria seeing the crescent Friday; they fast until thirty days or sighting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r14.anchor: فقال: لكنا رأيناه ليلة السبت فلا نزال نصوم حتى نكمل ثلاثين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r15.claim: Asked whether Muʿawiya's sighting and fast sufficed, Ibn Abbas answered that the Prophet had instructed them otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r15.anchor: فقلت: أو لا نكتفي برؤية معاوية وصيامه؟ فقال لا، هكذا أمرنا رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r16.claim: The scholars treat Ibn Abbas's words as explicitly attributing the rule to the Prophet; distant localities follow separate sightings unless the supreme imam compels unified practice, in which case he must be obeyed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#7/r16.anchor: فهو حجة على أن البلاد إذا تباعدت كتباعد الشام من الحجاز

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r1.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r1.claim: Al-Kiya says Ibn Abbas's “the Messenger ordered us” could interpret the Prophet's instruction to fast and break on sighting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r1.anchor: وقال الكيا الطبري: قوله «هكذا أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم» يحتمل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi weighs rejecting Kurayb as a lone reporter against rejecting cross-region transfer because horizons differ; he prefers the latter, since Kurayb reported a proven ruling and the Aghmat-Seville horizons can differ.
