QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r2.anchor: وقال ابن العربي: «واختلف في تأويل قول ابن عباس هذا فقيل: رده لأنه خبر واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r3.speaker: ابن وهب وابن القاسم عن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r3.claim: Malik's reported view is that a Basra Ramadan sighting reaching Kufa, Medina, or Yemen obliges them to fast or make up the missed fast.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r3.anchor: فروى ابن وهب وابن القاسم عنه في المجموعة أن أهل البصرة إذا رأوا هلال رمضان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r4.speaker: ابن الماجشون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r4.claim: Ibn al-Majishun says a publicly established Basra sighting obliges other towns to make up missed fasting; if established only by two witnesses before a local judge, it applies within his jurisdiction, unless the caliph confirms it for all Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r4.anchor: عن ابن الماجشون أنه إن كان ثبت بالبصرة بأمر شائع ذائع يستغنى عن الشهادة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r5.claim: The common nominative reading treats shahr as predicate of an omitted subject; alternatives make it the passive subject of kutiba, a subject with the relative phrase as predicate, or an appositive to fasting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r5.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «شهر» بالرفع على أنه خبر ابتداء مضمر أي ذلكم شهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r6.claim: The parse depends on whether the earlier command to fast referred to three days and ʿAshura or already to Ramadan: the former favors a fresh subject, the latter allows a subject or apposition to fasting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r6.anchor: فمن قال: إن الصيام في قوله { كتب عليكم الصيام } هي ثلاثة أيام وعاشوراء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r7.speaker: مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r7.claim: Mujahid and Shahr ibn Hawshab read shahr in the accusative; al-Kisa'i and al-Farra explain it as the obligation to fast the month.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r7.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب «شهر» بالنصب. قال الكسائي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r8.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r8.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects governing the accusative by taṣūmū or ṣiyām because it splits the relative clause; he allows an imperative “observe Ramadan,” though considers it distant because the month was not mentioned.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#8/r8.anchor: قال النحاس: «لا يجوز أن ينتصب «شهر رمضان» بتصوموا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r1.claim: The earlier “fasting was prescribed” implies the month, allowing an imperative accusative to observe Ramadan; Abu Ubayd prefers this analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r1.anchor: قوله { كتب عليكم الصيام } يدل على الشهر فجاز الإغراء وهو اختيار أبي عبيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r2.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash parses the accusative shahr as an adverbial expression.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r3.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r3.claim: Hasan and Abu Amr are reported to assimilate the rāʾ of Ramadan into the preceding rāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r3.anchor: وحكي عن الحسن وأبي عمرو إدغام الراء في الراء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r4.claim: The author says direct assimilation is impermissible because it brings together two unvoweled consonants; the Kufans shift the rāʾ vowel to hāʾ before assimilation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r4.anchor: وهذا لا يجوز لئلا يجتمع ساكنان ويجوز تقلب حركة الراء على الهاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r5.claim: The verse explicitly places the Qur'an's revelation in Ramadan and explains the verses about a blessed night and the Night of Decree; Laylat al-Qadr is therefore in Ramadan alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r5.anchor: نص في أن القرآن نزل في شهر رمضان، وهو يبين قوله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r6.claim: The agreed account is that the Qur'an descended whole from the Preserved Tablet to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then Gabriel brought it piecemeal over twenty years.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r6.anchor: ولا خلاف أن القرآن أنزل من اللوح المحفوظ ليلة القدر على ما بيناه جملة واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Qur'an descended whole to the scribes in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brought verses one or two at a time over twenty-one years.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أنزل القرآن من اللوح المحفوظ جملة واحدة إلى الكتبة في سماء الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r8.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r8.claim: Muqatil describes staged revelation from the Preserved Tablet; the author says this contradicts the consensus that the Qur'an descended all at once.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r8.anchor: قلت: وقول مقاتل هذا خلاف ما نقل من الإجماع «أن القرآن أنزل جملة واحدة»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r9.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r9.claim: Wathila reports that Abraham's scrolls came on Ramadan's first night, Torah after six nights, Gospel after thirteen, and Qur'an after twenty-four.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r9.anchor: وروى واثلة بن الأسقع عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r10.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r10.claim: The author says Wathila's report supports al-Hasan's view that Laylat al-Qadr falls on the twenty-fourth night.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r10.anchor: قلت: وفي هذا الحديث دلالة على ما يقوله الحسن أن ليلة القدر تكون ليلة أربع وعشرين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r11.claim: Qur'an names God's speech and means “that which is recited”; it can be a verbal noun, like calling what is drunk a drink and what is written a book.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r11.anchor: «القرآن»: اسم لكلام الله تعالى، وهو بمعنى المقروء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r12.claim: The author also analyzes Qur'an as the verbal noun of qaraʾa, meaning recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#9/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا قيل: هو مصدر قرأ يقرأ قراءة وقرآنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r1.claim: The cited line of poetry uses Qur'an to mean recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r1.anchor: ضحوا بأسمط عنوان السجود به يقطع الليل تسبيحا وقرآنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r2.claim: A Muslim report from Ibn Umar says Solomon imprisoned devils in the sea and they may emerge to recite a Qur'an to people; here Qur'an means recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r2.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن عبد الله بن عمر أن في البحر شياطين مسجونة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r3.claim: “Qur'an of dawn” means the dawn recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r3.anchor: وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا [الإسراء: 78] أي قراءة الفجر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r4.claim: Arabic names objects by verbal nouns; usage made Qur'an the name of God's speech, and “uncreated Qur'an” means the recited text, not recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r4.anchor: فصار القرآن اسما لكلام الله، حتى إذا قيل: القرآن غير مخلوق، يراد به المقروء لا القراءة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r5.claim: The written codex may also be called Qur'an by extension; the Prophet's ban on traveling with the Qur'an to enemy territory means the muṣḥaf.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r5.anchor: وقد يسمى المصحف الذي يكتب فيه كلام الله قرآنا توسعا وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r6.claim: Another derivation connects Qur'an to qaraʾtu, “I gathered.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r6.anchor: وهو مشتق من قرأت الشيء جمعته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r7.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is reported to treat Qur'an as an un-derived proper name, like Torah and Gospel; the author prefers derivation for all three.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو اسم علم لكتاب الله، غير مشتق كالتوراة والإنجيل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r8.claim: Hudā is an accusative circumstantial phrase describing the Qur'an as guiding people, and bayyināt is coordinated with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r8.anchor: «هدى» في موضع نصب على الحال من القرآن، أي هاديا لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r9.claim: Al-hudā means guidance and explanation; the Qur'an as a whole, including clear and ambiguous and abrogating and abrogated passages, guides and explains.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r9.anchor: و { الهدى } الإرشاد والبيان، كما تقدم أي بيانا لهم وإرشادا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r10.claim: The verse singles out manifest proofs: lawful and forbidden rulings, admonitions, and judgments; bayyināt is plural of bayyina from “be clear.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r10.anchor: ثم شرف بالذكر والتخصيص البينات منه، يعني الحلال والحرام والمواعظ والأحكام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r11.claim: Furqan is what separates truth from falsehood, that is, what distinguishes between them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r11.anchor: { والفرقان } ما فرق بين الحق والباطل، أي فصل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r12.claim: The common reading has the lām of command in the jussive; al-Hasan and al-Aʿraj read it with kasra.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r12.anchor: قراءة العامة بجزم اللام. وقرأ الحسن والأعرج بكسر اللام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r13.claim: The command lām is normally kasra when isolated; after fa, wāw, or thumma it may be jussive or kasra, as in the cited examples.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#10/r13.anchor: وحقها الكسر إذا أفردت فإذا وصلت بشيء ففيها وجهان: الجزم والكسر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r1.claim: Shahida means to be present; an implied sense is whoever is in his town during the month, sane, adult, healthy, and resident must fast. The month is a time adverb, not an object.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r1.anchor: و «شهد» بمعنى حضر، وفيه إضمار أي من شهد منكم المصر في الشهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r2.claim: The general command to fast is qualified by the following exception for illness and travel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r2.anchor: وهو يقال عام فيخصص بقوله: { فمن كان منكم مريضا أو على سفر }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r3.speaker: علي وابن عباس وسويد بن غفلة وعائشة وأبو مجلز وعبيدة السلماني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r3.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, Aisha, Abu Mujliz, and Ubayda say “witnesses” means resident when Ramadan begins: one must complete the fast even if traveling later; only someone already traveling when Ramadan begins may break and make it up.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r3.anchor: فقال علي ابن أبي طالب وابن عباس وسويد بن غفلة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r4.speaker: جمهور الأمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r4.claim: The majority say whoever witnesses Ramadan while resident fasts as long as resident, but may break after traveling; the author calls this correct and says authentic reports support it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r4.anchor: وقال جمهور الأمة: من شهد أول الشهر وآخره فليصم ما دام مقيما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r5.claim: Al-Bukhari's report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet left for Mecca in Ramadan fasting, broke his fast at al-Kadid, and the people broke with him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#11/r5.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال أنبأنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r1.claim: Al-Kadid lies between ʿUsfan and Qudayd.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r2.claim: Ali’s ruling may concern recommended travel, such as visiting virtuous people, or permissible travel for surplus livelihood.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r2.anchor: قد يحتمل أن يحمل قول علي رضي الله عنه ومن وافقه على السفر المندوب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r3.claim: For obligatory travel, the traveler need not fast; breaking the fast is preferable for piety, even if he started Ramadan at home, and Qurtubi expects no disagreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r3.anchor: ولا يجب عليه الإمساك بل الفطر فيه أفضل للتقوى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r4.claim: Hanafis require fasting from anyone who enters Ramadan legally competent, neither insane nor unconscious.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: من شهد الشهر بشروط التكليف غير مجنون ولا مغمى عليه فليصمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r5.claim: A person insane throughout Ramadan owes no make-up because he did not witness the month in a state that obligates fasting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r5.anchor: ومن دخل عليه رمضان وهو مجنون وتمادى به طول الشهر فلا قضاء عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r6.claim: Someone insane at the beginning and end of Ramadan makes up the days of insanity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r6.anchor: ومن جن أول الشهر وآخره فإنه يقضي أيام جنونه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r7.claim: On this interpretation, al-shahr is the explicit direct object of shahida.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r7.anchor: ونصب الشهر على هذا التأويل هو على المفعول الصريح ب «شهد»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r8.claim: The obligation of fasting presupposes Islam, puberty, and knowledge that the month has begun.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r8.anchor: قد تقرر أن فرض الصوم مستحق بالإسلام والبلوغ والعلم بالشهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r9.claim: A convert or newly pubescent child before dawn must fast that day; if this occurs after dawn, abstention is recommended, with no make-up for earlier days or that day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r9.anchor: وإن كان بعد الفجر استحب لهما الإمساك، وليس عليهما قضاء الماضي من الشهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r10.speaker: مالك والجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r10.claim: A convert owes no make-up for days before conversion because he witnessed Ramadan only after becoming Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r10.anchor: فقال الإمام مالك والجمهور: ليس عليه قضاء ما مضى لأنه إنما شهد الشهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r11.claim: Malik nevertheless considers it preferable for a convert to make up the day on which he converted.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r11.anchor: قال مالك: وأحب إلي أن يقضي اليوم الذي أسلم فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r12.speaker: عطاء والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r12.claim: Ata and al-Hasan say the convert fasts the remainder of Ramadan and makes up the days already passed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r12.anchor: وقال عطاء والحسن: يصوم ما بقي ويقضي ما مضى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r13.speaker: عبد الملك بن الماجشون وأحمد وإسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r13.claim: Ibn al-Majishun, Ahmad, and Ishaq require abstaining for the rest of the conversion day and making that day up.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r13.anchor: وقال عبد الملك بن الماجشون: يكف عن الأكل في ذلك اليوم ويقضيه. وقال أحمد وإسحق مثله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r14.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r14.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says a convert owes neither the past days of Ramadan nor the day of conversion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r14.anchor: وقال ابن المنذر: ليس عليه أن يقضي ما مضى من الشهر ولا ذلك اليوم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r15.speaker: الباجي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r15.claim: Al-Baji says scholars who hold that non-Muslims are addressed by Islamic law require a convert to abstain for the rest of the day; Ibn Nafi transmits this from Malik, as does Abu al-Qasim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r15.anchor: وقال الباجي: من قال من أصحابنا أن الكفار مخاطبون بشرائع الإسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r16.speaker: أشهب وعبد الملك بن الماجشون وابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r16.claim: Those who hold non-Muslims are not addressed by Islamic law do not require abstention for the remainder of the day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r16.anchor: ومن قال من أصحابنا ليسوا مخاطبين قال: لا يلزمه الإمساك في بقية يومه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r17.claim: Qurtubi prefers the view that a convert need not abstain or make up the day: “O believers” addresses believers, not non-Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r17.anchor: قلت: وهو الصحيح لقوله تعالى: { يأيها الذين آمنوا } فخاطب المؤمنين دون غيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r18.speaker: جماعة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r18.claim: A group reads al-yusr with a ḍamma on the sīn; it is a dialectal variant, as with al-ʿusr.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#12/r18.anchor: قراءة جماعة «اليسر» بضم السين لغتان، وكذلك «العسر».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r1.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r1.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak take ease to mean breaking the fast while traveling and hardship to mean fasting while traveling.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد والضحاك: «اليسر» الفطر في السفر، و «العسر» الصوم في السفر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r2.claim: Qurtubi says the wording is general and covers all matters of religion, citing the denial of hardship in religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r2.anchor: والوجه عموم اللفظ في جميع أمور الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r3.claim: A prophetic report says that God’s religion is easy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r3.anchor:
وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" دين الله يسر "

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r4.claim: The Prophet instructs people to make things easy and not difficult.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r4.anchor:
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" يسروا ولا تعسروا "

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r5.claim: Yusr derives from ease; al-yasār also means wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r5.anchor: واليسر من السهولة، ومنه اليسار للغنى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r6.claim: The left hand is named either optimistically or because it helps make tasks easier alongside the right hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r6.anchor: وسميت اليد اليسرى تفاؤلا، أو لأنه يسهل له الأمر بمعاونتها لليمنى قولان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r7.claim: The denial of hardship restates the affirmation of ease for emphasis.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r7.anchor: وقوله: { ولا يريد بكم العسر } وهو بمعنى قوله: { يريد الله بكم اليسر }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r8.speaker: أهل السنة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r8.claim: Ahl al-Sunna infer that God has an eternal, pre-eternal will additional to His essence, along with eternal attributes of knowledge, power, life, hearing, sight, and speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r8.anchor: هذا مذهب أهل السنة كما أنه عالم بعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r9.speaker: الفلاسفة والشيعة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r9.claim: Philosophers and Shiʿites deny these attributes; Qurtubi repudiates their position.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r9.anchor: وذهب الفلاسفة والشيعة إلى نفيها تعالى الله عن قول الزائغين وإبطال المبطلين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r10.claim: Qurtubi argues that will is perfection: an agent can choose whether to specify an outcome, while lacking will would be a deficiency.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r10.anchor: فإن من كانت له الصفات الإرادية فله أن يخصص الشيء وله ألا يخصصه فالعقل السليم يقضي بأن ذلك كمال له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r11.claim: God explicitly describes Himself as willing in several verses, including “Doer of what He wills.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r11.anchor: وقد وصف نفسه جل جلاله وتقدست أسماؤه بأنه مريد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r12.claim: The contingent, ordered world must have been specified for existence by an agent who wills, knows, and can create it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r12.anchor: هذا العالم على غاية من الحكمة والإتقان والانتظام والإحكام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r13.claim: Qurtubi argues that willing and power entail life, which entails hearing, sight, and speech; their opposites would imply impossible defects in God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#13/r13.anchor: وإذ ثبت كونه قادرا مريدا وجب أن يكون حيا إذ الحياة شرط هذه الصفات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r1.claim: One interpretation is completing the make-up days missed because of illness or travel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r1.anchor: أحدهما: إكمال عدة الأداء لمن أفطر في سفره أو مرضه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r2.claim: A second interpretation is completing the lunar month, whether it has twenty-nine or thirty days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r2.anchor: الثاني: عدة الهلال سواء كانت تسعا وعشرين أو ثلاثين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r3.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet said a lunar month can consist of twenty-nine days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r3.anchor:
قال جابر بن عبد الله قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إن الشهر يكون تسعا وعشرين "

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r4.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r4.claim: The majority understand the report that the two festival months do not fall short as referring to reward and expiation: either month may have twenty-nine or thirty days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r4.anchor: وتأوله جمهور العلماء على معنى أنهما لا ينقصان في الأجر وتكفير الخطايا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r5.claim: A Shawwal crescent seen in daylight on Ramadan’s thirtieth day belongs to the coming night, so it does not end that day’s fast.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r5.anchor: ولا اعتبار برؤية هلال شوال يوم الثلاثين من رمضان نهارا بل هو لليلة التي تأتي، هذا هو الصحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r6.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r6.claim: A letter attributed to Umar says crescents vary in apparent size and a daytime sighting does not permit breaking the fast unless two witnesses saw it the previous evening.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r6.anchor: إن الأهلة بعضها أكبر من بعض، فإذا رأيتم الهلال نهارا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r7.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وابن عمر وأنس بن مالك ومالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة ومحمد بن الحسن والليث والأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r7.claim: Abu Umar attributes the same position to Ali, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Umar, Anas, and the listed jurists: the daytime crescent is for the next night.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r7.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب مثل ما ذكره عبد الرزاق أيضا، وهو قول ابن مسعود وابن عمر وأنس بن مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r8.speaker: سفيان الثوري وأبو يوسف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r8.claim: Al-Thawri and Abu Yusuf distinguish by noon: a crescent before noon belongs to the previous night, while one after noon belongs to the next.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r8.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري وأبو يوسف: إن رؤي بعد الزوال فهو لليلة التي تأتي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r9.speaker: عمر وعلي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r9.claim: A report from Umar, with a similar report from Ali, says to break the fast if the crescent appears before noon on the thirtieth, but not if it appears after noon.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r9.anchor: إذا رأيتم الهلال نهارا قبل أن تزول الشمس لتمام ثلاثين فأفطروا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r10.claim: Qurtubi says no sound isnad is established from Ali on this question.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r10.anchor: ولا يصح في هذه المسألة شيء من جهة الإسناد عن علي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r11.speaker: سليمان بن ربيعة وعبد الملك بن حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r11.claim: Sulayman ibn Rabiʿa and Ibn Habib adopt al-Thawri’s timing rule; Ibn Habib issued fatwas for it in Cordoba.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r11.anchor: وروي عن سليمان بن ربيعة مثل قول الثوري، وإليه ذهب عبد الملك بن حبيب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r12.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r12.claim: Reports differ about Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz’s position on the daylight crescent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r12.anchor: واختلف عن عمر بن عبد العزيز في هذه المسألة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r13.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r13.claim: Abu Umar says the connected report from Umar supports Malik’s and the majority’s position; the report supporting al-Thawri is disconnected, and the connected report takes precedence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r13.anchor: قال أبو عمر: والحديث عن عمر بمعنى ما ذهب إليه مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة متصل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r14.speaker: أصحاب قول الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r14.claim: Proponents of al-Thawri’s view argue that al-Aʿmash’s report is general while Ibrahim’s report specifies the timing, so the specific report should govern.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r14.anchor: احتج من ذهب مذهب الثوري بأن قال: حديث الأعمش مجمل لم يخص فيه قبل الزوال ولا بعده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r15.speaker: عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r15.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet fasted the thirtieth morning, saw the Shawwal crescent by day, and did not break his fast until evening.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#14/r15.anchor: روته عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: أصبح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صائما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab says a Shawwal crescent seen from after dawn through sunset belongs to the coming night; Qurtubi calls this agreed upon.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r1.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن المسيب يقول: إن رؤي هلال شوال بعد أن طلع الفجر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r2.claim: Qurtubi says the rule that a daytime Shawwal crescent belongs to the coming night is agreed upon.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r3.speaker: رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r3.claim: An unnamed Companion reports that two Bedouins testified they had seen the crescent the previous evening; the Prophet ordered people to break the fast and attend the prayer ground the next morning. Al-Daraqutni grades the isnad hasan and established.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r3.anchor: عن ربعي بن حراش عن رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: اختلف الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r4.speaker: مالك وأصحابه وأبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r4.claim: Abu Umar says Malik and his school do not pray Eid on another day or after noon on Eid day, and this position is also reported from Abu Hanifa.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r4.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لا خلاف عن مالك وأصحابه أنه لا تصلى صلاة العيد في غير يوم العيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r5.speaker: الشافعي والمزني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r5.claim: One position of al-Shafiʿi, chosen by al-Muzani, follows Malik: if the prayer is not done after noon on Eid day, the following day is even less suitable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r5.anchor: واختلف قول الشافعي في هذه المسألة فمرة قال بقول مالك، واختاره المزني

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r6.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r6.claim: Another reported position of al-Shafiʿi permits Eid prayer on the second morning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r6.anchor: وعن الشافعي رواية أخرى أنها تصلى في اليوم الثاني ضحى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r7.speaker: البويطي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r7.claim: Al-Buwayti says Eid prayer should be held on the second day only if a hadith establishes that practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r7.anchor: وقال البويطي: لا تصلي إلا أن يثبت في ذلك حديث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r8.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r8.claim: Abu Umar argues that making up Eid prayer after its time would make it resemble an obligatory prayer, whereas the scholars agree other supererogatory prayers are not made up.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r8.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لو قضيت صلاة العيد بعد خروج وقتها لأشبهت الفرائض، وقد أجمعوا في سائر السنن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r9.speaker: الثوري والأوزاعي وأحمد بن حنبل وأبو يوسف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r9.claim: Al-Thawri, al-Awzaʿi, Ahmad, and Abu Yusuf permit going out for Eid prayer the next day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r9.anchor: وقال الثوري والأوزاعي وأحمد بن حنبل: يخرجون من الغد، وقاله أبو يوسف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r10.speaker: الحسن بن صالح بن حي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r10.claim: Hasan ibn Salih permits a next-day prayer for Eid al-Adha but not Eid al-Fitr.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن بن صالح بن حي: لا يخرجون في الفطر ويخرجون في الأضحى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r11.speaker: أبو يوسف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r11.claim: Abu Yusuf says the Eid al-Adha prayer may be held for people on the third day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r11.anchor: قال أبو يوسف: وأما في الأضحى فيصليها بهم في اليوم الثالث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r12.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r12.claim: Abu Umar explains that Adha has several festival days, while Fitr has only one; if missed, its non-obligatory prayer is not made up.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r12.anchor: لأن الأضحى أيام عيد وهي صلاة عيد، وليس الفطر يوم عيد إلا يوم واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r13.speaker: الليث بن سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r13.claim: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd permits going out the next day for both Fitr and Adha prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r13.anchor: وقال الليث بن سعد: يخرجون في الفطر والأضحى من الغد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r14.claim: Qurtubi prefers holding Eid prayer the next day because of the established Sunnah, since the Lawgiver may make an exception allowing a Sunnah to be performed after its time.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#15/r14.anchor: قلت: والقول بالخروج إن شاء الله أصح للسنة الثابتة في ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r1.claim: The Prophet says that anyone who missed the two dawn Sunnah rakʿahs may pray them after sunrise; Abu Muhammad authenticates the report, and al-Tirmidhi mentions scholars who act on it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r1.anchor: من لم يصل ركعتي الفجر فليصلهما بعد ما تطلع الشمس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r2.speaker: الترمذي والثوري والشافعي وأحمد وإسحق وابن المبارك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi says some scholars act on this report, naming al-Thawri, al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Ibn al-Mubarak; Umar is also reported to have done so.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r2.anchor: قال الترمذي: والعمل على هذا عند بعض أهل العلم، وبه يقول سفيان الثوري والشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r3.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r3.claim: Maliki scholars say someone who prayed dawn because time was short may pray the omitted dawn Sunnah after sunrise if he wishes; another view forbids it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r3.anchor: قال علماؤنا: من ضاق عليه الوقت وصلى الصبح وترك ركعتي الفجر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r4.speaker: الشيخ أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r4.claim: Abu Bakr says treating those two rakʿahs as make-up follows the school’s principle, though calling them qada is loose usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو بكر: وهذا الجاري على أصل المذهب، وذكر القضاء تجوز

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r5.claim: Qurtubi says next-day Fitr prayer may likewise be allowed after its time, especially because it occurs only once yearly and the Sunnah establishes it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r5.anchor: قلت: ولا يبعد أن يكون حكم صلاة الفطر في اليوم الثاني على هذا الأصل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r6.speaker: أبو عمير بن أنس عن عمومة له
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r6.claim: Anas’s uncles report that people who saw the crescent came to the Prophet; he ordered them to break the fast once the day had advanced and go to the Eid prayer the next day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r6.anchor: عن أبي عمير بن أنس عن عمومة له: أن قوما رأوا الهلال فأتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأمرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r7.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو والحسن وقتادة والأعرج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r7.claim: Abu Bakr’s transmission from ʿAsim, one report from Abu ʿAmr, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Aʿraj read tukammilū with a doubled mīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو في بعض ما روي عنه والحسن وقتادة والأعرج { ولتكملوا العدة } بالتشديد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r8.speaker: الباقون والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r8.claim: The remaining readers use the un-doubled form; al-Kisaʾi prefers it, comparing it with “Today I completed your religion.”

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r9.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r9.claim: Al-Nahhas says the two forms are dialects with the same meaning, as in the paired forms in 86:17.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r9.anchor: قال النحاس: وهما لغتان بمعنى واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r10.claim: The phrase is not read with a vowelless lām; the Basran analysis supplies an understood أن after the purpose lām.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r11.speaker: البصريون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r11.claim: Basran grammarians parse the lām as introducing a purpose clause, estimated as “He wills that you complete”; they disallow deleting أن and its vowel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r11.anchor: ولا يجوز حذف أن والكسرة هذا قول البصريين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r12.speaker: كثير أبو صخر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r12.claim: The poetic phrase “I wish to forget her memory” is cited to show the construction لِأَنْسى, with أن after the lām.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r12.anchor: قول كثير أبو صخر: أريد لأنسى ذكرها أي لأن أنسى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r13.claim: Qurtubi says this lām can introduce an object, as in “I struck for Zayd,” so the sense is that God intends completion of the number.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r13.anchor: وهذه اللام هي الداخلة على المفعول كالتي في قولك: ضربت لزيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r14.speaker: الكوفيون والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r14.claim: The Kufans, as al-Farraʾ relates, attach the lām to an implicit later verb: God granted this concession so that people may complete the number; al-Nahhas calls this a good analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#16/r14.anchor: وهذا قول الكوفيين وحكاه النحاس عن الفراء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r1.claim: The construction is compared to 6:75, where showing Abraham the kingdom of heaven and earth was done so he would be among the certain.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r1.anchor: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r2.claim: One grammatical explanation treats the waw as superfluous.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r3.claim: Another explanation makes the lām imperative, with the waw coordinating one sentence to another.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r3.anchor: وقيل: يحتمل أن تكون هذه اللام لام الأمر والواو عاطفة جملة كلام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r4.speaker: أبو إسحق إبراهيم بن السري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq interprets the wording by its meaning: God did this to make matters easy and so people would complete the number.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحق إبراهيم بن السري: هو محمول على المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r5.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r5.claim: Sibawayh’s cited couplet supplies an implicitly repeated phrase, illustrating the ellipsis proposed in this construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r5.anchor: ومشجج أما سواء قذاله فبدا وغيب ساره المعزاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r6.speaker: جمهور أهل التأويل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r6.claim: The majority of exegetes take the clause as urging magnification of God at the end of Ramadan.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولتكبروا الله } عطف عليه، ومعناه الحض على التكبير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وعروة وأبو سلمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi reports that Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwa, and Abu Salama would say takbir and praise God on the night of Fitr, by analogy with the night of Adha.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r7.anchor: روي عن سعيد ابن المسيب وعروة وأبي سلمة أنهم كانوا يكبرون ليلة الفطر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muslims must say takbir upon seeing the Shawwal crescent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#17/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: حق على المسلمين إذا رأوا هلال شوال أن يكبروا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r1.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas places takbir from sighting the crescent through the sermon, pausing when the imam comes out and joining his takbir.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r1.anchor: وروي عنه: يكبر المرء من رؤية الهلال إلى انقضاء الخطبة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r2.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r2.claim: Some say takbir begins with sighting the crescent and ends when the imam comes out for prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: يكبر من رؤية الهلال إلى خروج الإمام للصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r3.speaker: سفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r3.claim: Sufyan says the takbir is said on the day of Fitr.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r3.anchor: وقال سفيان: هو التكبير يوم الفطر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم ومالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says takbir runs from setting out for the prayer ground until prayer ends; Malik’s school places it from leaving home until the imam comes out.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r4.anchor: زيد بن أسلم: يكبرون إذا خرجوا إلى المصلى فإذا انقضت الصلاة انقضى العيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r5.speaker: ابن القاسم وعلي بن زياد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r5.claim: Malik’s transmitters say one leaving before sunrise does not say takbir en route or while waiting until sunrise; one leaving later says it en route and while waiting for the imam.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r5.anchor: وروى ابن القاسم وعلي بن زياد: أنه إن خرج قبل طلوع الشمس فلا يكبر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r6.speaker: مالك والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r6.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi apply the same takbir practice to Fitr and Adha.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r6.anchor: والفطر والأضحى في ذلك سواء عند مالك، وبه قال الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa requires takbir for Adha but not Fitr.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: يكبر في الأضحى ولا يكبر في الفطر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r8.claim: Qurtubi invokes the command to magnify God and the annual Fitr celebration in support of takbir at Fitr.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r8.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى: { ولتكبروا الله } ولأن هذا يوم عيد لا يتكرر في العام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r9.claim: Al-Sulami reports that people were more emphatic about takbir at Fitr than at Adha.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r9.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال: كانوا في التكبير في الفطر أشد منهم في الأضحى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r10.claim: A report from Ibn Umar says the Prophet said takbir from leaving home until reaching the prayer ground on Fitr.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r10.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكبر يوم الفطر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r11.claim: Ibn Umar himself would loudly say takbir on Fitr and Adha while going out, continuing until the imam arrived.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r11.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر: أنه كان إذا غدا يوم الأضحى ويوم الفطر يجهر بالتكبير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r12.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم وابن المنذر والأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r12.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says most early Muslims and scholars held takbir at Fitr; al-Awzaʿi transmitted this from Ilyas.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r12.anchor: وأكثر أهل العلم على التكبير في عيد الفطر من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r13.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r13.claim: Al-Shafiʿi favors communal and individual takbir from the Shawwal crescent until setting out and when the imam comes to pray, and likewise on Adha night for non-pilgrims.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r13.anchor: وكان الشافعي يقول إذا رأى هلال شوال: أحببت أن يكبر الناس جماعة وفرادى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r14.speaker: مالك وجماعة من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r14.claim: Malik and a group of scholars use three repetitions of “Allahu akbar”; this wording is also reported from Jabir ibn Abd Allah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r14.anchor: ولفظ التكبير عند مالك وجماعة من العلماء: الله أكبر الله أكبر الله أكبر، ثلاثا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r15.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r15.claim: Some scholars mix takbir with declarations of divine oneness and glorification, while others use the longer formula “Allahu akbar kabira …”.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r15.anchor: ومن العلماء من يكبر ويهلل ويسبح أثناء التكبير. ومنهم من يقول: الله أكبر كبيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r16.speaker: ابن المبارك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r16.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak’s Fitr formula includes takbir, the testimony of oneness, praise, and “God is greatest for guiding us.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r16.anchor: وكان ابن المبارك يقول إذا خرج من يوم الفطر: الله أكبر الله أكبر، لا إله إلا الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r17.speaker: ابن المنذر وأحمد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r17.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says Malik set no fixed formula or limit; Ahmad calls the practice broad.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r17.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وكان مالك لا يحد فيه حدا. وقال أحمد: هو واسع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r18.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r18.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says his scholars choose unrestricted takbir as the Qurʾan’s apparent sense; Qurtubi inclines to that view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r18.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «واختار علماؤنا التكبير المطلق، وهو ظاهر القرآن وإليه أميل»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r19.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r19.claim: One explanation links the praise to Christians’ error in changing their fast.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r19.anchor: قيل: لما ضل فيه النصارى من تبديل صيامهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r20.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r20.claim: Another explanation contrasts divine guidance with the pagan custom of boasting about ancestors, lineage, and accomplishments.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r20.anchor: وقيل: بدلا عما كانت الجاهلية تفعله من التفاخر بالآباء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r21.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r21.claim: A broader explanation is to magnify God for guiding people to the religious laws.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r21.anchor: وقيل: لتعظموه على ما أرشدكم إليه من الشرائع فهو عام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:185#18/r22.claim: Qurtubi refers readers back to his earlier explanation of “so that you may be grateful.”

QASHANI:2:185/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:185/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:185/r1.claim: Ramadan signifies the soul burning in the light of the Real.

QASHANI:2:185/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:185/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:185/r2.claim: The Quran is comprehensive, undifferentiated knowledge, the Quranic intellect leading to unity and guiding humanity through comprehensiveness.
QASHANI:2:185/r2.anchor: أي: العلم الجامع الإجمالي، المسمى بالعقل القرآني

QASHANI:2:185/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:185/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:185/r3.claim: The clear signs are proofs of union and distinction: detailed knowledge called the discriminative or Furqanic intellect.
QASHANI:2:185/r3.anchor: ودلائل متصلة من الجمع والفرق، أي: العلم التفصيلي

QASHANI:2:185/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:185/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:185/r4.claim: Witnessing the month means reaching the station of witnessing the Essence; fasting means refraining from speech, act, or movement not in God.
QASHANI:2:185/r4.anchor: أي: فليمسك عن قول وفعل وحركة ليس بالحق فيه

QASHANI:2:185/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:185/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:185/r5.claim: The sick have heart diseases caused by psychic veils; travelers are still journeying and must traverse further stations before essential witnessing.
QASHANI:2:185/r5.anchor: أي: مبتلى بأمراض قلبه من الحجب النفسانية المانعة من ذلك الشهود

QASHANI:2:185/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:185/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:185/r6.claim: Ease is arrival at unity and extension through God's power; hardship is forcing deeds through the weak, incapable self.
QASHANI:2:185/r6.anchor: بالوصول إلى مقام التوحيد والامتداد بقدرة الله

QASHANI:2:185/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:185/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:185/r7.claim: Completing the count means completing successive stations, states, and ranks that lead to the goal.
QASHANI:2:185/r7.anchor: ولتتمموا تلك المراتب والأحوال والمقامات الموصلة

QASHANI:2:185/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:185/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:185/r8.claim: Magnifying God means recognizing His greatness for guiding you to unity; gratitude is steadfastness in His command.
QASHANI:2:185/r8.anchor: ولتعظموا الله وتعرفوا عظمته وكبرياءه على هدايته

RAZI-FULL:v5p62/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p62/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p62/r5.claim: On either identification of the numbered days, some abrogation is required; if they were Ramadan, the next verse abrogates the option, though al-Razi flags a problem with treating an immediately connected verse as abrogator.
RAZI-FULL:v5p62/r5.anchor: الآية الثانية ناسخة لحكم هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās a Prophetic rule against shortening prayer on a journey shorter than four mail-stations, from Mecca to ʿAsfān; each station is four farsakhs, totaling sixteen.
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r1.anchor: ما رواه الشافعي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : يا أهل مكة لا تقصروا في أدنى من أربعة برد

RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومالك
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly told ʿAṭāʾ that trips to ʿArafa or Mar al-Ẓahrān do not qualify, but journeys to Jeddah, ʿAsfān, or Ṭāʾif do; Mālik says Mecca to Jeddah or ʿAsfān is four stations.
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن الشافعي أيضا أن عطاء قال لابن عباس : أقصر إلى عرفة ؟ فقال : لا

RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues that the verse commands fasting; a three-day travel concession is established by consensus, while shorter journeys are disputed, so the fasting rule remains for them.
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r3.anchor: يقتضي وجوب الصوم عدلنا عنه في ثلاثة أيام بسبب الإجماع

RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r4.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r4.claim: A Prophetic report permits wiping over footwear for one day and night to a resident and three days and nights to a traveler; Abū Ḥanīfa infers a three-day minimum travel period from the ruling’s cause-and-effect relation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r4.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( يمسح المقيم يوما وليلة والمسافر ثلاثة أيام ولياليهن )

RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r5.claim: Against prioritizing caution in worship, al-Razi prefers the legal aim of travel relief, supported by the Prophet’s description of the concession as God’s charity to be accepted; that specific evidence outweighs general caution.
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r5.anchor: رجحنا جانبنا بأن التخفيف في رخص السفر مطلوب الشرع ، بدليل قوله عليه السلام : ( هذه صدقة تصدق الله بها عليكم فاقتبلوا منه صدقته )

RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r6.claim: The wiping report does not establish a three-day minimum for travel: stating a resident wipes one day does not preclude residence after an hour, and the traveler’s three-day allowance likewise does not exclude shorter travel.
RAZI-FULL:v5p64#2/r6.anchor: وهذا لا يدل على أنه لا تحصل الإقامة في أقل من يوم وليلة

RAZI-FULL:v5p66/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p66/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك وعثمان بن أبي أوفى والشافعي وأبو حنيفة ومالك والثوري وأبو يوسف ومحمد
RAZI-FULL:v5p66/r4.claim: Anas, Uthman ibn Abi Awfa, al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Thawri, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad hold that fasting while travelling is better.
RAZI-FULL:v5p66/r4.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك وعثمان بن أبي أوفى الصوم أفضل وهو مذهب الشافعي وأبي حنيفة ومالك والثوري وأبي يوسف ومحمد

RAZI-FULL:v5p67/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p67/r1.speaker: فرقة ثالثة
RAZI-FULL:v5p67/r1.claim: The third group's view is supported by God's statement that He intends ease, so a traveller should fast if fasting is easier and break the fast if that is easier.
RAZI-FULL:v5p67/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر

RAZI-FULL:v5p69/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p69/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p69/r4.claim: Making the witnessing-Ramadan verse an abrogator would contradict the adjacent declaration that God intends ease, since this reading changes restrictive obligation to an option and reverses ease and hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v5p69/r4.anchor: ولو كانت الآية ناسخة لهذا لما كان

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r1.claim: Shahr derives from visibility or fame: the month is named for its clear appearance, and people need to know it to time debts, rites, fasting, and pilgrimage.

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r2.claim: Some say the month is named after the crescent because it is conspicuous and clear.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم سمي الشهر شهرا باسم الهلال

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r3.claim: Mujahid says Ramadan is one of God's names, so 'the month of Ramadan' means the month of God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد : إنه اسم الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says not to say Ramadan came or went, but to say the month of Ramadan, because Ramadan is one of God's names; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r4.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r5.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r5.claim: Al-Khalil derives Ramadan from ramda', a pre-autumn rain that washes dust from the earth; by analogy, the month washes the community's bodies of sins and purifies hearts.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r5.anchor: ما نقل عن الخليل أنه من الرمضاء بسكون الميم

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r6.claim: Another derivation is ramad, the heat of sun-scorched stones: the name evokes burning hunger and severe hardship; it was also called tabi' because it followed and distressed people.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r6.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من الرمض وهو حر الحجارة

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r7.claim: A further explanation says the transferred month names were given from the seasons in which they fell, and Ramadan coincided with days of intense heat.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r7.anchor: لما نقلوا أسماء الشهور عن اللغة القديمة سموها بالأزمنة

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r8.claim: A report from the Prophet explains Ramadan as the month that burns God's servants' sins; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r8.anchor: وقد روى عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r9.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r9.claim: Al-Azhari derives Ramadan from the verb for tempering a blade between stones until thin; weapons were tempered during this month for use.

RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r10.claim: If Ramadan is God's name, the month shares it because sins disappear in God's mercy, or because they burn through the month's blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71/r10.anchor: فالمعنى أن الذنوب تتلاشى في جنب رحمة الله

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads shahr in the nominative as a substitute for al-siyam: fasting prescribed for you means the month of Ramadan.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r1.anchor: وهو قول الكسائي أنه ارتفع على البدل من الصيام

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r2.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra and al-Akhfash take the nominative as predicate of an omitted subject, replacing 'days': the counted days are the month of Ramadan.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r2.anchor: وهو قول الفراء والأخفش أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r3.claim: Abu Ali allows shahr in the nominative as a subject with an omitted predicate: among the fasts prescribed is the fast of Ramadan.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي : إن شئت جعلته مبتدأ محذوف الخبر

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r4.claim: Some grammarians allow shahr as a subject whose predicate is the relative clause, 'in which the Quran was revealed.'
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : يجوز أن يكون بمبتدأ وخبره

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r5.claim: Abu Ali prefers taking the relative clause as an adjective of shahr, which makes the command to fast the month explicit; using it as the predicate would only state that Quran was revealed then.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي : والأشبه أن يكون

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r6.claim: In the accusative, one analysis supplies an imperative: 'Fast the month of Ramadan.'

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r7.claim: A second accusative analysis makes shahr a substitute for the counted days.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r7.anchor: وثانيها : على الإبدال من أيام معدودات

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf proposes that the accusative shahr is the object of 'that you fast.'

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r9.claim: An objection to al-Kashshaf's parsing is that it separates the subject from its predicate with the long clause 'in which Quran was revealed ... is better,' an impermissible break between what functions as one unit.

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r10.claim: God singled Ramadan out for fasting because He singled it out for the greatest sign of lordship, the Quran's revelation; fasting is a fitting great sign of servanthood.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r10.anchor: لما خص هذا الشهر بهذه العبادة بين العلة لهذا التخصيص

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r11.claim: Razi says fasting is among the strongest means of removing bodily attachments that veil divine light from human spirits; people of spiritual unveiling reach that light only through fasting.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r11.anchor: الصوم أقوى الأسباب في إزالة العلائق البشرية

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r12.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that if satans did not hover around human hearts, people would see the kingdom of the heavens; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r12.anchor: عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( لولا أن الشياطين يحومون

RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r13.claim: The shared spiritual character of fasting and Quran revelation explains why the month that receives revelation is specifically assigned fasting.
RAZI-FULL:v5p71#2/r13.anchor: فثبت أن بين الصوم وبين نزول القرآن مناسبة عظيمة

RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet dates Abraham's scrolls to Ramadan's first night, the Torah to its sixth, the Gospel to its thirteenth, and the Quran to its twenty-fourth; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r2.claim: Razi raises the problem that the Quran came to Muhammad piecemeal over twenty-three years, with portions revealed in months other than Ramadan, so the verse needs explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r2.anchor: أن القرآن ما نزل على محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام دفعة

RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r3.claim: The first answer is that the entire Quran descended on Laylat al-Qadr to the lowest heaven, then came down to earth gradually; this arrangement may have benefited the angels, the Prophet, or Gabriel.
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r3.anchor: أن القرآن أنزل في ليلة القدر جملة إلى سماء الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r4.claim: Razi refers to his explanation of why revelation was gradual at Quran 25:32, where disbelievers ask why it was not sent all at once.
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r4.anchor: شرحناها في سورة الفرقان في تفسير قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq's second answer is that revelation began on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan; beginnings of religions and states mark history because they are noble and occur at known, fixed times.

RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r6.claim: Razi prefers the first answer because it needs no figurative interpretation; Ibn Ishaq's answer requires taking 'the Quran' to mean only some of its parts.
RAZI-FULL:v5p72/r6.anchor: واعلم أن الجواب الأول لا يحتاج فيه إلى تحمل شيء من المجاز

RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r1.claim: Ibn Umar infers from this verse and Quran 97:1 that Laylat al-Qadr must fall in Ramadan: revelation on that night is therefore revelation in Ramadan, just as a month can be clarified by specifying its day.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r1.anchor: روي أن ابن عمر استدل بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r2.claim: One account is that the entire Quran descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then was sent to Muhammad gradually through the end of his life.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r2.anchor: إن الله تعالى أنزل كل القرآن من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r3.claim: Another account is that each year portions needed by Muhammad and his community were sent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, then revealed to the Prophet as needed.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r3.anchor: كان ينزل من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا من القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r4.claim: Razi says both accounts are possible, since 'Ramadan' may denote a particular month or the kind of month; he therefore suspends judgment.

RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r5.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة والحسين بن الفضل
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r5.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna, a view chosen by al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, interprets the phrase as saying that the Quran was revealed concerning Ramadan's virtue.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r5.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة : أنزل فيه القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari interprets 'in Ramadan' as referring to Quranic revelation about the obligation to fast it, as in saying that revelation 'in' zakat concerns its obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : أنزل في إيجاب صومه على الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r1.claim: Quran is the name for God's speech contained between the two covers.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r1.anchor: القرآن اسم لما بين الدفتين من كلام الله

RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r2.claim: Al-Shafi'i says Quran is a proper, unhamzated name for God's Book, not derived from qara'a, like Torah and Gospel; qira'ah is hamzated.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن عبد الله بن الحكم أن الشافعي رضي الله عنه كان يقول

RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r3.speaker: القائلون بالاشتقاق من قرن
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r3.claim: Some who derive the unhamzated form connect it with qarn, joining: the Quran joins its suras, verses, and letters, its rulings and wisdom, or evidences of its divine origin, including eloquence, unique style, unseen reports, and abundant knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r3.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من قرنت الشيء بالشيء

RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra suggests the name comes from qarā'in, indicators, because the Quran's verses corroborate one another, as Quran 4:82 says a non-divine book would contain many inconsistencies.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r4.anchor: قال الفراء : أظن أن القرآن سمي من القرائن

RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r5.speaker: القائلون بالهمز
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r5.claim: Those who hamz the name derive it from qara'a, recitation, a verbal noun; an anonymous poetic line uses قرآنا to mean recitation, and the recited object can take its verbal noun as a name.

RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r6.claim: Razi cites Quran 17:78's wording as an example in his account of the Quran's name.

RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج وأبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Abu Ubayda derive Quran from qar', gathering, because it collects and joins the suras.
RAZI-FULL:v5p73#2/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج وأبو عبيدة : إنه مأخوذ من القرء وهو الجمع

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r1.claim: Razi glosses Amr's line: taqra' means she has not gathered a fetus in her womb, illustrating qar' as gathering.
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r1.anchor: أي لم تجمع في رحمها ولدا

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r2.speaker: قطرب
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r2.claim: Qutrub says Quran is what the reciter casts from his mouth, drawing on an Arab expression about a camel that has not expelled its afterbirth; the related term also names menstruation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r2.anchor: قول قطرب وهو أنه سمي قرآنا

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r3.speaker: قطرب
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r3.claim: Qutrub supports his derivation with the saying 'the camel has never expelled a fetus membrane': just as the animal casts something out, the reciter casts the Quran from his mouth.
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r3.anchor: قول قطرب وهو أنه سمي قرآنا ، لأن القارىء يكتبه ، وعند القراءة كأنه يلقيه من فيه أخذا من قول العرب : ما قرأت الناقة سلى قط

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r4.claim: Razi distinguishes tanzil as gradual descent from inzal as descent all at once, citing Quran 2:23 and 3:3; this supports taking the verse's inzal as the Quran's descent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, which he prefers over other explanations.
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r4.anchor: التنزيل مختص بالنزول على سبيل التدريج

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r5.claim: Razi refers back to Quran 2:2, where the Quran is guidance for the God-fearing, to reconcile that description with calling it guidance for all people here.
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r5.anchor: بينا تفسير الهدى في قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r6.claim: The accusatives 'guidance for people' and 'clear proofs' are circumstantial: God sent the Quran down as guidance to truth and manifest signs that guide to truth and distinguish truth from falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r6.anchor: نصب على الحال ، أي أنزل وهو هداية

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r7.claim: To explain the apparent repetition, Razi says the verse first names guidance generally, then singles out its clearest and best form: manifest guidance that distinguishes truth from falsehood, as emphasis.
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r7.anchor: هذا من باب ما يذكر الجنس ويعطف نوعه عليه

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r8.claim: A second explanation is that the Quran is guidance itself and also contains guidance from earlier books, the Torah and Gospel, which were themselves guidance and criterion; Razi cites 3:3-4, 2:53, and 21:48.

RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p74/r9.claim: A third explanation removes repetition by assigning the first guidance to fundamentals of religion and the later guidance to derivative rulings.

RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r1.speaker: الأخفش والمازني
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Mazini call the fa in 'whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it' extra, seeing no coordinating or conditional role for it.

RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r2.claim: Razi says the fa is conditional: because Ramadan has special virtue, it appropriately receives a special act of worship, making the prior account of its virtue relevant.
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r2.anchor: وأقول : يمكن أن يقال الفاء ههنا للجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r3.claim: Razi says the fa in Quran 62:8 is not extra either; it marks the consequence that those who flee death have death brought near, showing caution cannot avert fate.
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r3.anchor: الفاء فيه غير زائدة وأيضا بل هذا من باب مقابلة الضد بالضد

RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r4.claim: Shahida means to be present; shuhud means presence.

RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r5.claim: On the first analysis, the object of shahida is omitted, meaning the town or home; al-shahr is a temporal adverb and the pronoun in falyasumhu refers to it, so the sense is whoever is present and not travelling.
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r5.anchor: أن مفعول شهد محذوف لأن المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r6.claim: On the second analysis, al-shahr itself is the object: whoever apprehends the month with knowledge should fast it, as in saying one witnessed someone's era.

RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r7.claim: Razi prefers the second analysis by the legal-theory principle that when ellipsis and specification conflict, specification is preferable; the first requires both an omitted object and exclusions, while the second needs only exclusions for children, the insane, and the ill.
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r7.anchor: متى وقع التعارض بين التخصيص والإضمار فالتخصيص أولى

RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r8.speaker: الواحدي وصاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r8.claim: Despite Razi's preference for the second parse, most leading scholars, including al-Wahidi and al-Kashshaf, adopt the first analysis with an omitted object.
RAZI-FULL:v5p75/r8.anchor: كالواحدي وصاحب ( الكشاف ) ذهبوا إلى الأول

RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r1.claim: The definite article in “the month” refers back to the already identified Ramadan; likewise, the witnesses in 24:13 are the four previously specified witnesses.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r1.anchor: الألف واللام في قوله : { فمن شهد منكم الشهر } للمعهود السابق وهو شهر رمضان

RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r2.claim: Taking “the month” as its entire span makes the condition complete only at month’s end, yet would then require fasting the elapsed month; that is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r2.anchor: فالشرط هو شهود الشهر والجزاء هو الأمر بالصوم وما لم يوجد الشرط بتمامه لا يترتب عليه الجزاء والشهر اسم للزمان المخصوص من أوله إلى آخره

RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r3.claim: Resolve the difficulty by taking “the month” in the condition to mean a part of it: seeing Ramadan’s crescent fulfills the condition and entails fasting the whole month, a familiar whole-for-part metaphor.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r3.anchor: وطريقه أن يحمل لفظ الشهر على جزء من أجزاء الشهر في جانب الشرط فيصير تقريره : من شهد جزأ

RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r4.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r4.claim: Ali explains the verse as requiring whoever witnesses the beginning of the month to fast all of it; al-Razi says this is the only sound reading of the condition.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r4.anchor: واعلم أن المنقول عن علي أن المراد من هذه الآية ، فمن شهد منكم أول الشهر فليصم جميعه

RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r5.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r5.claim: Ali holds that someone who entered Ramadan resident and then traveled must fast the entire month, since witnessing its beginning obligates the whole fast.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r5.anchor: نقل عن علي رضي الله عنه أن من دخل عليه الشهر وهو مقيم ثم سافر ، أن الواجب أن يصوم الكل

RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r6.speaker: سائر المجتهدين
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r6.claim: Other jurists let one who travels after Ramadan begins break the fast: the travel exemption is a specific rule that qualifies the general command to fast the month.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76/r6.anchor: وأما سائر المجتهدين فيقولون : إن قوله تعالى : { فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه }

RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa says a person who regains sanity during Ramadan must make up the elapsed days: witnessing any part obligates the entire month, including missed days that cannot now be fasted.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r1.anchor: وأما الثاني : وهو أن أبا حنيفة زعم أن المجنون إذا أفاق في أثناء الشهر يلزمه قضاء ما مضى ، قال

RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r2.claim: The month’s onset is established either by sighting the crescent or by hearing testimony about it.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r2.anchor: فنقول : إما بالرؤية وإما بالسماع ، أما الرؤية فنقول : إذا رأى إنسان هلال رمضان

RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r3.claim: A person who alone sees Ramadan’s crescent must fast even if the imam rejects his testimony, because the sighting establishes the obligation for that observer; accepted or shared sighting also obligates fasting.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r3.anchor: فإن تفرد بالرؤية ورد الإمام شهادته ، لزمه أن يصوم ، لأن الله تعالى جعل شهود الشهر سببا

RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r4.claim: Two upright witnesses establish both Ramadan fasting and Shawwal breaking; one witness establishes Ramadan, but not Shawwal, to preserve the fast as a precaution.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r4.anchor: إذا شهد عدلان على رؤية الهلال حكم به في الصوم والفطر جميعا ، وإذا شهد عدل واحد على رؤية هلال شوال

RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r5.claim: The distinction between one witness for Ramadan and Shawwal serves the same precaution in both cases: accept Ramadan testimony to keep people fasting, and reject Shawwal testimony so they keep fasting.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r5.anchor: وعلى أنه لا فرق بينهما في الحقيقة ، لأنا إنما قبلنا قول الواحد في هلال رمضان لكي يصوموا ولا يفطروا احتياطا

RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r6.claim: Fasting is abstention from invalidators, knowingly, from true dawn until sunset, with an intention.
RAZI-FULL:v5p76#2/r6.anchor: إن الصوم هو الإمساك عن المفطرات مع العلم بكونه صائما من أول طلوع الفجر الصادق إلى حين غروب الشمس مع النية

RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r1.claim: The required abstention excludes accidental swallowing of a fly or road dust: avoidance is difficult, and the verse promises ease rather than hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r1.anchor: لو طارت ذبابة إلى حلقه ، أو وصل غبار الطريق إلى بطنه لا يبطل صومه ، لأن الاحتراز عنه شاق

RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r2.claim: Food or drink forced into someone’s throat, or poured there while asleep, does not break the fast because coercion is inconsistent with the fasting person’s abstention.
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r2.anchor: لوصب الطعام أو الشراب في حلقه كرها أو حال نوم لا يبطل صومه ، لأن المعتبر هو الإمساك

RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r3.claim: Fast invalidators fall into three classes: entry into the body, things exiting it, and intercourse; intentional vomiting, masturbation, and penetration invalidate the fast.
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r3.anchor: وهي ثلاثة : دخول داخل ، وخروج خارج ، والجماع ، وحد الدخول كل عين وصل من الظاهر إلى الباطن

RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p77/r4.claim: Entry through an open passage into the brain or abdomen invalidates fasting: nasal snuff reaches the brain, while an enema reaches the abdomen.
