TABATABAI:2:185#6/r1.claim: Quranic speech can address events as they occur, as in the verses about a woman's plea, people leaving for trade, and believers fulfilling their covenant.
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r1.anchor: قد سمع الله قول التي تجادلك في زوجها وتشتكي إلى الله والله يسمع تحاوركما

TABATABAI:2:185#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r2.claim: The Quran contains abrogating and abrogated rulings, which cannot coexist at the same time in the sequence of revelation.
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r2.anchor: على أن في القرآن ناسخا ومنسوخا، ولا معنى لاجتماعهما في زمان بحسب النزول

TABATABAI:2:185#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r3.speaker: ربما أجيب
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r3.claim: Another proposed answer takes the Ramadan descent to mean only the first portion revealed, but he rejects it as unsupported and historically implausible.
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r3.anchor: وربما أجيب عن الإشكال أن المراد من نزول القرآن في شهر رمضان أن أول ما نزل منه نزل فيه

TABATABAI:2:185#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r4.claim: The usual account places Muhammad's commissioning on 27 Rajab, more than thirty days before Ramadan; the first verses of al-ʿAlaq and al-Muddaththir also locate revelation at the mission's start.
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r4.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إنما بعث بالقرآن، وقد بعث اليوم السابع والعشرين من شهر رجب

TABATABAI:2:185#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r5.claim: It is highly unlikely that the first revelation waited until Ramadan; neither this verse nor the similar blessed-night and Laylat al-Qadr verses say only the first portion descended then.
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r5.anchor: على أن قوله تعالى { أنزل فيه القرآن } ، غير صريح الدلالة على أن المراد بالقرآن أول نازل منه

TABATABAI:2:185#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r6.claim: The Ramadan and sacred-night verses use إنزال, signaling a single descent, unlike تنزيل for the Quran's gradual revelation.
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r6.anchor: عبرت عن ذلك بلفظ الإنزال الدال على الدفعة دون التنزيل

TABATABAI:2:185#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r7.claim: He applies this single-descent wording to the parallel blessed-night and Laylat al-Qadr statements as well as the Ramadan verse.
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى حم * والكتاب المبين إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة

TABATABAI:2:185#6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r8.claim: He introduces a different account of the Ramadan descent, saying close consideration of Quranic passages points beyond the proposed lowest-heaven and first-portion explanations.
TABATABAI:2:185#6/r8.anchor: والذي يعطيه التدبر في آيات الكتاب أمر آخر

TABATABAI:2:183-185#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#2/r1.claim: The Quran's visible detail is secondary to a prior, undivided book: 11:1 says its verses were first made firm and only then set out in detail.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#2/r1.anchor: فإن هذا الإحكام مقابل التفصيل، والتفصيل هو جعله فصلا فصلا وقطعة قطعة

TABATABAI:2:183-185#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#2/r2.claim: From 7:52–53 and 10:37–39, he infers that detailed form overlays the original book; deniers fail to know its ta'wil, which they will confront at judgment, and the original is that detailed Quran's ta'wil.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#2/r2.anchor: فإن الآيات الشريفة وخاصة ما في سورة يونس ظاهرة الدلالة على أن التفصيل أمر طار على الكتاب

TABATABAI:2:185#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r1.claim: Zukhruf 43:1–4 describes an Arabic, recited form made for human understanding, while the original remains in God's elevated and undivided Umm al-Kitab.
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r1.anchor: إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

TABATABAI:2:185#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r2.claim: The Quran has a hidden location in the guarded book, touched only by the purified; before its descent it remains concealed from outsiders.
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r2.anchor: إنه لقرآن كريم في كتاب مكنون لا يمسه إلا المطهرون تنزيل من رب العالمين

TABATABAI:2:185#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r3.claim: This concealed book is called Umm al-Kitab in Zukhruf and the Preserved Tablet in al-Buruj, preserved from alteration.
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r3.anchor: وهو الذي عبر عنه في آيات الزخرف، بأم الكتاب، وفي سورة البروج، باللوح المحفوظ

TABATABAI:2:185#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r4.claim: Because the gradual revealed Quran includes abrogation and change over time, the Clear Book that is its source is a reality beyond the revealed form, which is like its garment.
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r4.anchor: فالكتاب المبين الذي هو أصل القرآن وحكمه الخالي عن التفصيل أمر وراء هذا المنزل

TABATABAI:2:185#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r5.claim: He describes the revealed Quran as garment, image, and likeness of the underlying reality; this relation permits Quran to name the source itself, as in 85:21.
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r5.anchor: بمنزلة اللباس من المتلبس وبمنزلة المثال من الحقيقة وبمنزلة المثل من الغرض المقصود بالكلام

TABATABAI:2:185#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r6.claim: Thus the Ramadan and sacred-night descent refers to the underlying Reality of the Book descending to Muhammad's heart all at once, while its detailed Quranic form descends gradually during his mission.
TABATABAI:2:185#7/r6.anchor: على إنزال حقيقة الكتاب والكتاب المبين إلى قلب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم دفعة

TABATABAI:2:185#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r1.claim: Verses commanding the Prophet to wait until revelation is complete imply that he knew what was coming while receiving the Quran gradually.
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r1.anchor: فإن الآيات ظاهره في أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان له علم بما سينزل عليه فنهى عن الاستعجال بالقراءة قبل قضاء الوحي

TABATABAI:2:185#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r2.claim: The gradually revealed Quran rests on a transcendent reality beyond ordinary intellect and material thought; God descended that reality to the Prophet and taught him its intended meaning.
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r2.anchor: كون هذا القرآن المنزل على النبي تدريجيا متكئا على حقيقة متعالية عن أن تدركها أبصار العقول العامة أو تناولها أيدي الأفكار المتلوثة

TABATABAI:2:185#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r3.claim: Hadith traditionalists, most theologians, and modern empiricists who deny realities beyond matter reduce Quranic descriptions of revelation and guidance to metaphor, making it mere scattered poetry.
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r3.anchor: أرباب الحديث، والغالب من المتكلمين والحسيون من باحثي هذا العصر لما أنكروا أصالة ما وراء المادة المحسوسة اضطروا إلى حمل هذه الآيات ونظائرها

TABATABAI:2:185#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r4.speaker: بعض الباحثين
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r4.claim: Some researchers place the first mission and revelation, with the command to preach, at night in Ramadan, citing the blessed night and this verse.
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r4.anchor: أن بعثة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان مقارنا لنزول أول ما نزل من القرآن

TABATABAI:2:185#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r5.speaker: بعض الباحثين
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r5.claim: They argue that al-Fatiha, which contains the Quran's central teachings, descended that night, so its portion can stand for the whole Quran; their account places Gabriel's encounter on Ramadan 25 as Muhammad traveled to Khadija.
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r5.anchor: لكن لما نزلت سورة الحمد فيها، وهي تشتمل على جمل معارف القرآن فكان كأن القرآن نزل فيها جميعا

TABATABAI:2:185#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r6.speaker: بعض الباحثين
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r6.claim: The researcher further argues that Quran can name either a part or the whole, and by Quranic convention can also name the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
TABATABAI:2:185#8/r6.anchor: على أن القرآن يطلق على البعض كما يطلق على الكل بل يطلق القرآن على سائر الكتب السماوية أيضا كالتوراة والإنجيل والزبور باصطلاح القرآن

TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r1.speaker: بعض الباحثين
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r1.claim: The researcher says other reports mean the whole Quran descended before the Prophet's mission from the Preserved Tablet to the Inhabited House, where Gabriel recited it to angels for its later piecemeal descent.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r1.anchor: معنى نزول القرآن في شهر رمضان أنه نزل فيه قبل بعثة النبي من اللوح المحفوظ إلى البيت المعمور وأملاه جبرائيل هناك على الملائكة

TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r2.claim: Al-Tabatabai rejects the proposed first-revelation story as imaginative and unsupported by a decisive Quranic verse or established Prophetic report.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r2.anchor: ففيه أولا أن هذا التقول العجيب الذي تقوله في البعثة ونزول القرآن أول ما نزل وأنه صلى عليه وآله وسلم نزل عليه اقرأ باسم ربك

TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r3.claim: He answers the attack on Shi'i hadith collections' late compilation by noting that every Sunni or Shi'i hadith collection was compiled at least two centuries after the Prophet, while historical writing is less reliable still.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r3.anchor: إذ لا شيء من كتب الحديث مما ألفته العامة أو الخاصة إلا وتأليفه متأخر عن عصر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قرنين فصاعدا

TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r4.claim: The first-revelation account conflicts with al-Alaq, whose opening unit already depicts the Prophet praying publicly while opponents try to stop him.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#3/r4.anchor: مشتملة على أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يصلي بمرئى من القوم وأنه كان منهم من ينهاه عن الصلاة

TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r1.claim: Al-Alaq shows the Prophet praying before the first Quranic revelation; the command not to obey his opponent identifies him as already a prophet, though al-Fatiha and the preaching command had not yet come.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r1.anchor: فالآيات كما ترى ظاهرة في أنه كان هناك من ينهي مصليا عن الصلاة، ويذكر أمره في النادي، ولا ينتهي عن فعاله

TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r2.claim: If al-Fatiha had followed al-Alaq immediately as the researcher supposes, its wording and ending at 'Master of Judgment Day' would have been rhetorically better suited to the claimed occasion.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r2.anchor: ولو كان نزولها عقيب نزول سورة العلق بلا فصل عن خطور في قلب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كما ذكره هذا الباحث لكان حق الكلام

TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r3.claim: The seven oft-repeated verses are al-Fatiha; pairing it with the Magnificent Quran exalts it, while its designation as seven verses marks it as part of the Quran, as 39:23 also indicates.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#4/r3.anchor: والمراد بالسبع المثاني سورة الحمد وقد قوبل بها القرآن العظيم وفيه تمام التجليل لشأنها والتعظيم لخطرها لكنها لم تعد قرآنا

TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r1.claim: Al-Hijr's command to proclaim what was commanded shows that the Prophet had paused warning for a time and was then ordered to resume it.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r1.anchor: كان قد كف عن الإنذار مدة ثم أمر به ثانيا بقولة تعالى فاصدع.

TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r2.claim: If al-Muddaththir descended all at once, its 'arise and warn' repeats the later command in al-Hijr; if in portions, its opening appears to belong to the beginning of the messenger's mission.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r2.anchor: فإن كانت السورة نازلة بتمامها دفعة كان حال هذه الآية { قم فأنذر } ، حال قوله تعالى { فاصدع بما تؤمر }

TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r3.claim: The reports about a collective descent do not conflict with the Quran and do not say that descent preceded the Prophet's mission; the researcher added that chronology.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r3.anchor: لا شيء من ظاهر الكتاب يخالف هذه الأخبار على ما عرفت. وأما ثانيا فلأن الأخبار خالية عن كون النزول الجملي قبل البعثة

TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r4.claim: The Preserved Tablet cannot mean the material world: it is in constant motion and change, is not protected from corruption, and is perceptible to everyone, unlike the protected book touched only by the purified.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#5/r4.anchor: فهو عالم الحركات، سيال الذات، متغير الصفات!

TABATABAI:2:185#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r1.claim: The proposed reading that the Quran descended only 'as though' it did cannot fit the verse's wording in ordinary Arabic usage.
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r1.anchor: فإن حاصل توجيهه أن معنى أنزل فيه القرآن كأنما أنزل فيه القرآن،

TABATABAI:2:185#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r2.claim: If al-Fatiha's containing the Quran's teachings could explain the whole Quran's descent, a coherent alternative is that its total meanings descended to the Prophet's heart at once, as explained earlier.
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r2.anchor: جاز أن يقال إن معنى نزول القرآن نزوله جملة واحدة، أي نزول إجمال معارفه على قلب رسول الله

TABATABAI:2:185#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r3.claim: 'People' here means the lower, imitative class whose limited understanding cannot distinguish metaphysical truths or separate truth from falsehood without an explaining guide; the Quran guides them.
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r3.anchor: الناس، وهم الطبقة الدانية من الإنسان الذي سطح فهمهم المتوسط أنزل السطوح

TABATABAI:2:185#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r4.claim: For those mature in knowledge and action, the Quran provides clear signs of divine guidance and a criterion that distinguishes truth and teaches them how to distinguish it; this is the particular side of the contrast with general guidance.
TABATABAI:2:185#9/r4.anchor: فالقرآن بينات وشواهد من الهدى والفرقان في حقهم فهو يهديهم إليه ويميز لهم الحق ويبين لهم كيف يميز

TABATABAI:2:185#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r1.claim: Witnessing the month means reaching it and knowing it while present; one may witness only part of the month or all of it.
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r1.anchor: الشهادة هي الحضور مع تحمل العلم من جهته، وشهادة الشهر إنما هو ببلوغه والعلم به، ويكون بالبعض كما يكون بالكل.

TABATABAI:2:185#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r2.claim: The verse gives no evidence that witnessing means sighting the crescent or that being present means resident rather than traveling; these are contextual associations, absent here.
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r2.anchor: كون المراد بشهود الشهر رؤية هلاله وكون الإنسان بالحضر مقابل السفر فلا دليل عليه إلا من طريق الملازمة في بعض الأوقات

TABATABAI:2:185#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r3.claim: Repeating the sick and traveler rule is not redundant: the two preceding verses prepare the way, while this third verse states the legal ruling.
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r3.anchor: الآيتين السابقتين مع ما تشتملان عليه مسوقتان للتوطئة والتمهيد دون بيان الحكم وأن الحكم هو الذي بين في الآية الثالثة

TABATABAI:2:185#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r4.claim: The exception combines breaking the Ramadan fast to relieve hardship with making up the same number of days to complete the count.
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r4.anchor: كأنه بيان لمجموع حكم الاستثناء وهو الافطار في شهر رمضان لمكان نفي العسر، وصيام عدة من أيام أخر لمكان وجوب اكمال العدة،

TABATABAI:2:185#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r5.claim: The lām in 'so that you complete the count' marks purpose and coordinates with God's willing, since willing includes the sense of an aim.
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r5.anchor: واللام في قوله { لتكملوا العدة } ، للغاية، وهو عطف على قوله يريد، لكونه مشتملا على معنى الغاية

TABATABAI:2:185#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r6.claim: The command to complete the count may explain why the fidya clause is absent here: its ruling is understood from denying hardship and was stated in the preceding verse.
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r6.anchor: ولعل إيراد قوله { ولتكملوا العدة } هو الموجب لإسقاط معنى قوله { وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين } ، عن هذه الآية

TABATABAI:2:185#10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r7.claim: The two purpose clauses concern the original fast, not its exception: the Ramadan fast magnifies God for revealing the Quran and gives thanks for guidance and discernment between truth and falsehood.
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r7.anchor: ظاهر الجملتين على ما يشعر به لام الغاية أنهما لبيان الغاية غاية أصل الصيام دون حكم الاستثناء

TABATABAI:2:185#10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r8.claim: Fasting counts as gratitude only when sincerely abstaining from material taint and desire; its outward form magnifies God even without sincere intent, so gratitude is stated as a hope while magnification is not.
TABATABAI:2:185#10/r8.anchor: فإن صورة الصوم والكف سواء اشتمل على إخلاص النية أو لم يشتمل يدل على تكبيره تعالى وتعظيمه فرق بين التكبير والشكر

TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r6.speaker: قتادة
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r6.claim: A report says Ramadan is a divine name and one should say 'the month of Ramadan'; the same view is also attributed to the exegete Qatada.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r6.anchor: وقد نقل هذا الكلام عن قتادة أيضا من المفسرين

TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r7.claim: Al-Tabatabai calls the report singular and strange: lists of divine names omit Ramadan, while reports often say bare Ramadan or Ramadanayn, making omission of 'month' by transmitters implausible.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r7.anchor: والأخبار الواردة في عد أسمائه تعالى خال عن ذكر رمضان، على أن لفظ رمضان من غير تصديره بلفظ شهر وكذا رمضانان

TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r8.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r8.claim: Al-Sadiq tells Sabah b. Nabatih that one who is at home when Ramadan enters should not travel except for Hajj, umra, or urgent pursuit of wealth; al-Tabatabai treats this as an inferred recommendation from the verse's general wording.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r8.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الصباح بن نباتة قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام إن ابن أبي يعفور، أمرني أن أسألك عن مسائل فقال

TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r9.speaker: قوم
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r9.claim: Ali b. al-Husayn reports one juristic view that a traveler or sick person may fast.

TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r10.speaker: آخرون
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r10.claim: Ali b. al-Husayn reports another juristic view that a traveler or sick person must not fast.

TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r11.speaker: قوم
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r11.claim: A third juristic view reported by Ali b. al-Husayn lets a traveler or sick person choose whether to fast or break the fast.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r11.anchor: وقال قوم إن شاء صام وإن شاء أفطر

TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r12.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r12.claim: Ali b. al-Husayn states the Ahl al-Bayt position: sick and traveling people break the fast, and anyone who fasts in those states must make it up.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#7/r12.anchor: وفي الكافي عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام قال

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r1.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r1.claim: Al-Baqir explains that whoever witnesses Ramadan must fast, while whoever travels during it must break the fast.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r1.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الباقر عليه السلام في قوله { فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه } ، قال عليه السلام ما أبينها لمن عقلها،

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r2.claim: Many reports from the Imams require sick and traveling people to break the fast; al-Tabatabai says this is their position and the verse supports it.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r2.anchor: والأخبار عن أئمة أهل البيت في تعين الإفطار على المريض والمسافر كثيرة ومذهبهم ذلك، وقد عرفت دلالة الآية عليه.

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r6.claim: The sick person in Abu Basir's fidya report is chronically ill and unable to make up fasts later, not the temporary Ramadan illness covered by 2:184; excessive thirst is itself an illness.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r6.anchor: والمراد بالمريض في رواية أبي بصير المريض في سائر أيام السنة غير أيام شهر رمضان ممن لا يقدر على عدة أيام أخر

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r7.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r7.claim: Al-Sadiq says the Eid al-Fitr takbir is recommended at Maghrib, Isha, dawn, noon, afternoon, and the two-rak'a Eid prayer.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r7.anchor: وفي تفسيره أيضا عن سعيد عن الصادق عليه السلام قال إن في الفطر تكبيرا

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r8.claim: Sa'id al-Naqqash reports that Abu Abdillah recommends the Eid-night takbir at Maghrib, last Isha, dawn, and Eid prayer, with a specified formula, then stopping it.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r8.anchor: وفي الكافي عن سعيد النقاش قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام لي في ليلة الفطر تكبيرة ولكنه مسنون، قال قلت وأين هو؟

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r9.claim: The disagreement over including noon and afternoon prayers can reflect different grades of recommendation; completing the fast's count can be associated with Eid prayer and takbir with the prayers.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r9.anchor: أقول اختلاف الروايتين في إثبات الظهرين وعدمه يمكن أن يحمل على مراتب الاستحباب، وقوله عليه السلام يعني الصلاة لعله يريد

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r10.claim: This recommended practice does not conflict with the verse's apparent sense: it is a recommended ruling inferred from a context of obligation, like the recommendation against traveling after Ramadan begins at home.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r10.anchor: وهو غير مناف لما ذكرناه من ظاهر معنى قوله { ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم } ، فإنه استفادة حكم استحبابي من مورد الوجوب

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r11.claim: The differing endings of the takbir formulas support reading 'magnify' as including praise, which explains why the verse uses the preposition 'ala'.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r11.anchor: يؤيد ما قيل إن قوله { ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم } ، بتضمين التكبير معنى الحمد ولذلك عدي بعلي.

TABATABAI:2:185#11/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r12.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r12.claim: Al-Sadiq rejects the claim that the Prophet more often fasted twenty-nine than thirty days: he says the Prophet always completed thirty, as the verse requires.
TABATABAI:2:185#11/r12.anchor: عن ابن أبي عمير عن الصادق عليه السلام قال قلت له جعلت فداك ما يتحدث به عندنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم صام تسعة وعشرين أكثر

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r1.claim: The report supports the reading that completing the count means completing the month of Ramadan.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r1.anchor: الرواية تدل على ما قدمناه أن ظاهر التكميل تكميل شهر رمضان

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r2.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r2.claim: A report in al-Barqī’s Maḥāsin glosses takbīr as magnification and guidance as wilāya.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r2.anchor: وفي محاسن البرقي عن بعض أصحابنا رفعه في قوله ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم قال التكبير التعظيم

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r3.claim: He treats guidance as wilāya as an application or identification of an instance, possibly taʾwīl; reports also identify ease with wilāya and hardship with opposition and the rule of God’s enemies.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r3.anchor: والهداية الولاية من باب الجري وبيان المصداق ويمكن أن يكون من قبيل ما يسمى تأويلا

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r4.claim: Some reports identify ease with wilāya and hardship with opposition to it and the authority of God’s enemies.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r4.anchor: في بعض الروايات أن اليسر هو الولاية، والعسر الخلاف

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r5.claim: Asked how the Qur’an was revealed in Ramadan though its descent spanned twenty years, al-Ṣādiq says it descended all at once to al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, then over twenty years.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r5.anchor: نزل القرآن جملة واحدة في شهر رمضان إلى البيت المعمور ثم نزل في طول عشرين سنة

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r6.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r6.claim: The Prophet’s chronology says the Suḥuf came on Ramadan’s first night, Torah on the sixth, Zabūr on the eighteenth, and Qur’an on the twenty-third.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r6.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r7.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes that al-Suyūṭī also transmits the Prophet’s revelation chronology through several routes from Wāʾila b. al-Asqaʿ.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r7.anchor: رواه السيوطي في الدر المنثور بعدة طرق عن وائلة بن الأسقع عن النبي

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r8.claim: Asked whether the Night of Decree occurred once or recurs annually, al-Ṣādiq answers that if it were removed, the Qur’an would be removed.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r8.anchor: عن يعقوب قال سمعت رجلا يسأل أبا عبد الله عن ليلة القدر فقال أخبرني عن ليلة القدر كانت أو تكون في كل سنة

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies Ramadan, the blessed night, and the Night of Decree as the same night: the Qur’an descended whole to al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, then piecemeal to Muhammad in commands, prohibitions, and wars.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r9.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور عن ابن عباس، قال شهر رمضان والليلة المباركة

TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the same account of the Qur’an’s whole descent to al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr is also narrated from Saʿīd b. Jubayr.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#8/r10.anchor: وروي هذا المعنى عن غيره أيضا كسعيد بن جبير

TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r1.claim: The cited Qur’anic evidence includes al-Tur’s references to an inscribed book, al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, and the raised ceiling.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r1.anchor: وكتاب مسطور في رق منشور والبيت المعمور

TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r2.claim: The cited passages are mostly clear, but reading the star positions as the first heaven and the Qur’an’s location there is obscure; al-Wāqiʿa does not clearly prove it.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r2.anchor: وجميع ذلك ظاهر إلا ما ذكره في مواقع

TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r3.speaker: أهل البيت
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r3.claim: Reports from the Prophet’s Household place al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr in heaven.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r3.anchor: وقد ورد من طرق أهل البيت أن البيت المعمور في السماء

TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r4.claim: Hadith, like the Qur’an, includes clear and ambiguous material; allusion and symbol are common for realities such as the Tablet, Pen, veils, heaven, al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, and the sealed sea, so interpretation needs contextual clues.
TABATABAI:2:183-185#9/r4.anchor: أن الحديث كمثل القرآن في اشتماله على المحكم والمتشابه

AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r1.claim: ولتكملوا continues the preceding clause with an understood يريد: God wants you to complete the count and magnify Him.
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r1.anchor: وهو معطوف على ما قبله كأنه قال "ويريد لتكملوا العدة"

AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r2.claim: يريد الله ليبين لكم means He wants this in order to explain to you; alternatively, an omitted أن after the lām governs the verb, as in 2:213.
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r2.anchor: وأما قوله {يريد الله ليبين لكم} فانما معناه يريد هذا ليبين لكم

AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r3.claim: The poem أريد لأنسى likewise means I want this thing in order to forget her, with the intended object of يريد left implicit.
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r3.anchor: أريد لأنسى ذكرها فكأنما * تمثل لي ليلى بكل سبيل

AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r4.claim: شهر رمضان explains the previously mentioned counted days: those days are the month of Ramadan.

AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r5.claim: Some read شهر رمضان in the accusative, either as an imperative understood as 'Ramadan, so fast,' or as a time adverbial to the fasting obligation; رمضان is genitive by annexation and diptote.
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r5.anchor: وقد نصب بعضهم {شهر رمضان} [وذلك] * جائز على الامر

AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r6.claim: هدى and بينات are accusative because the verb is already occupied by القرآن, like وجد عبد الله ظريفا.

AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r7.claim: الفرقان is genitive, coordinated with the من in من الفرقان.
AKHFASH:v1p169#2/r7.anchor: وأما قوله {والفرقان} فجر على "وبينات من الفرقان"

TABRISI:2:185/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:2:185/r5.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits from Muḥammad ibn Muslim that the Prophet first broke a Ramadan journey fast at Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, ordered the people to break theirs, and called those who continued disobedient; the name persisted until his death.
TABRISI:2:185/r5.anchor: إلى محمد بن مسلم عن أبي عبد الله قال: لم يكن رسول الله يصوم في السفر

TABRISI:2:185/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:185/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Shaʿbī understand the phrase to cover all people under an initial choice between fasting and feeding, later abrogated by the command to fast when present for Ramadan.
TABRISI:2:185/r8.anchor: أنه ساير الناس كما قدمنا ذكره من التخيير والنسخ بعده وهو قول ابن عباس والشعبي

TABRISI:2:185#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
TABRISI:2:185#2/r1.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads ولتكملوا with a doubled consonant; the other readers use the lighter form.
TABRISI:2:185#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم ولتكملوا بالتشديد والباقون لتكملوا بالتخفيف

TABRISI:2:185#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:2:185#2/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads العسر and اليسر with the heavier articulation; the remaining readers use the lighter articulation.
TABRISI:2:185#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر العسر واليسر بالتثقيل فيهما والباقون بالتخفيف

TABRISI:2:185#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#2/r3.claim: The reading ولتكملوا is supported by the Qur'anic wording اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم.
TABRISI:2:185#2/r3.anchor:
ولتكملوا قوله:
اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم

TABRISI:2:185#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r4.speaker: النابغة
TABRISI:2:185#2/r4.claim: The other form is supported by the interchangeability of the فعل and أفعل patterns; al-Nābigha's verse uses كملت in this sense.
TABRISI:2:185#2/r4.anchor:
النابغة.
فكملت مائة منها حمامتها وأسرعت حسبة في ذلك العدد

TABRISI:2:185#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#2/r5.claim: Shahr is the familiar word for month, pluralized as أشهر for a small number and شهور for larger numbers; its root concerns appearing, as the crescent makes a month known.
TABRISI:2:185#2/r5.anchor: الشهر معروف وجمعه في القلة أشهر وفي الكثرة شهور وأصله من اشتهاره بالهلال

TABRISI:2:185#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#2/r6.claim: The root شهَر also means to make something manifest or draw it out; a broad, heavy she-camel is also called شهيرة.

TABRISI:2:185#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#2/r7.claim: Ramadan derives from intense heat striking sand; the months were named for their seasons, and Ramadan coincided with hot weather. Its plural includes رمضانات.
TABRISI:2:185#2/r7.anchor: وأصل رمضان من الرمض، وهو شدة وقع الشمس على الرمل

TABRISI:2:185#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:185#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid reports that Ramadan is one of God's names and advises saying شهر رمضان because one cannot know what Ramadan is.
TABRISI:2:185#2/r8.anchor:
عن مجاهد:
" لا تقل رمضان ولكن قل شهر رمضان

TABRISI:2:185#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#2/r9.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:185#2/r9.claim: A Prophetic report promises forgiveness of prior sins to whoever fasts Ramadan with faith and expectation of reward.
TABRISI:2:185#2/r9.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" من صام رمضان إيمانا واحتسابا

TABRISI:2:185#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r1.claim: Another proposed etymology says Ramadan was named because it burns away sins.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r1.anchor: سمي رمضان لأنه يرمض الذنوب أي يحرقها

TABRISI:2:185#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r2.claim: Qur'an is connected to gathering: Arabs said a she-camel had not gathered her womb around a foetus, and reading gathers letters together.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r2.anchor: والقرآن أصله الجمع لقولهم ما قرأت الناقة سلأ قط

TABRISI:2:185#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r3.claim: Furqān means that which distinguishes truth from falsehood.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r3.anchor: والفرقان الذي يفرق بين الحق والباطل

TABRISI:2:185#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r4.claim: Irāda has an original wāw, as related forms such as rāwadahu and rād; it means seeking the intended object and is its cause.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r4.anchor: والإرادة أصلها الواو لأنك تقول راودته على أن يفعل كذا

TABRISI:2:185#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r5.claim: Yusr is the opposite of hardship and has related senses of wealth, the left hand, and a group sharing a camel in maysir; its root is ease.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r5.anchor: واليسر ضد العسر واليسار الغنى والسعة واليسار اليد اليسرى واليسر الجماعة يجتمعون على الجزور

TABRISI:2:185#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r6.claim: The root of ʿusr is hardness; aʿsar can mean left-handed, and aʿsara can mean becoming poor, with ease as its opposite.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r6.anchor: وأصل العسر الصلابة يقال عسر الشيء عسرا ورجل أعسر يعمل بشماله وأعسر الرجل إذا افتقر

TABRISI:2:185#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r7.claim: The verbs كمل الشيء, أكمله, and كمّله all mean that something was completed or brought to completion.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r7.anchor: ويقال كمل الشيء وأكملته وكملته أي تممته

TABRISI:2:185#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r8.claim: شهر رمضان may be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, as apposition to الصيام, or as a subject whose relative clause or description supplies an omitted predicate.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r8.anchor: شهر رمضان في ارتفاعه ثلاثة أوجه

TABRISI:2:185#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r9.claim: Ramadan does not take nunation because it is definite and ends in the augmented alif and nūn resembling the feminine dual endings.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r9.anchor: لا ينصرف رمضان للتعريف وزيادة الألف والنون

TABRISI:2:185#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r10.claim: In Arabic, شهر رمضان can also be accusative as the object of an implied command to fast, or in apposition to أياما.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r10.anchor: ويجوز في العربية شهر رمضان بالنصب من وجهين

TABRISI:2:185#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r11.claim: هدى is accusative as a circumstantial expression, meaning that the Qur'an guides people.

TABRISI:2:185#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r12.claim: Here الشهر is an adverbial time expression meaning the person is resident in the town during Ramadan, not an object; otherwise a traveler who witnesses the month would also have to fast.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r12.anchor: فالشهر ينتصب على أنه ظرف لا على أنه مفعول به

TABRISI:2:185#3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r13.claim: The attached pronoun in فليصمه is permissible through syntactic extension after الشهر has already been used adverbially.
TABRISI:2:185#3/r13.anchor: الاتساع وقع فيه بعد أن استعمل ظرفا

TABRISI:2:185#3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#3/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#3/r14.claim: The preposition in على سفر coordinates with the adjective مريضا because it has the sense of the noun مسافرا.

TABRISI:2:185#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#4/r1.claim: The same coordination of an adverbial phrase with an adjective appears in Yunus 10:12, where lying, sitting, and standing are coordinated forms.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r1.anchor: دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما

TABRISI:2:185#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r2.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:2:185#4/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats ولتكملوا as a coordinated sentence with an omitted clause, approximately: this was prescribed or intended so that you complete the count; he compares 6:75.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r2.anchor: عطف جملة على جملة لأن بعده محذوفا

TABRISI:2:185#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:185#4/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj coordinates the phrase with the understood meaning of God's willing ease: He has made matters easy for you so that you complete the count.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r3.anchor: عطفا على تأويل محذوف ودل عليه ما تقدم من الكلام

TABRISI:2:185#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#4/r4.claim: The first grammatical analysis is illustrated by the wording in 6:75: God showed Abraham the kingdom so that he might become certain.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r4.anchor: إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

TABRISI:2:185#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#4/r5.claim: A cited poem illustrates coordination with the inferred sense of an omitted part of the preceding statement; al-Zajjāj gives this analysis, while the first is al-Farrāʾ's.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r5.anchor: بادت وغير آيهن مع البلى إلا رواكد جمرهن هباء

TABRISI:2:185#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#4/r6.claim: The counted days are identified as Ramadan, and it is singled out for fasting because of its special virtues: the Qur'an, on which religion and faith depend, was sent down in it.

TABRISI:2:185#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:185#4/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda say the whole Qur'an descended to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then came to the Prophet piecemeal over twenty years; this is also transmitted from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وقتادة وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله

TABRISI:2:185#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TABRISI:2:185#4/r8.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the Qur'an's revelation began on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r8.anchor: ابتدأ إنزاله في ليلة القدر من شهر رمضان عن ابن إسحاق

TABRISI:2:185#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r9.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:2:185#4/r9.claim: Al-Suddī, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbās, says the year's needed revelation descended together to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then was sent down in stages over months and days.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r9.anchor: في الشهور والأيام عن السدي بسنده إلى ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:185#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#4/r10.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:185#4/r10.claim: A report through Abū Dharr attributes to the Prophet that Abraham's scriptures were sent down on the third of Ramadan.
TABRISI:2:185#4/r10.anchor:
أبي ذر الغفاري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" أنزلت صحف إبراهيم لثلاث مضين

TABRISI:2:185#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#5/r1.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:185#5/r1.claim: In the report's continuation, Abraham's scriptures are dated to the first or third night of Ramadan; Moses' Torah to the sixth, Jesus' Gospel to the thirteenth, David's Psalms to the eighteenth, and the Qur'an to the twenty-fourth. Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits this from al-Ṣādiq and his forefathers, ending with the Prophet.
TABRISI:2:185#5/r1.anchor: لأربع وعشرين من شهر رمضان وهذا بعينه رواه العياشي عن أبي عبد الله عن آبائه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:2:185#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#5/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes أنزل فيه القرآن to mean that the Qur'an was revealed concerning the obligation and prescription of fasting, with فيه meaning concerning its prescription.
TABRISI:2:185#5/r2.anchor: أنه أنزل في فرضه وإيجاب صومه على الخلق

TABRISI:2:185#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#5/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#5/r3.claim: The Qur'an is guidance for people, directing them to the kinds of knowledge they are obligated to acquire, and its signs are proofs of guidance.
TABRISI:2:185#5/r3.anchor: دالا لهم على ما كلفوه من العلوم

TABRISI:2:185#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:185#5/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first guidance is guidance away from error, while the second means clarification of the lawful and unlawful.
TABRISI:2:185#5/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد بالهدى الأول الهدى من الضلالة وبالثاني بيان الحلال والحرام عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:185#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#5/r5.speaker: الأصم
TABRISI:2:185#5/r5.claim: Al-Aṣamm and al-Qāḍī say the first guidance is the initial knowledge required of people; the second comprises accounts of prophets, their laws, and histories, which are known through the Qur'an.
TABRISI:2:185#5/r5.anchor: وقيل أراد بأول ما كلف من العلم وبالثاني ما يشتمل عليه من الأنبياء وشرائعهم وأخبارهم لأنها لا تدرك إلا بالقرآن عن الأصم والقاضي

TABRISI:2:185#6/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#6/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#6/r1.claim: Furqān is that which separates truth from falsehood.
TABRISI:2:185#6/r1.anchor: أي ومما يفرق بين الحق والباطل

TABRISI:2:185#6/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#6/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:2:185#6/r2.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh distinguishes the Qur'an as the book as a whole from the Furqān, the decisive rulings that must be followed.
TABRISI:2:185#6/r2.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه قال: القرآن جملة الكتاب

TABRISI:2:185#6/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#6/r3.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:185#6/r3.claim: In a sermon reported by al-Bāqir through al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, Abū Ayyūb, and Abū al-Ward, the Prophet describes Ramadan's night better than a thousand months, obligatory fast, and voluntary night prayer worth seventy months' prayers; good deeds equal obligatory deeds elsewhere and an obligatory deed equals seventy. He calls it a month of patience, mutual aid, and increased provision; feeding a faster brings emancipation and forgiveness, even a sip of milk, water, or a few dates suffices, and easing a servant's work eases one's reckoning. He describes its beginning as mercy, middle as forgiveness, and end as answered prayer and release from fire; he urges testimony, asking for needs and Paradise, and seeking refuge from Hell.
TABRISI:2:185#6/r3.anchor: خطب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الناس في آخر جمعة من شعبان

TABRISI:2:185#6/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#6/r4.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
TABRISI:2:185#6/r4.claim: Salman al-Fārisī's version urges four practices: the testimony of faith and seeking forgiveness please God, while asking for Paradise and refuge from Hell are indispensable.
TABRISI:2:185#6/r4.anchor:
وفي رواية سلمان الفارسي
" فاستكثروا فيه من أربع خصال

TABRISI:2:185#7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r1.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:185#7/r1.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that a fasting person's sleep is worship, silence is glorification, prayer is answered, and deeds are multiplied.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r1.anchor:
وقال رسول الله:
" نوم الصائم عبادة وصمته تسبيح ودعاؤه مستجاب وعمله مضاعف "

TABRISI:2:185#7/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#7/r2.claim: The stronger reading is that one who is present in town and not away during Ramadan must fast the whole month; الشهر is definite for the known month.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r2.anchor: فمن شهد منكم المصر وحضر ولم يغب في الشهر والألف واللام في الشهر للعهد والمراد به شهر رمضان

TABRISI:2:185#7/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:2:185#7/r3.claim: Asked about the wording, Abū Jaʿfar says it plainly means whoever witnesses Ramadan should fast it, while whoever travels in it should break the fast; this report is from Zurāra.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r3.anchor: ما رواه زرارة عن أبي جعفر أنه قال لما سئل عن هذه ما أبينها لمن عقلها قال من شهد رمضان فليصمه

TABRISI:2:185#7/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r4.speaker: علي
TABRISI:2:185#7/r4.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and other exegetes say that entering Ramadan while resident obliges fasting its entire month.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r4.anchor: وقد روي أيضا عن علي وابن عباس ومجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين أنهم قالوا: من شهد الشهر بأن دخل عليه الشهر

TABRISI:2:185#7/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#7/r5.claim: A second reading takes the phrase to mean a legally responsible person who is resident when the month arrives must fast that month; it abrogates the earlier choice of fasting or fidya, since recitation order does not determine order of revelation. Tabrisi prefers the first reading.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r5.anchor: من شاهد منهم الشهر مقيما مكلفا فليصم الشهر بعينه وهذا نسخ للتخيير بين الصوم والفدية

TABRISI:2:185#7/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#7/r6.claim: The qualifying illness is one that makes a person fear an extreme worsening of the illness.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r6.anchor: وحد المرض الذي يوجب الإفطار ما يخاف الإنسان معه الزيادة المفرطة في مرضه

TABRISI:2:185#7/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:2:185#7/r7.claim: Abū Baṣīr reports that al-Ṣādiq leaves assessment of illness to the person: if weak, break the fast; if strong enough, fast, whatever the illness.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r7.anchor: وروى أبو بصير قال: سألت أبا عبد الله عن حد المرض الذي على صاحبه فيه الإفطار قال: هو مؤتمن عليه مفوض إليه

TABRISI:2:185#7/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:185#7/r8.claim: Another transmitted definition is any illness that prevents someone from standing for as long as a prayer; al-Ḥasan holds this, and jurists disagree.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r8.anchor: وروي أيضا: أن ذلك كل مرض لا يقدر معه على القيام بمقدار زمان صلاته وبه قال الحسن وفي ذلك اختلاف بين الفقهاء

TABRISI:2:185#7/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#7/r9.claim: In the Imāmī school, a journey allowing a fast to be broken is permitted or devotional and measures eight farsakhs, twenty-four miles; al-Shāfiʿī requires sixteen farsakhs and Abū Ḥanīfa twenty-four.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r9.anchor: وأما السفر الذي يوجب الإفطار عندنا فما كان مباحا أو طاعة وكانت المسافة ثمانية فراسخ أربعة وعشرين ميلا

TABRISI:2:185#7/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r10.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:185#7/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others require making up missed days immediately once the sick person recovers or the traveler returns.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r10.anchor: فقال الحسن وجماعة هي على التضييق إذا برىء المريض أو قدم المسافر

TABRISI:2:185#7/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
TABRISI:2:185#7/r11.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa allows make-up days to be delayed; the Imāmī school sets the period before the next Ramadan, allows consecutive or separate days, and prefers consecutive days.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r11.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة موسع فيها وعندنا موقت بما بين رمضانين وتجوز متتابعة ومتفرقة والتتابع أفضل

TABRISI:2:185#7/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#7/r12.claim: If make-up fasting is delayed until another Ramadan arrives, fidya is due along with the make-up fast; al-Shāfiʿī agrees.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r12.anchor: فإن فرط حتى لحقه رمضان آخر لزمه الفدية والقضاء وبه قال الشافعي

TABRISI:2:185#7/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#7/r13.claim: God wills ease by granting the sick and traveler a dispensation not to fast during those circumstances.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r13.anchor: أي في الرخصة للمريض والمسافر إذ لم يوجب الصوم عليهما

TABRISI:2:185#7/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#7/r14.claim: Another interpretation takes God's willing ease to apply to all human affairs.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r14.anchor: وقيل يريد الله بكم اليسر في جميع أموركم

TABRISI:2:185#7/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#7/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#7/r15.claim: Tabrisi uses the verse against the compulsion doctrine: God wills ease in some human acts, does not will hardship in others, and therefore does not will imposing the impossible.
TABRISI:2:185#7/r15.anchor: وفيه دلالة على بطلان قول المجبرة لأنه بين أن في أفعال المكلفين ما يريده سبحانه وهو اليسر

TABRISI:2:185#8/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#8/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#8/r1.claim: The completion is the make-up of the days missed through illness or travel, fasted after recovery or return; alternatively, the concession to break the fast was prescribed so the count could be completed later.
TABRISI:2:185#8/r1.anchor: أي تتموا عدة ما أفطرتم فيه وهي أيام السفر والمرض بالقضاء إذا أقمتم وبرأتم

TABRISI:2:185#8/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#8/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#8/r2.claim: Another possibility is completing the month's count: people without an excuse complete it then, while the sick and travelers complete it at another time.
TABRISI:2:185#8/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون معناه ولتكملوا عدة الشهر لأنه مع الطاقة وعدم العذر يسهل عليه إكمال العدة

TABRISI:2:185#8/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#8/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#8/r3.claim: Those who argue Ramadan is never shorter say the command requires an undiminished full count; Tabrisi answers that the required count may be twenty-nine or thirty days, or that the wording refers to making up missed days.
TABRISI:2:185#8/r3.anchor: أن المراد أكملوا العدة التي وجب عليكم صيامها

TABRISI:2:185#8/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#8/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#8/r4.claim: In the Imāmī school, this refers to the takbīr on the night of Eid al-Fiṭr after Maghrib, ʿIshāʾ, dawn, and the Eid prayer.
TABRISI:2:185#8/r4.anchor: المراد به تكبير ليلة الفطر عقيب أربع صلوات المغرب والعشاء الآخرة والغداة وصلاة العيد على مذهبنا

TABRISI:2:185#8/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#8/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:185#8/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others interpret it as saying the takbīr on Eid day.
TABRISI:2:185#8/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وجماعة التكبير يوم الفطر

TABRISI:2:185#8/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#8/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#8/r6.claim: Another interpretation is to magnify God for guiding people to the religious laws.
TABRISI:2:185#8/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد به ولتعظموا الله على ما أرشدكم له من شرائع الدين

TABRISI:2:185#8/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:185#8/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:185#8/r7.claim: The verse's close means that people should thank God for His blessings.

THALABI:v2p71/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r1.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v2p71/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says that while traveling during Ramadan, he broke his fast at the bridge gate.
THALABI:v2p71/r1.anchor: وعن الشعبي: إنه سافر في رمضان فأفطر عند باب الجسر

THALABI:v2p71/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p71/r2.claim: One view permits breaking the fast for any condition called an illness.
THALABI:v2p71/r2.anchor: فقال قوم: هو كل مرض يسمى مريضا

THALABI:v2p71/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r3.speaker: طريف بن تمام العطاردي
THALABI:v2p71/r3.claim: Tarif ibn Tammam al-Ataridi reports that he visited Ibn Sirin eating in Ramadan; afterward Ibn Sirin said his finger had hurt, illustrating a broad use of illness.
THALABI:v2p71/r3.anchor: وقال [طريف بن تمام] العطاردي: دخلت على محمد بن سيرين يوما في شهر رمضان وهو يأكل

THALABI:v2p71/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r4.speaker: الشافعي
THALABI:v2p71/r4.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits breaking the fast when fasting would usually worsen an illness beyond what the patient can bear.
THALABI:v2p71/r4.anchor: زيادة غير محتملة، وهو اختيار الشافعي

THALABI:v2p71/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r5.speaker: الحسن، إبراهيم
THALABI:v2p71/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibrahim say a patient unable to pray standing may break the fast; generally, fasting that exhausts someone permits breaking it, while a fast that causes no strain leaves them like a healthy person.
THALABI:v2p71/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن وإبراهيم: إذا لم يستطع المريض أن يصلي قائما أفطر

THALABI:v2p71/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r6.speaker: عمرو، أبو هريرة، ابن عباس، علي بن الحسين، عروة بن الزبير، الضحاك
THALABI:v2p71/r6.claim: This group says breaking the fast while traveling is obligatory, not a concession, so a traveler who fasts must make it up after returning; they cite the report that fasting on a journey is not righteousness.
THALABI:v2p71/r6.anchor: فقال قوم: الإفطار في السفر عزيمة واجبة وليس برخصة فمن صام في السفر فعليه القضاء إذا أقام، وهو قول عمرو أبي هريرة وابن عباس

THALABI:v2p71/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p71/r7.claim: Umm al-Dardaʾ reports from Kaʿb ibn ʿAsim the Prophet’s statement that fasting while traveling is not an act of righteousness.
THALABI:v2p71/r7.anchor: عن كعب بن عاصم قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «ليس من البر الصيام في السفر»

THALABI:v2p71/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r8.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
THALABI:v2p71/r8.claim: Al-Zuhri reports from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf that a fasting traveler is like someone breaking the fast at home.
THALABI:v2p71/r8.anchor: عن حميد بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف عن أبيه قال: الصائم في السفر كالمفطر في الحضر

THALABI:v2p71/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p71/r9.claim: The author calls the majority position correct: breaking the fast is a divine concession, and a traveler may choose either to fast and fulfill the duty or to break the fast under the concession.
THALABI:v2p71/r9.anchor: وهذا هو الصحيح وعليه عامة الفقهاء. ويدل عليه: ما روى عاصم بن الأحول

THALABI:v2p71/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r10.speaker: جابر
THALABI:v2p71/r10.claim: Jabir reports that on a journey some companions fasted and others did not, and neither group criticized the other.
THALABI:v2p71/r10.anchor: عن جابر قال: كنا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفر فمنا الصائم ومنا المفطر فلم يكن بعضنا يعيب

THALABI:v2p71/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p71/r11.claim: The Prophet tells Hamza ibn Amr that while traveling he may choose to fast or break his habitual fast.
THALABI:v2p71/r11.anchor: إن حمزة بن عمرو قال: يا رسول الله إني كنت أتعود الصيام أفأصوم في السفر قال: «إن شئت فصم

THALABI:v2p71/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p71/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p71/r12.claim: In another report to Hamza ibn Amr, the Prophet calls breaking the fast a concession: taking it is good, and one who prefers to fast incurs no blame.
THALABI:v2p71/r12.anchor: عن حمزة بن عمرو إنه قال: يا رسول الله أجد بي قوة على الصيام في السفر فهل علي جناح قال: «هي رخصة من الله عز وجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p566/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p566/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p566/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, ʿAlqama, Ibn Shihāb, and most scholars say fasting initially allowed a choice to fast or feed one poor person instead; 2:185 abrogated that option.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p566/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كانت الإطاقة أن الرجل أو المرأة كان يصبح صائما، ثم إن شاء أفطر وأطعم لذلك مسكينا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r1.claim: The name shahr derives from visibility or public recognition: the month is prominent in dealings, debts, and ritual observances people need to schedule.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r1.anchor: الشهر: مأخوذ من الشهرة، تقول شهر الشيء يشهره شهرا: إذا أظهره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r2.speaker: الليث وابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r2.claim: Al-Layth and Ibn al-Aʿrābī explain the moon’s name as month by its visibility: it becomes apparent or is made conspicuous.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r2.anchor: قال الليث: والشهر: ظهور الشيء، وسمي (¬2) الهلال شهرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the crescent is called a month because it is visible and clear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: سمي الهلال شهرا لشهرته وبيانه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم؛ ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r4.claim: Some say the month is named for the crescent: Arabs say they saw the month to mean its new moon, as witnessed by Dhū al-Rumma’s line using al-shahr for the crescent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r4.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: يرى الشهر قبل الناس وهو بخيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says he has heard no verb from the word except ashhernā, meaning a month has arrived for us.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: ولم أسمع منه فعلا إلا هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r6.claim: One parsing makes shahr an appositive for al-ṣiyām, yielding the sense that fasting Ramadan was prescribed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r6.anchor: وارتفع على البدل من الصيام، كأن المعنى: كتب عليكم شهر رمضان.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r7.claim: Another parsing makes shahr the subject of an independent clause, with the relative clause as its predicate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ابتداء، وخبره الذي مع صلته، كقولك: زيد الذي في الدار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r8.speaker: الأخفش والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ parse the phrase as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning this is Ramadan, which explains the previously mentioned numbered days.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r8.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ارتفع على أنه خبر ابتداء محذوف، المعنى:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r9.claim: The author finds it more fitting to make alladhī an adjective for the month, explicitly requiring its fast; if it were the predicate, the text would only report that the Qurʾan was revealed in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r9.anchor: قال: والأشبه أن يكون {الذي} وصفا، ليكون النص قد وقع على الأمر بصيام الشهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r10.claim: On the preferred parsing, naming the month again in whoever is present during it honors and emphasizes it, as in the repeated openings of 69:1–2 and 101:1–2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r10.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {الحاقة (1) ما الحاقة} [الحاقة:1 - 2] و {القارعة (1) ما القارعة} [القارعة:1 - 2]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r11.claim: The fāʾ before man shahida is unexpected for the predicate of an independent subject; the author postpones its discussion until that phrase is reached.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p569#2/r11.anchor: والفاء في قوله: {فمن شهد} داخل على خبر الابتداء، وليس من حق خبر الابتداء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the whole Qurʾan descended from the Preserved Tablet on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel delivered it to Muhammad in installments over twenty years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ في ليلة القدر من شهر رمضان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r2.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r2.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, an interpretation chosen by al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl, says the Qurʾan was revealed concerning Ramadan’s merit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r2.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: {أنزل فيه القرآن} معناه: أنزل في فضله القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says it was revealed regarding the obligation to fast Ramadan, just as revelation concerning alms or wine can refer to their legal rulings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأنبارى: أنزل في فرضه وإيجاب صومه على الخلق القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r4.claim: Qurʾan names God’s speech, and authorities disagree over whether the name is derived and whether it takes a hamza.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r4.anchor: فأما (¬5) القرآن فهو اسم لكلام الله تعالى # واختلفوا (¬1) في اشتقاقه وهمزه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r5.speaker: ابن كثير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the word without a hamza.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r6.speaker: الشافعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī treats Qurʾan as an unhamzated name for God’s Book, not derived from qaraʾa; the author says this suggests a proper name like Torah or Gospel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r6.anchor: أن الشافعي، رحمه الله، كان يقول: القرآن اسم، وليس بمهموز، ولم يؤخذ من قرأت،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r7.speaker: جماعة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r7.claim: Another group likewise treats Qurʾan as an un-derived proper name for God’s speech, analogous to those who regard the name Allah as non-derived.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r7.anchor: وقد قال بهذا جماعة، قالوا: إنه اسم كلامه، يجرى مجرى الأعلام في أسماء غيره،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r8.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r8.claim: Others derive the name from qarana, to join things: its chapters, verses, and letters are joined together, so the form qirān is unhamzated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p573/r8.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أنه مأخوذ من قرنت الشيء بالشيء: إذا ضممت أحدهما إلى الآخر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r1.claim: Hudan means guiding, a circumstantial expression that supplies the second object of anzala.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r1.anchor: أي: هاديا، وهو حال قد سد مسد المفعول الثاني لأنزل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r2.claim: Bayyināt is coordinated with hudan, so the verse says the Qurʾan was sent as clarification for people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r3.claim: Bayyināt is the plural of bayyina and means clear, evident proofs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r3.anchor: والبينات: جمع بينة، يقال: بان الشيء يبين بيانا فهو بين، مثل: بيع بمعنى بايع. والبينات: الواضحات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r4.claim: The guidance includes what is lawful and forbidden, legal limits, and rulings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r4.anchor: يريد: من الحلال والحرام والحدود والأحكام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that guidance is direction toward God’s pleasure and the Furqān distinguishes truth from falsehood and clarifies what to do or leave; al-Wāḥidī refers to his earlier explanation at 2:53.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r5.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وبينات من الهدى}: يريد: من الرشاد إلى مرضاة الله، {والفرقان} يريد: فرق فيه بين الحق والباطل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r6.speaker: الأخفش والمازني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Māzinī call the fāʾ redundant because here it marks neither coordination nor a conditional consequence; they cite 62:8 and a poetic line with two fāʾs, one unnecessary after idhā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r6.anchor: زعم الأخفش والمازني: أن الفاء ههنا زائدة، وذلك أن الفاء تدخل للعطف أو للجزاء أو زيادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r7.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī argues the fāʾ can mark a conditional result: Ramadan is a generic, not uniquely specified month, and the command means whoever witnesses the month in which the Qurʾan was revealed must fast it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p580/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: ولا يمتنع (¬1) أن يكون دخول الفاء لمعنى الجزاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r1.claim: Shahida means to be present; its object is omitted, with the sense of being present at one’s town or home rather than traveling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {شهد} أي: حضر. ومعنى الشهود في اللغة: الحضور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r2.claim: Al-shahr is an adverb of time, not a direct object, since everyone experiences the month; the intended meaning is being at home during it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {الشهر} انتصابه على الظرف، ولا يجوز أن يكون مفعولا به؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r3.claim: The verse assumes the witness is rational, adult, resident, and healthy for fasting to be obligatory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r3.anchor: ولا بد أيضا من إضمار حال الشاهد وصفته، التي بوجودها يجب الصوم، وهو أن يقال: من شهد منكم الشهر عاقلا بالغا مقيما صحيحا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر أهل التأويل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most exegetes read it as fasting the part of the month one witnesses; a person who travels during the month may break the fast.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأكثر أهل التأويل: معناه: فليصم ما شهد منه؛ لأنه إن سافر في حال الشهر كان له الإفطار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r5.speaker: النخعي والسدي وابن سيرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p582/r5.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, al-Suddī, Ibn Sīrīn, and a group hold that someone resident at the beginning of the month may not break the fast after traveling.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r1.claim: The sick and traveler exemption is repeated because the earlier command to fast could otherwise suggest the abrogation removed everyone’s former option; its repetition confirms their dispensation remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r1.anchor: أعاد هاهنا تخيير المريض والمسافر وترخيصهما في الإفطار؛ لأن الله تعالى ذكر في الآية الأولى تخيير المقيمين بقوله: {فليصمه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r2.claim: A person may break the fast for any illness likely to worsen beyond what they can bear; if fasting exhausts the person, they should break it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r2.anchor: هو كل مرض كان الأغلب من أمر صاحبه بالصوم الزيادة في علته زيادة لا يحتمله، والأصل فيه: أنه إذا أجهده الصوم أفطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r3.claim: The journey that permits breaking the fast is sixteen farsakhs or more.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r3.anchor: وحد السفر الذي يبيح الإفطار (¬1): ستة عشر فرسخا (¬2) فصاعدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r4.speaker: عامة الفقهاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r4.claim: Most jurists regard breaking the fast as a divine concession for travelers: one who breaks it accepts the concession, and one who fasts fulfills the obligation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r4.anchor: والإفطار رخصة من الله للمسافر، فمن (¬3) أفطر فبرخصة الله أخذ، ومن صام ففرضه أدى، على هذا عامة الفقهاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r5.claim: The Prophet’s statement that fasting while traveling is not righteousness is directed at a traveler whom fasting strains and exhausts; fasting is disliked for that person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r5.anchor: ومن أجهده الصوم في السفر كره له ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r6.speaker: قوم من الصحابة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r6.claim: Some Companions hold that breaking the fast during travel is obligatory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p584/r6.anchor: وذهب قوم من الصحابة إلى أن الإفطار في السفر واجب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r1.claim: God wills ease by granting the sick and traveler a concession to break the fast.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r2.claim: Yusr means ease; yasar (wealth or abundance) is so called because it makes affairs easier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r2.anchor: معناه: السهولة، ومنه يقال للغنى والسعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r3.claim: The left hand is said either to be named optimistically for ease or because it helps the right hand make tasks easier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r3.anchor: قيل: على التفاؤل باليسر، وقيل: لأنه يتسهل الأمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r4.claim: God does not will hardship because He has not imposed severity or restriction on you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r4.anchor: لأنه لم يشدد ولم يضيق عليكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r5.claim: The affirmation and negation of divine will here concern legal rulings for Muslims.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r5.anchor: وهذه الإرادة ونفي الإرادة تختص بالأحكام لأهل الإسلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r6.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r6.claim: God intends His command to fast to be easy for you, not difficult.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r6.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل: يريد الله أن يكون أمره بالصوم عليكم ميسرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r7.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r7.claim: A period of days is called an ʿidda; Abu Zayd says a man’s ʿidda ends when his appointed term ends.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r7.anchor: قال أبو زيد: يقال انقضت عدة الرجل إذا انقضى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r8.claim: Through ʿAta, Ibn Abbas says to complete the month’s days exactly: thirty if it has thirty, twenty-nine if it has twenty-nine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r8.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: ولتكملوا عدة أيام الشهر، إن كان ثلاثين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r9.claim: A report through al-Kalbi from Abu Salih says to make up each missed day with one day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r9.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا يعني: عدة ما أفطرتم، يوما مكان يوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r10.claim: In both reports, Ibn Abbas interprets completing the count as making up Ramadan fasts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r10.anchor: فحمل ابن عباس إكمال العدة في الروايتين على قضاء رمضان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r11.claim: On the make-up reading, the conjunction follows the sense rather than wording: the concession eases matters so people can complete the count after recovery or returning home.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r11.anchor: العطف على معنى الكلام لا على ظاهر اللفظ، وذلك أن في إباحته الإفطار للمريض والمسافر تسهيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r12.claim: Arabic may coordinate according to intended meaning; al-Zajjaj’s cited poetry supplies an example of coordination by sense.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p586/r13.claim: Ibn al-Anbari supports coordination by sense with a poem: if snakes spare a foot, the foot has spared them too.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r1.claim: One analysis coordinates the phrase with an omitted earlier purpose clause: God wills ease and does not will hardship, to make people happy and let them complete the count.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r1.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الواو عاطفة على مضمر في الكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ instead treats the waw as resumptive and the lām as governed by an omitted verb: God granted the concession so people would make up missed fasts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r2.anchor: واختار الفراء هذا القول، وقال: معنى الآية: ولتكملوا العدة في قضاء ما أفطرتم، والواو واو استئناف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ compares the omitted verb to God showing Abraham the kingdoms so that he would become certain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r3.anchor: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the phrase means completing the month’s days, implying performance rather than make-up.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أيضا ما يدل على أن المراد بإكمال العدة إكمالها في الأداء لا في القضاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r5.claim: Most exegetes understand completing the count as making up missed fasts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r5.anchor: والمفسرون على أن المراد به إكمال العدة في القضاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r6.claim: The light form is supported by the verse today I have perfected your religion and Imruʾ al-Qays’s poetic usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r6.anchor: فمن خفف فلقوله: {اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r7.claim: The doubled form is valid because faʿʿala and afʿala often alternate; al-Nabigha’s verse is another example.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r7.anchor: ومن شدد فلأن فعل وأفعل يتعاقبان في أكثر الأحوال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p588/r8.claim: The lām is purposive, not imperative; an imperative lām after waw, fa, or thumma may be vowelless, as in the two readings of the Hajj verse.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r1.claim: In ʿAta’s report, Ibn Abbas says to magnify God for the religious laws to which He guided you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد لتعظموا الله على. ما أرشدكم له من شرائع الدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r2.speaker: أكثر العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r2.claim: Most scholars understand this as the takbir on the night of Eid al-Fitr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r2.anchor: أكثر العلماء (¬6): أراد به التكبير ليلة الفطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muslims are obliged to pronounce takbir when they see the Shawwal crescent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p590/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: حق على المسلمين إذا رأوا هلال

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r2.claim: The earlier provision allowing a ransom meal for one poor person was abrogated by the command to fast when present for the month.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r2.anchor: وهذا منسوخ بقوله: {فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه} (2) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r3.speaker: author
