IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r3.claim: Al-shahr is accusative as a temporal adverb, not as an object of shahida; the sense is whoever is present during the month and is not traveling should fast.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r3.anchor: والشهر منصوب لأنه ظرف. ولم ينصب بإيقاع شهد عليه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r4.claim: Being present during the month can describe either a resident or a traveler, which is why shahida is not construed as taking the month as its object.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p73#4/r4.anchor: لأن الشهادة للشهر قد تكون للحاضر والمسافر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r1.claim: Ramadan is the numbered-days period mentioned in the preceding verse.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r1.anchor: هي شهر رمضان. يعني: تلك الأيام المعدودات شهر رمضان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r2.claim: The Quran descended as a whole from the Preserved Tablet on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan, was placed in the lower heaven’s Bayt al-ʿIzza, then Gabriel brought it to Muhammad in installments over twenty years.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r2.anchor: أنزل جملة واحد من اللوح المحفوظ في ليلة القدر من شهر رمضان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r3.claim: The Quran is guidance in the sense that it guides people.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r4.claim: Its clear signs explain the lawful and unlawful, prescribed limits, and rulings.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r4.anchor: وآيات واضحات من الحلال والحرام، والحدود والأحكام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r5.claim: Al-Furqān is the distinction between truth and falsehood.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r6.claim: Witnessing the month means being present in one’s own town during it; such a person must fast.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r6.anchor: فمن حضر منكم بلده في الشهر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r7.claim: The sick and travelers retain the earlier dispensation because the earlier verse gave them and residents a choice, while this verse abrogated the resident’s choice.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r7.anchor: لأن الآية الأولى وردت في التخيير للمريض والمسافر والمقيم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r8.claim: God wills ease through the concession for a sick person or traveler.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r8.anchor: بالرخصة للمسافر والمريض { ولا يريد بكم العسر }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r9.claim: God does not intend hardship because He has neither imposed strictness nor narrowed matters for them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r9.anchor: لأنه لم يشدد ولم يضيق عليكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r10.claim: The phrase is joined to an omitted clause; the sense is that God wills ease rather than hardship so that people can complete the count.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r10.anchor: [عطف على محذوف] والمعنى: يريد الله بكم اليسر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r11.claim: They complete the count of missed fasts through make-up days after settling from travel or recovering.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r11.anchor: أي: ولتكملوا عدة ما أفطرتم بالقضاء إذا أقمتم وبرأتم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r12.claim: The commanded magnification is the takbīr on the night of Eid al-Fitr when the crescent of Shawwal is sighted.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r12.anchor: يعني التكبير ليلة الفطر إذا رئي هلال شوال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r13.claim: God guided them to the religious laws.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:185/r13.anchor: على ما هداكم } أرشدكم من شرائع الدين

ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r18.claim: Observing divine law requires soul-training, patience, and restraint of the commanding self; fasting is imposed here as an effective spiritual and bodily discipline that renews believers’ inner life.
ELMALILI:2:180-182#5/r18.anchor: iyi bir terbiye-i nefsiyeye mütevakkıftır. Bu ise insanda sabır ve nefs-i emmâreyi zabt ile evâmir-i ilâhiyeye inkıyad melekesini

ELMALILI:2:185/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the verse as saying Ramadan is the month when the Qur’an descended as true criterion and clear proofs of guidance to direct humanity.
ELMALILI:2:185/r1.anchor: O şehr-i Ramazan ki insanları irşâd için hak furkānı, hidâyet delîli beyyineler hâlinde Kur’an onda indirildi.

ELMALILI:2:185/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r2.claim: Shahr derives from publicity or manifestation: the crescent first appears, and the month is named for the interval from one crescent’s appearance to its next appearance, normally twenty-nine or thirty days.
ELMALILI:2:185/r2.anchor: “Şehr” esasında şöhretten masdar olup bir şeyi izhar etmek mânasınadır.

ELMALILI:2:185/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r3.claim: Astronomers define the month as the interval between two solar conjunctions, but that specialist definition differs from the common lexical sense, measured between the appearances of crescents.
ELMALILI:2:185/r3.anchor: Müneccimîn bunu kamerin şems ile iki ictimâ‘ı

ELMALILI:2:185/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r4.speaker: Mücâhid
ELMALILI:2:185/r4.claim: Mujāhid reports that Ramadan is one of God’s names, making shahr Ramadan mean God’s month.
ELMALILI:2:185/r4.anchor: Mücâhid’den mervî olduğu üzere esmâullahdan bir isimdir. Ve “şehr-i Ramazan” demek

ELMALILI:2:185/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r5.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
ELMALILI:2:185/r5.claim: A Prophetic report cautions against saying Ramadan came or went, instructing people to say the month of Ramadan; al-Bayhaqī grades this report weak.
ELMALILI:2:185/r5.anchor: Ve bir hadîs-i nebevî olmak üzere şöyle rivayet edilmiştir: “Ramazan geldi, Ramazan gitti demeyiniz

ELMALILI:2:185/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r6.speaker: Beyhâkî
ELMALILI:2:185/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqī considers weak the report that Ramadan is one of God’s names and that one should say the month of Ramadan.
ELMALILI:2:185/r6.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh Beyhâkî bu hadîse zayıf demiştir.

ELMALILI:2:185/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r7.claim: A second opinion takes Ramadan, like Rajab and Shaʿbān, as the proper name of a particular month rather than a divine name.

ELMALILI:2:185/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r8.claim: If Ramadan is a divine name, the full phrase shahr Ramadan is a proper name; if Ramadan names the month, the phrase is an explanatory genitive of a general term to a specific one.
ELMALILI:2:185/r8.anchor: Evvelkine göre “şehr” dâhil olarak شَهْرُ رَمَضَان terkîbinin mecmû‘u bir ism-i ‘alemdir. İkinciye göre isim yalnız “Ramazan”

ELMALILI:2:185/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r9.claim: Ramadan, Rabīʿ al-Awwal, and Rabīʿ al-Thānī are properly named with shahr, though it is sometimes omitted for brevity; omission for Ramadan is mildly disfavored by Imam Muḥammad but allowed without risk of confusion.
ELMALILI:2:185/r9.anchor: Tahkīke göre şühûr-ı kameriyeden üçü; şehr-i ramazan, şehr-i rebî‘u’l-evvel, şehr-i rebî‘u’l-âhir, “şehr” kelimesiyle beraber ism-i ‘alemdir.

ELMALILI:2:185/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r10.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
ELMALILI:2:185/r10.claim: A Prophetic hadith says that whoever fasts Ramadan in faith and seeking reward will have earlier sins forgiven, illustrating omission of shahr before Ramadan.
ELMALILI:2:185/r10.anchor: Nitekim hadîs-i nebevîde dahi مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيْمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ

ELMALILI:2:185/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r11.claim: The nine other lunar-month names are proper nouns without shahr; some also treat Rajab like Ramadan in being named with shahr.
ELMALILI:2:185/r11.anchor: Mütebâkī dokuz ayın isimleri muharrem, safer, cumâde’l-ûlâ, cumâde’l-âhire, receb, şaban, şevvâl, zilkade, zilhicce “şehr”siz olarak

ELMALILI:2:185/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r12.speaker: Halîl
ELMALILI:2:185/r12.claim: One etymology derives Ramadan from ramḍā, a late-summer or early-autumn rain that cleanses dust; analogously, Ramadan washes believers’ sins away and purifies their hearts.
ELMALILI:2:185/r12.anchor: İmam Halîl’den nakl olunduğu üzere yaz sonunda güz mevsiminin evvelinde yağıp yeryüzünü tozdan tathir eden yağmur mânasına رَمْضَى’dan me’huzdur.

ELMALILI:2:185/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r13.claim: The majority derive Ramadan from ramad, the heat that makes stones glow: ramida means to burn walking barefoot on hot ground, evoking fasting’s heat and the burning away of sins.
ELMALILI:2:185/r13.anchor: Ekseriyet kavline göre ramazan رَمَض (ramaz)dan me’huzdur.

ELMALILI:2:185/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r14.claim: Another account says Arab month names were changed according to the seasons; this month, formerly called Nāṭiq, fell in an exceptionally hot season and received the name Ramadan.
ELMALILI:2:185/r14.anchor: Bir de deniliyor ki Arablar ayların isimlerini lügat-ı kadîmelerinden tahvil ettikleri zaman

ELMALILI:2:185/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r15.speaker: Ezherî
ELMALILI:2:185/r15.claim: Al-Azharī derives Ramadan from the verb for hammering a sword blade or arrowhead between stones to thin and sharpen it, because Arabs sharpened and prepared weapons during this month.

ELMALILI:2:185/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r16.claim: If Ramadan is truly one of God’s beautiful names, the month takes its name from it with divine mercy and the burning away of sins in view; the name evokes purification, burning, and sharpening.
ELMALILI:2:185/r16.anchor: “ramazan” isminin esmâ-i hüsnâdan olduğu sahih ise şehr-i Ramazan bizzat bununla tesmiye edilmiş ve bunda bilhassa rahmet-i ilâhiye ile günahların ihtirâkı

ELMALILI:2:185/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r17.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
ELMALILI:2:185/r17.claim: A Prophetic report describes Ramadan’s beginning as mercy, middle as forgiveness, and end as release from the Fire; the month’s most blessed night also begins the Qur’an’s descent.
ELMALILI:2:185/r17.anchor: “evveli rahmet, evsatı mağfiret, âhiri ateşten âzâtlık”

ELMALILI:2:185/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r18.claim: Al-Qur’an is God’s speech revealed specifically to Muḥammad, transmitted to us by mass transmission, and written between the two covers of the codices.
ELMALILI:2:185/r18.anchor: Peygamberimiz Muhammed Mustafa sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’e sûret-i mahsûsada inzal olunup bize tevâtüren nakledilen kelâmullâhın ismidir

ELMALILI:2:185/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r19.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads Qur’an without hamza in pause and connection, Ḥamza without hamza only in connection, and the remaining readers with hamza; the forms are linked respectively to qarn and qirāʾa.
ELMALILI:2:185/r19.anchor: İbn Kesîr kıraatinde vakıf ve vasılda ve Hamza kıraatinde yalnız vasılda hemzesiz olarak, mütebâkī kıraatlerde hemze ile okunur.

ELMALILI:2:185/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r20.claim: With hamza, Qur’an means that which is recited; without hamza, it derives from qarn and denotes parts and contents joined together, mutually confirming and coherent.
ELMALILI:2:185/r20.anchor: Hemzelisi “kıraat”ten, hemzesizi “karn” maddesindendir, hemze ile مَقْرُوء yani tilâvetle okunan

ELMALILI:2:185/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r21.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
ELMALILI:2:185/r21.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says the unhamzated Qur’an is, like Torah and Gospel, an un-derived proper name for God’s scripture.
ELMALILI:2:185/r21.anchor: İmam Şâfiî hazretleri bunun hemzesiz olarak, Tevrat, İncil gibi bilâ iştikāk ism-i kitâbullâh olduğunu söylemiştir.

ELMALILI:2:185/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r22.speaker: Katâde, Atâ
ELMALILI:2:185/r22.claim: Qatāda and ʿAṭāʾ say the earlier counted days were an initial fast of three days each month, perhaps with ʿĀshūrāʾ; they differ over whether it began voluntary or obligatory, but agree Ramadan later abrogated it completely.
ELMALILI:2:185/r22.anchor: Katâde ve Atâ bâlâdaki اَيَّاماً مَعْدُودَات’ın ramazan olmayıp savm-ı evvel, yani her aydan üç gün veya bunlarla beraber yevm-i âşûrâ’dan ibaret bulunduğuna zâhib olmuş

ELMALILI:2:185/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r23.speaker: Hazret-i Mu‘âz
ELMALILI:2:185/r23.claim: The same earlier-fast account is also attributed to Muʿādh; on it, Ramadan’s obligation is established by this verse’s command rather than by the earlier fasting passage.
ELMALILI:2:185/r23.anchor: Hazret-i Mu‘âz’ın kavli de bu olduğu söylenmiştir. Bunlara göre sıyâm-ı ramazanın delîl-i farziyeti

ELMALILI:2:185/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r24.speaker: cumhûr
ELMALILI:2:185/r24.claim: The majority hold that the earlier fast was established by Sunna and Ramadan’s obligation began with the earlier command; the counted days mean Ramadan, which this verse explains.
ELMALILI:2:185/r24.anchor: Lâkin cumhûra göre savm-ı evvel sünnet ile sâbit olmuş ve ramazan orucunun farziyeti ber vech-i bâlâ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُم âyetiyle başlamıştır.

ELMALILI:2:185/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185/r25.claim: The counted days prescribed for fasting are the blessed month of Ramadan, in which the Qur’an was sent as guidance for all humanity, with clear proofs of guidance and the Criterion.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r1.claim: Inzal means sending down at once, while tanzil means gradual descent; although the Qur’an came gradually over twenty-three years, the verse describes its descent in Ramadan.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r1.anchor: “İnzâl” def‘aten, “tenzîl” de tedrîcen indirmek demekdir. Kur’an yirmi üç senede tedrîcen tenzil buyurulmuş olduğu hâlde

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r2.speaker: Ekser müfessirîn
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r2.claim: Most exegetes, based on transmitted reports, say the Qur’an descended all at once on Laylat al-Qadr to the lowest heaven or Bayt al-Maʿmūr, then gradually to earth over twenty-three years.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r2.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin rivâyât-ı vâridesine göre Kur’an şehr-i ramazanın “Kadir Gecesi” denilen bir leyle-i mübârekesinde semâ-i dünyâya, Beyt-i Ma‘mûr’a def‘aten inzal

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r3.claim: Under this account, the Qur’anic reality manifested collectively in the created realm and nearest heaven on a Ramadan night before its descent to earth.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r3.anchor: hakīkat-i Kur’âniye arza nüzûlünden evvel âlem-i kevnde ve arza en yakın olan semâda bir ramazan gecesi toptan tecellî etmiş

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r4.speaker: Muhammed b. İshak
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r4.claim: A second interpretation, reported from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq and seeming more apparent to Elmalılı, is that Qur’an began to be revealed in Ramadan, using the whole to indicate a part.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r4.anchor: Kur’an bu ayda inzal olunmaya başladı demektir. Zikr-i kül ve irâde-i cüz kabîlinden mecaz olmakla beraber Muhammed b. İshak’tan mervî ve ma‘amâfîh zâhir gibidir.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r5.claim: On the beginning-of-revelation interpretation, the first verses of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq at Cave Ḥirāʾ were revealed on Laylat al-Qadr of Ramadan.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r5.anchor: Gār-ı Hirâ’da اِقْرَاْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ âyetinin nüzûlü ramazân-ı şerîfin Kadir gecesine müsâdif olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r6.claim: The revelation in the heat and pressure of a Ramadan night began a great divine disclosure; 2:153’s call to seek help through patience and prayer offers glad tidings to the distressed.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r6.anchor: mazmûnu üzere ne büyük bir tebşir vardır!

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r7.claim: A third reading makes the phrase mean the month in which the Qur’an was revealed; Ramadan alone among months is explicitly named in the Qur’an for divine praise, which helps explain fasting’s assignment to it.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r7.anchor: Kur’an inzal edilmiş bulunan şehr-i ramazan demektir. Fi’l-hakīka Kur’ân-ı azîmü’ş-şân’da bu mübarek aydan başka bilhassa medh-i celîl-i ilâhîye mazhar olarak ismi tasrih edilmiş bir ay yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r8.claim: Shuhud fundamentally means being present rather than absent, as do shahada and mushahada; al-shahr may be construed as an adverbial of time or as the object of witnessing.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r8.anchor: “Şuhûd” esasen “gıyâb” mukabili huzur demektir ki, “şehadet” ve “müşahede” de bu huzur cümlesindendir.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r9.claim: The phrase can mean a person residing in Ramadan, knowing it with certainty, or seeing its crescent; because time cannot literally be seen, witnessing can mean certain knowledge or sight of the crescent.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r9.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهْرَ şu mânalara muhtemildir. 1. Sizden her kim ramazanda mukīm ise onu tutsun.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r10.claim: The resident and certain-knowledge readings concern witnessing part of Ramadan, not its full duration, since the duty is to fast the entire month; the verse leaves means of knowledge unstated.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r10.anchor: şehr mânasınadır. Bu iki mânaya göre esbâb-ı ilim meskûtün anhdır.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r11.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r11.claim: Rāzī says most investigators, including Wāḥidī and the author of al-Kashshāf, choose presence in Ramadan, but he prefers certain knowledge because that reading avoids ellipsis.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r11.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Vâhidî ve sâhib-i Keşşâf gibi ekser muhakkıkīn birinci mânaya zâhib olmuşlardır. Lâkin benim indimde ikinci evlâdır.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r12.claim: The wording does not necessarily require sighting the crescent; after seeking the evidence, the means by which Ramadan is known remain unspecified here.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r12.anchor: Hulasâ burada şuhûd-ı hilâl mânası zarûrî değildir. O hâlde esbâb-ı ilim meskûtün ‘anhtır, bunu taharrî etmek lâzım gelecektir.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r13.claim: If witnessing means residence or certain knowledge and no other text applied, some would allow ijtihad about how to establish the month, including astronomical calculation.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r13.anchor: Bunun için bazıları başka nas yok zannıyla hisâbât-ı nücûmiye ile dahi amel olunabileceğine kāil olmuşlardır.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r14.speaker: cumhûr-ı eslâf
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r14.claim: The majority of early authorities reject ijtihad on this matter because other Qur’anic and Prophetic texts specify the evidence for establishing the month.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r14.anchor: Lâkin cumhûr-ı eslâfa göre başkaca nas mevcud olduğundan bu mesele mevrid-i ictihad değildir.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r15.claim: Qur’an 2:189 says crescents are time markers for people, establishing the crescent as the religious indicator of time; Prophetic reports then specify how it is observed.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r15.anchor: Bu bize kat‘iyyen gösterir ki şer‘an vakti tâyin eden delil hilâldir.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r16.claim: A Prophetic report says a month has twenty-nine days and says not to begin fasting or break it until the crescent is seen; if clouds obscure it, estimate its measure.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r16.anchor: اَلشَّهْرُ تِسْعَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ لاَ تَصُومُوا حَتَّى تَرَوْهُ وَلاَ تُفْطِرُوا حَتَّى تَرَوْهُ فَإِنْ غُمَّ عَلَيْكُمْ.

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r17.claim: A further report clarifies the instruction for cloudy weather: do not fast until the crescent is seen, and count thirty days when it is obscured.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r17.anchor: لاَ تَصُومُوا حَتَّى تَرَوُا الْهِلَاَلَ فَإِنْ غُمَّ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاقْدُرُوا ثَلَاَثِينَ

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r18.claim: Another report directs people to fast and end the fast upon sighting; if cloud or haze blocks the view, they should count thirty.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r18.anchor: صُومُوا لِرُؤْيَتِهِ وَأَفْطِرُوا لِرُؤْيَتِهِ فَإِنْ حَالَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَنْظَرِهِ سَحَابٌ أَوْ قَتَرَةٌ فَعُدُّوا ثَلَاَثِينَ

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r19.claim: Another report says to begin Ramadan upon sighting, complete Shaʿbān to thirty if cloud or fog intervenes, and not to preempt Ramadan with a fast on a day of Shaʿbān.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r19.anchor: صُومُوا رَمَضَانَ لِرُؤْيَتِهِ فَإِنْ حَالَ بَيْنَكُمْ غَمَامَةٌ أَوْ ضَبَابَةٌ فَأَكْمِلُوا عِدَّةَ شَهْرِ شَعْبَانَ ثَلَاَثِينَ

ELMALILI:2:185#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r20.claim: A final report says months are sometimes thirty and sometimes twenty-nine days: fast and break upon sighting, and count thirty when the sky is cloudy.
ELMALILI:2:185#2/r20.anchor: اَلشَّهْرُ هٰكَذَا وَهٰكَذَا الخ: yani ay kâh otuz ve kâh yirmi dokuz olur.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r1.claim: Sound hadiths explain the legally valid grounds for establishing the month's sighting, in agreement with 2:189; the matter leaves no room for independent legal opinion.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r1.anchor: İşte bunlar ve emsâli ehâdîs-i sahîha يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْأَهِلَّةِ قُلْ هِىَ مَوَٰقِيتُ âyetine mutâbık olarak

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r2.claim: The month is legally measured as thirty days from a new moon; when it is twenty-nine days, the new moon's sighting is the required proof.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r2.anchor: şer‘an bir hilâlden itibaren şehrin mikyâs-ı aslîsi otuz gündür. Otuzun tamam olduğu mâlum olunca başkaca hiçbir delîle ihtiyaç yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r3.claim: Establishing a twenty-nine-day month rests on sighting the new moon, a direct observational knowledge rather than inferential knowledge.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r3.anchor: Bu delil rü’yet-i hilâldir, yani ilm-i istidlâlî değil ilm-i şuhûdîdir.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r4.claim: The general address to believers means that a ruling established for one person in these divine rights extends to the community.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r4.anchor: bu gibi ahkâm-ı şer‘iye ve hukūk-ı ilâhiyede vâhid üzere hüküm, cemaat üzere hükümdür

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r5.claim: Once one believer's sighting establishes fasting as obligatory, it applies by implication to others; private testimony binds its hearers, while court-established public testimony binds everyone.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r5.anchor: Bu vücûb ve sübût ise ancak o mü’minin şuhûd ve şehâdetiyle olur. Bu şehadet, ferdî surette ise vücûb yalnız işitenlere sirâyet eder.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r6.claim: Fasting is solely God's right, while breaking the fast and Eid concern human rights; human-rights cases require at least two upright witnesses, but a solitary upright report can establish Ramadan.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r6.anchor: Savm مَحْض حَقُّ اللّٰهّٰ (mahz-ı hakkullah) iftar ve bayram hakk-ı abddir.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r7.speaker: eimme-i Hanefiyye
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r7.claim: The Hanafi imams accept one upright witness for Ramadan and two for Shawwal or Dhul Hijjah when the sky is obstructed; with clear skies, they require a numerous testimony that yields knowledge.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r7.anchor: eimme-i Hanefiyye bi’l-ittifak demişlerdir ki semâda bir illet bulunduğu, yani hava açık olmadığı zaman şevvâl ve zilhicce için lâekal iki âdilin, ramazan için yalnız âdil bir adamın dahi şehâdeti kabul edilebilirse de

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r8.claim: On the twenty-ninth, believers must search for the new moon; if many search under a clear sky, a few witnesses contradicted by the healthy observers' failure to see it are ordinarily implausible.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r8.anchor: Zira ayın yirmi dokuzuncu günü taharrî-i hilâl umûm mü’minlere farzdır.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r9.claim: A clear sky and a proper communal search can discredit a few claims as error, illusion, or deliberate falsehood; this protects a commonly needed religious matter from confusion caused by solitary reports.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r9.anchor: Bu bir asl-ı sahîhdir, akıllar sıhhatine hükm eyler ve emr-i şerî‘atın mebnâsı da bunun üzerinedir. Bunda hata büyük zarara bâ‘is olur.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r10.claim: Hanafi jurists require widely transmitted, knowledge-producing reports for matters everyone needs to know, rather than solitary reports.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r10.anchor: eimme-i Hanefiyye ahkâm-ı şer‘iyeden umûm nâsın bilmeye muhtaç bulunduğu husûsâtın tarîk-i sübûtu istifâza ve mûcib-i ilm olan haberler olabileceğine

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r11.claim: When an obstruction clouds the sky, outward circumstances no longer contradict the accepted testimony: one upright witness suffices for Ramadan and two for Eid.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r11.anchor: semâda illet bulunduğu zaman böyle zâhir-i hâlin tekzîbi olamayacağından hakkullah olan ramazanda bir, hukūk-ı ‘ibâd olan bayramlarda iki âdilin şehâdetini tekzib etmeye de hak yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r12.claim: The apparent contradiction applies only when believers collectively search; later jurists facing lax searches set aside the large-crowd condition and accepted two upright witnesses unconditionally, as other schools did.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r12.anchor: Müteahhirîn bu derekeye düştükleri için cemm-i gafîr şartından sarf-ı nazar ederek diğer mezheblerde olduğu gibi ‘ale’l-ıtlâk iki şâhid-i âdil ile iktifâya lüzûm hissetmişlerdi.

ELMALILI:2:185#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r13.claim: Because fasting is an individual duty for all, the month is established for all through possible communal moon sighting, or completion of thirty days; searching on the twenty-ninth is at least a communal obligation.
ELMALILI:2:185#3/r13.anchor: şer‘an şehrin sebeb-i sübûtu da umum için mümkin olan şuhûd-ı hilâle, olmadığı hâlde otuz mikyâsına rabt edilmiştir. Binâen‘aleyh ayın yirmi dokuzunda taharrî-i hilâl de umûma lâekal farz-ı kifâye olarak farzdır.

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r1.claim: Astronomical months between conjunctions or new moons are fractional, averaging twenty-nine and a half days, while fasting is measured in whole days; this calculation is not the legal month standard.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r1.anchor: ictimâ‘veya iki hilâl beynindeki şehr-i nücûmî yirmi dokuzla otuz arasında dâima kesirlidir. Vasatîsi ise yirmi dokuz buçuk gün eder.

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r2.claim: Astronomical determination of the new moon is inferential knowledge, which may count in inferential matters but not where the law requires direct sighting.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r2.anchor: hisâb-ı nücûmî ile idrâk-i hilâl, ilm-i şuhûdî değil ilm-i istidlâlîdir. Binâen‘aleyh istidlâl mevki‘lerinde şer‘an dahi muteber olsa da şuhûd mevki‘inde olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r3.claim: Making astronomy the criterion would force lay Muslims to rely on experts for fasting and deprive them of direct observation; making astronomy basic obligatory learning for everyone conflicts with Islam's universal ease.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r3.anchor: avam taklîde cebredilmiş ve farîza-i savmiyelerini edâ için ibâdetinde behemehâl havâssın vesâtatına mecbur kılınmış ve ilm-i şuhûdî zevkinden mahrum edilmiş olur.

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r4.claim: The conjunction is hidden and relative, while the new moon's sighting is its outward sign; in religious matters, an outward sign must stand in for what is hidden.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r4.anchor: ictimâ‘-i neyyireyn umûr-ı hafiyye ve izâfiyedendir. Bunun delîl-i zâhirîsi şuhûd-ı hilâldir. Şer‘an umûr-ı hafiyyede bir şeyin delîli o şey makāmına ikāme olunacağından

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r5.claim: If calculation were the standard, the criterion would be the conjunction's occurrence and completion rather than the moon's visibility, leaving sighting without scientific or legal meaning.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r5.anchor: hesab esas ittihaz olunduğu takdirde itibar hilâlin zuhûruna değil, ictimâ‘ın vukū‘ve hitâmına olmak lâzım gelir. Binâen‘aleyh hesab nokta-i nazarından rü’yet-i hilâl itibârının ne fennen ne şer‘an bir mânası olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r6.claim: The absence of a text validating astronomical calculation for fasting reflects its unsuitability as a universal standard, not a judgment that astronomy is worthless.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r6.anchor: Bu gibi hikmetlere mebnî hisâb-ı nücûma itibar hakkında bir nas vârid olmamıştır. Bu da fennin ‘ale’l-ıtlâk kıymetsizliğinden değil

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r7.claim: Instead of making astronomy obligatory, Muslims should build observatories that help everyone observe the new moon on sacred days.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r7.anchor: senenin bazı mukaddes günlerinde Müslümanlara taharrî-i hilâli teshil edecek rasadhâneler yaparak herkesin bu zevkleri tatması için teşvîkātta bulunmak elbette daha güzeldir.

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r8.claim: Valid testimony conveys direct observational knowledge and must not be contradicted by outward circumstances; astronomical calculation can be a better safeguard than trusting a few potentially corrupt witnesses.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r8.anchor: Yoksa hiç kimse şüphe etmez ki para için din ve vicdânını satıp yalan yere şehadet edebilecek birkaç fâsıkın ihbârına itimad etmekten ise hesab ile amel etmek evlâdır.

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r9.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r9.claim: The Prophet forbade greeting Ramadan with a fast on the final day of Sha'ban; false reports that lead to fasting on known Sha'ban or celebrating Eid during Ramadan are sinful, so caution is needed.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r9.anchor: Peygamberimiz şabanın son günü orucuyla ramazan karşılamayı da nehiy buyurduğu için şaban olduğu mâlum bulunan bir günde yalan bir haber ile oruç tutmak veya ramazan olan bir günde yalan bir haber ile bayram yapmak da günah olacağından

ELMALILI:2:185#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r10.claim: When mass testimony is absent, astronomical calculation should serve as an apparent circumstance for assessing witnesses in the present age, while Muslims retain their duty to search for the moon.
ELMALILI:2:185#4/r10.anchor: cemm-i gafîrin şehâdeti bulunmadığı zaman dinlenecek şâhidler hakkında hisâb-ı nücûmîyi zâhir-i hâl gibi muteber tutmak zamanımızın hâline muvâfık olacaktır ve Müslüman olanlar her hâlde hilâli taharrî etmek farîzasını unutmamalıdırlar.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r1.claim: The duty to fast begins when part of Ramadan is witnessed: sight the moon on the twenty-ninth, or complete thirty days; fasting is then obligatory for every accountable resident believer.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r1.anchor: savmın sebeb-i vücûbu şuhûd-ı şehr, daha doğrusu şuhûd-ı cüz’-i şehrdir. Yirmi dokuzda rü’yet-i hilâl ile, bu olmadığı takdirde tekmîl-i selâsîn ile

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r2.claim: A seriously ill person or traveler may break the Ramadan fast and must make up the same number of days later; making them up incurs no sin.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r2.anchor: bunların orucu da ramazandan başka günlerden sayısıncadır. Yani bunlara ramazanda ruhsat vardır, tutmayabilirler ve tutmazlarsa diğer günlerde adedi adedine kazâ etmeye borçludurlar.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r3.claim: Healthy residents have no such concession; leaving the fast for make-up later is sinful, and deliberate breaking requires both make-up and expiation.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r3.anchor: mukīm ve sahih olanlara bu ruhsat yoktur, onlar kazâya bırakırsa farzı terk etmekle âsim olurlar. Ve ‘amden nakz ettikleri takdirde kazâdan başka keffâret de lâzım gelir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r4.claim: The verse repeats illness and travel exemptions after making Ramadan fasting definitive so readers will not assume that the earlier excuses have ceased to count.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r4.anchor: mazeretlerin itibardan sukūtu tevehhüm olunmamak için maraz ve sefer mazeret ve ruhsatları da tekrar zikredilmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r10.claim: God does not intend hardship through fasting; when illness or travel makes fasting difficult, the concession to break the fast supplies ease and averts harm and hardship.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r10.anchor: Allah böyle orucu farz kılmakla sizi zora, sıkıntıya giriftâr etmek istemez, bilakis size kolaylık vermek ister. Maraz ve seferde savm ise bazen ‘usret olabilir

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r11.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r11.claim: A Prophetic hadith says that a person who forgetfully eats, drinks, or has intercourse after intending to fast does not invalidate the fast; this concession is called God's hospitality.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r11.anchor: oruca niyet edip de oruçlu olduğunu unutarak yiyip içen veya mu‘âmele-i zevciye yapan nâsînin orucu bozulmayacağı hadîs-i nebevîde beyan buyurulmuş ve buna “ziyâfetullah” ıtlak edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r13.claim: Fidya is ease for people whose permanent weakness would make make-up fasting a hardship.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r13.anchor: Çünkü bunlar için kazâ dahi bir ‘usret olacağından yüsr fidye suretindedir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r14.claim: Fasting trains believers in self-discipline and patience, helps them overcome life's hardships, and leads to felicity in the hereafter.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r14.anchor: Oruçla kolay kolay mücâhede-i nefse alışılacak, lüzûmunda sabır yolları öğrenilecek, metâ‘ib-i hayat yenilecek, sa‘âdet-i uhreviyeye erişilecektir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r15.speaker: Zâhiriyye
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r15.claim: The Zahirites read the verses as requiring travelers to break the fast and make it up later, by analogy with shortening prayer; they cite the hadith that fasting on a journey is not piety.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r15.anchor: Zâhiriyye bu âyetlerin zâhirine bakarak seferde kasr-ı salât gibi seferde iftâr-ı savmın vücûbuna bile kāil olmuşlar, “müsâfir olana başka günlerde oruç tutmak farzdır” demişler

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r16.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r16.claim: On the basis of that view, Abu Hurayra says a traveler who fasts must still make the days up; Elmalılı calls this position anomalous.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r16.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre radıyallahu ‘anh dahi buna binâen “seferde sâim olana yine kazâ lâzım gelir” demiştir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r17.speaker: bütün sahâbe ve tâbiîn ve fukahâ
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r17.claim: All other Companions, Successors, and jurists agree that fasting during travel is permissible and entails no make-up if completed.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r17.anchor: bütün sahâbe ve tâbiîn ve fukahâ seferde savmın namaz gibi olmayıp câiz olduğunda ve tutarsa kazâ lâzım gelmeyeceğinde müttefiktirler.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r18.speaker: Ebû Saîd-i Hudrî, Enes b. Mâlik, Câbir b. Abdullah, Ebü’d-Derdâ, Seleme b. Muhabbık ve İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r18.claim: These Companions transmit widely attested reports that the Prophet himself fasted while traveling, countering Abu Hurayra's view.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r18.anchor: Ebû Saîd-i Hudrî, Enes b. Mâlik, Câbir b. Abdullah, Ebü’d-Derdâ, Seleme[^31] b. Muhabbık ve İbn Abbas radıyallâhu ‘anhüm seferde sıyâm-ı nebevîyi rivayet eylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r19.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r19.claim: When Hamza b. Amr al-Aslami said he fasted while traveling, the Prophet told him he could either fast or break his fast.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r19.anchor: Risâletmeâb Efendimiz’in “إِنْ شِئْتَ فَصُمْ وَإِنْ شِئْتَ فَأَفْطِرْ: dilersen tut dilersen ye”

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r20.speaker: Hamza, Urve b. Zübeyr ve Ebû Merâvih
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r20.claim: Hamza, Urwa b. al-Zubayr, and Abu Marawih practiced continuous fasting both at home and while traveling.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r20.anchor: Müşârün ileyh Hamza ve Urve b. Zübeyr ve Ebû Merâvih sefer ve hazarda savm-ı dehr tutarlardı.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r21.claim: Neither this verse nor its sick-and-traveler concession proves that either group is obliged to break the fast.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r21.anchor: Bu âyetlerde ise marîz ve müsâfire iftarın vücûbuna delâlet yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r22.claim: The hadith that fasting during travel is not piety applies only to particular circumstances, rather than forbidding travel fasting generally.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r22.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh لَيْسَ مِنَ الْبِرِّ الصِّيَامُ فِي السَّفَرِ hadîsi de bazı ahvâl-i mahsûsaya maksurdur.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r23.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r23.claim: During the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet and Companions fasted while traveling in Ramadan; as they approached the enemy, he ordered them to break their fast for strength.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r23.anchor: sonra Resûlullah “düşmanınıza yaklaştınız, fıtır sizin için daha kuvvetlidir, binâen‘aleyh iftar ediniz” buyurdu.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r24.speaker: Ebû Saîd-i Hudrî
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r24.claim: Abu Sa'id says that before the Prophet's order to break the fast, he had been fasting alongside him.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r24.anchor: Ebû Saîd-i Hudrî “Vallahi ben bu emirden evvel görüyordum ki Resûlullah ile beraber tutuyordum” demiştir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r25.claim: The order to break the fast came after ten Ramadan days had passed, at Kedid between Usfan and Amij, situating the hadith in a specific case.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r26.claim: Travel fasting is not forbidden and may even be preferable under the general wording that fasting is better for you in 2:184.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r26.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh seferde oruç memnû‘değil, belki وَأَن تَصُومُوا۟ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ ıtlâkiyle efdaldir bile.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r27.speaker: Hazret-i Enes
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r27.claim: Anas says that when this verse was revealed, travelers went hungry and were not sated at camp, yet later they traveled and stopped fed; he ordered his servant to fast while traveling.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r27.anchor: Hazret-i Enes de “Biz وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ âyeti nâzil olduğu vakit seferlerimizde ac acına gider ve konduğumuz zaman da karnımız doymazdı

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r28.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r28.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r28.claim: The travel concession serves ease; unlike shortening prayer, it does not impose a decisive duty to break the fast.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r28.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah’ın bu ruhsatı teysir içindir, seferdeki salât gibi azîmet mânasında değildir.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r29.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r29.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r29.claim: Since it is agreed that a sick person is not obliged to break the fast, the Zahirite claim that a traveler must break it is untenable.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r29.anchor: Marîz için iftarın vâcib olmadığı müttefekun ‘aleyh iken Zâhiriyye’nin seferde iftarı vâcib addetmesi doğru olamaz.

ELMALILI:2:185#5/r30.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r30.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r30.claim: Sometimes fasting on time with everyone is easier for a sick person or traveler than making up the days alone later; obliging them to break fast would oppose God's intent of ease.
ELMALILI:2:185#5/r30.anchor: Zaman olur ki marîz ve müsâfir için vaktinde herkesle beraber edâen tutmak bilâhare yalnız kazâen tutmaktan daha ‘usretli olabilir, bu da irâde-i yüsre muhalif olur.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r1.speaker: Ebû Bekir Şu‘be ve Ya‘kūb
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r1.claim: Shuʿba's transmission from ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read the verb with fatḥ on kāf and doubled mīm, in the sense of completing the count.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r1.anchor: Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir Şu‘be rivayeti ve Ya‘kūb kıraatinde kâf’ın fethi ve mîm’in teşdîdiyle وَلِتُكَمِّلُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r2.claim: God wills ease, and requires completing the number of fasting days through performance or make-up fasting.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r2.anchor: Hâsılı Allah yüsr ister, bir de {وَلِتُكْمِلُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ} şehrin aded-i eyyâmına göre edâen veya kazâen savmın adedini ikmal eylemenizi

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r3.claim: The commands seek magnification and reverence of God with praise for His guidance, and the gratitude expected of believers.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r3.anchor: size hidâyet etmesine veya hidâyet ettiğine hamd ederek Allah’a tekbir ve tâziminizi

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r4.claim: On his preferred syntactic connection, the lām is not causal: the sense is that God wills you to complete the count, like the lām in 5:6 and 61:8.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r4.anchor: Bu rabta göre وَيُرِيدُ لِتُكْمِلُوا,وَلِتُكْمِلُوا۟ demektir ki “lâm”lar ta‘lîl olmayıp يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ [el-Mâide 5/6], يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِـُٔوا۟ [es-Saff 61/8] âyetlerindeki “lâm”lar gibidir.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r5.speaker: sâhib-i Keşşâf
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r5.claim: Al-Kashshāf says reading the lām as causal, with an implied “He prescribed all this,” gives the ending a subtler and more eloquent structure.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r6.claim: The count is measured by individual days: each day's fast has its own cause, so make-up fasting matches missed days rather than requiring the whole month.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r6.anchor: Aded her günün kendi orucuna sebeb ve mi‘yâr olduğunu gösterir.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r7.claim: Because the verse says to complete the count rather than the month, someone who misses several Ramadan fasts need not make up the entire month; the month's days are not one fast.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r7.anchor: ramazanda birkaç oruç yiyen kimsenin bütün şehri kazâ etmesi lâzım gelmez.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r8.claim: Since the duty can change during the month, a minor reaching puberty becomes obligated, while one who loses the conditions of obligation is released.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r8.anchor: ramazanın içinde tehavvül-i teklif muteberdir. Ortasında bâliğ olanlar mükellef olduğu gibi, şerâit-i teklîfi zâyi‘edenlerden de sâkıt olur.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r9.claim: A resident who begins Ramadan and travels during it receives the travel concession, but the day on which he departs while fasting is not included.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r9.anchor: ramazan bidâyetinde mukīm olan kimse ramazan içinde sefere çıkarsa yine ruhsata mazhardır. Ancak oruçlu olarak çıktığı günü bu ruhsata dâhil olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r10.claim: A single intention at the month's beginning can still make the whole month's fast valid, because witnessing Ramadan is a general cause of obligation.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r10.anchor: evvelinden tamamına bir niyet ile de oruç sahih olabilir. Çünkü şuhûd-ı şehr bir sebeb-i icmâlîdir.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r11.claim: Magnifying God means reverence expressed in belief, speech, and action: affirming divine unity and justice, confessing His names and attributes, and worshipping through commanded acts.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r11.anchor: “Allah’ı tekbîr”, esasen Allah’a tâzim demektir ki üç mâna ile olur: ‘Akd-i kalb, kavl, amel.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r12.claim: Speech and deeds are accepted only when grounded in faith; 17:19 likewise conditions a deed's being thanked upon the worker being a believer.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r12.anchor: meşkûriyyet-i sa‘y, mü’min olmak hâliyle takyid edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r13.claim: Because faith underlies every worship and other acts have causes unrelated to Ramadan, the contextual takbir is an uttered glorification marking completion of the Ramadan count and Eid.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r13.anchor: bu tekbîrin aded-i ramazanı ikmâle müte‘allik olarak bayrama işaret olması ve buna evlâ olan da lafz-ı tekbîrin izhar edilmesidir.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r14.claim: The phrase “upon what He guided you to” carries an implicit sense of praise, which explains why takbir is joined to God with ʿalā.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r14.anchor: Bu âyette tekbîrin عَلَىٰ ile sılalanması da ma‘nâ-yı hamdin tazmînine mebnî olduğundan buna pek münâsibdir.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r15.claim: The verse may concern takbir at sighting the Shawwal crescent, while going to Eid prayer, or during its takbirs; it does not specifically select one or establish loudness as obligatory.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r16.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly said Muslims should takbir upon seeing the Shawwal crescent and continue until their Eid celebration is over, citing the verse.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r16.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden rivayet olunuyor ki: “Müslümanlar şevvâl hilâline baktıklarında bayramlarından fâriğ oluncaya kadar tekbir almaları üzerlerine

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r17.speaker: Hazret-i Ali, Ebû Katâde, İbn Ömer, Saîd b. Müseyyeb, Urve, Kāsım, Hârice b. Zeyd, Nâfi‘ b. Cübeyr b. Mut‘im and other Companions
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r17.claim: Reports say these Companions and early Muslims took takbir when setting out for the prayer ground on Eid.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r17.anchor: Hazret-i Ali, Ebû Katâde, İbn Ömer, Saîd b. Müseyyeb, Urve, Kāsım, Hârice b. Zeyd ve Nâfi‘b. Cübeyr b. Mut‘im vesâir ashâb-ı kirâmdan dahi mervîdir

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r18.speaker: Şu‘be
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r18.claim: Shuʿba said that when he took Ibn ʿAbbās to the prayer ground, Ibn ʿAbbās questioned the crowd's takbir and asked whether the imam had begun it.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r18.anchor: Ebû Bekir Râzî Ahkâmü’l-Kur’ân’da bunları naklederken der ki: “İbn Abbas’ın mevlâsı Şu‘be şöyle demiştir:

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r19.claim: Elmalılı infers that Ibn ʿAbbās disliked takbir on the route and understood the verse as the imam's takbir in the sermon, which others may join; the crescent report does not require loudness.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r19.anchor: Bundan anlaşılır ki İbn Abbas tarîk-i musallâda tekbîri hoş görmemiştir

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r20.claim: The preferred Hanafi position makes none of these takbirs obligatory; a quiet takbir at the Eid crescent is recommended, and takbir on the way to Eid prayer is sunnah, quiet for Ramadan Eid and aloud for Sacrifice Eid.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r20.anchor: mezheb-i Hanefî’de muhtâr olan şudur ki bu tekbirlerin hiçbiri vâcib değildir.

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r21.claim: If the verse implies an obligatory takbir at Eid's arrival, Elmalılı says it can mean the Eid prayer and its takbirs: complete Ramadan, glorify God, and pray Eid.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r21.anchor: Şu hâlde hâsıl-ı ma‘nâ: “Ramazanı ikmal edip tekbir alarak bayram namazını

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r22.claim: The closing gratitude points especially to celebrating Eid as thanksgiving and connects the fasting passage with the earlier commands to eat and give thanks in 2:172.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r22.anchor: Ve bu suretle farîza-i sıyâmın tâ yukarıdaki كُلُوا وَاشْكُرُوا [bk. el-Bakara 2/172] emirlerine tenâsuku

ELMALILI:2:185#6/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r23.claim: Elmalılı says the verse's linked clauses contain arguments that refute the Jabriyya.
ELMALILI:2:185#6/r23.anchor: bu âyette Cebriyye mezhebini ibtal edecek deliller vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r1.claim: Earlier verses prepared believers for fasting by specifying its days and concessions; this verse supplies details, and the complementary verses do not abrogate one another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r1.anchor: birbirini tamamlayan âyetler arasında bir nesih (birinin diğerini hükümsüz kılması) ilişkisi yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s revelation to Muhammad began in the Hira cave in Mecca on Ramadan 27, 610 CE, and was completed over about 23 years at intervals God deemed fitting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r2.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in Hz. Peygamber’e indirilmesi Mekke’de Hira mağarasında, milâdî 610 yılı Ramazan ayının 27. gününde başlamış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r3.claim: The verse means the Qur’an’s first verses, not the entire Qur’an, were sent down in Ramadan; scripture can call a part by the name Book or Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r3.anchor: “ramazan ayında Kur’an’ın indirilmesi”nden maksat onun tamamının değil ilk âyetlerinin indirilmesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r4.claim: God chose as the fasting month the month in which He began revealing the final guide and means of guidance for all humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r4.anchor: bütün insanlığa son rehber ve irşad aracı kıldığı kitabını vahyetmeye başladığı ayı oruç zamanı olarak seçmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r5.claim: Shahida here means to reach or be present in the month, not to see it.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r6.claim: Thus the verse does not say that whoever sees the Ramadan crescent must fast.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r6.anchor: âyetin, “Ramazan hilâlini gören oruç tutsun” şeklinde bir mânası yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r7.claim: Hadiths establish beginning the fast at the entry crescent, ending it and celebrating Eid at the exit crescent, and completing the prior month to thirty days if clouds prevent sighting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r7.anchor: Kamerî aylardan biri olan ramazanın giriş hilâlini görünce oruca başlanması, çıkış hilâlini görünce de oruca son verilip bayram yapılması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r8.claim: A 1978 Istanbul meeting of Islamic-country representatives approved calendars based on the crescent becoming visible somewhere in the world and observatory checks of the calculation; countries adopting it achieved unity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r8.anchor: 1978 yılında İstanbul’da İslâm ülkeleri temsilcilerinin katılımıyla yapılan ilmî bir toplantıda ramazan ve bayram hilâllerinin, dünyanın herhangi bir yerinde görülebilir hale gelmesine dayalı hesaplar ve buna uygun takvim yapılmasına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r9.claim: The author endorses the decisions and their religious and scientific grounds, and advises people in Turkey to follow the Diyanet calendar rather than be confused by reports of impossible sightings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r9.anchor: Türkiye’de yaşayanlara, alınan kararlara titizlikle uyan Diyanet İşleri Başkanlığı’nın takvimine uymalarını, etrafı dinleyerek kafalarını karıştırmamalarını tavsiye ediyoruz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r10.speaker: bazı tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r10.claim: Some exegetes say the sick-and-traveler concession is repeated to prevent people from thinking the removal of the fasting-or-fidya option also removed other concessions; sick people and travelers still make up the fast later.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r10.anchor: “oruç tutmakla fidye vermek arasında muhayyer bırakma” hükmünün bu âyetle kaldırılmış olmasından dolayı diğer ruhsatların da kaldırıldığı zannını engellemektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r11.claim: The author rejects abrogation among these verses: people struggling to fast retain the fidya option, and the sick-and-traveler concessions are repeated to show they too remain in force.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r11.anchor: Oruç tutmakta zorlananların fidye verme imkânları devam etmektedir. Burada iki geçici mazeretin tekrar zikredilmesinin sebebi, onların da neshedilmediğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r12.claim: Takbir means embracing God’s greatness in the heart and expressing it verbally; Allahu akbar means God is greatest and most exalted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r12.anchor: Allah’ın ululuğunu gönülden benimseyip dile getirmeye tekbir denir. “Allahü ekber” cümlesiyle ifade edilen tekbirin mânası “Allah en uludur, en büyüktür” demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r13.claim: Takbir acknowledges God’s unity and uniqueness: anything less than the greatest has a defect or limitation and cannot be God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r13.anchor: Bu cümle aynı zamanda Allah’ın birlik, teklik ve eşsizliğinin itirafıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r14.claim: Takbir at the start of prayer, bowing, prostration, and sacrifice declares that worship belongs to God alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r14.anchor: Namaza başlarken, rükûya ve secdeye giderken, kurban keserken tekbir getiren müminler, bununla ibadetin ancak Allah’a yapılacağını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r15.claim: Eid prayers and sermons include takbir for the same reason, and takbir is also said after obligatory prayers on the days of Tashriq.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:185/r15.anchor: Ramazan ayını oruçlu geçiren, kurban bayramında kurban ibadetini yerine getiren müslümanların bayram namazına giderken ve bayram namazını kılarken tekbir getirmeleri

NAHHAS:v1p286/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r1.claim: The common reading has «شهر» in the nominative; Mujāhid and Shahr ibn Ḥawshab read it in the accusative.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r1.anchor: حكيت فيه ستة أوجه ( شهر رمضان ) قراءة العامة وقرأ مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب ( شهر رمضان ) بالنصب

NAHHAS:v1p286/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r2.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v1p286/r2.claim: A reading attributed to al-Hasan and Abū ʿAmr assimilates the two rāʾs; Abū Jaʿfar rejects it because two quiescent consonants would meet.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r2.anchor: وحكي عن الحسن وأبي عمرو إدغام الراء في الراء وهذا لا يجوز لئلا يجتمع ساكنان

NAHHAS:v1p286/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v1p286/r4.claim: The Kufans allow shifting the rāʾ's vowel to the preceding hāʾ, which then takes ḍamma.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r4.anchor: الوجه الخامس أن تقلب حركة الراء على الهاء فتضم الهاء وهذا قول الكوفيين

NAHHAS:v1p286/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r5.speaker: امروء القيس
NAHHAS:v1p286/r5.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line «فليس بنا سينا» illustrates the vowel transfer discussed for the reading.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r5.anchor: امروء القيس ( فمن كان ينسانا وحسن بلائنا … فليس بنا سينا على حالة بكر )

NAHHAS:v1p286/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r6.claim: A reading with «شهر» is also explained by shifting the rāʾ's vowel to hāʾ or by dialect forms such as «حلم/لحم» and «نهر/نهر».
NAHHAS:v1p286/r6.anchor: ويجوز شهر رمضان من جهتين إحداهما على قراءة من نصب فقلب حركة الراء على الهاء

NAHHAS:v1p286/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r7.claim: The nominative «شهر» begins a nominal clause whose predicate is «الذي أنزل فيه القرآن»; it may instead be an independent subject with an implied start such as “the fast prescribed for you.”
NAHHAS:v1p286/r7.anchor: شهر رمضان رفع بالابتداء وخبره ( الذي أنزل فيه القرآن ) ويجوز أن يكون شهر مرفوعا على إضمار ابتداء

NAHHAS:v1p286/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r8.claim: «رمضان» is diptote because its nūn is augmentative.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r8.anchor: ورمضان لا ينصرف لأن النون فيه زائدة

NAHHAS:v1p286/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r9.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v1p286/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī construes the accusative as “fasting was prescribed for you, that you fast the month of Ramadan.”
NAHHAS:v1p286/r9.anchor: قال الكسائي المعنى كتب عليكم الصيام وأن تصوموا شهر رمضان

NAHHAS:v1p286/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r10.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p286/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ similarly understands “fasting was prescribed for you, meaning that you fast the month of Ramadan.”
NAHHAS:v1p286/r10.anchor: قال الفراء أي كتب عليكم الصيام أي أن تصوموا شهر رمضان

NAHHAS:v1p286/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r11.claim: Abū Jaʿfar rejects governing «شهر» by «تصوموا» or «الصيام» because that would split a relative clause from its antecedent; an exhortative object is possible but remote since the month was not previously mentioned.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r11.anchor: لا يجوز أن تنصب شهر رمضان بتصوموا لأنه يدخل في الصلة ثم يفرق بين الصلة والموصول

NAHHAS:v1p286/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r12.claim: «هدى للناس وبينات» is accusative as a circumstantial from «القرآن», which is passive subject.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r12.anchor: ( هدى للناس وبينات ) في موضع نصب على الحال من القرآن والقرآن اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

NAHHAS:v1p286/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r13.claim: The question about the benefit of “whoever witnesses the month” is answered by treating the month as a time adverb: whoever is in town during it.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r13.anchor: يقال ما الفائدة في هذا والحاضر والمسافر يشهدان الشهر فالجواب أن الشهر ليس بمفعول وإنما هو ظرف زمان

NAHHAS:v1p286/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r14.claim: A second interpretation supplies “not traveling or ill” after the phrase.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r14.anchor: وجواب آخر أن يكون التقدير فمن شهد منكم الشهر غير مسافر ولا مريض

NAHHAS:v1p286/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r15.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v1p286/r15.claim: Al-Hasan reads the imperative lām with kasra, whether it begins a phrase or follows another word; the sukun reading drops the heavy kasra.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r15.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( فليصمه ) وكان يكسر لام الأمر كانت مبتدأة أو كان قبلها شيء

NAHHAS:v1p286/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r16.claim: «كان» has an implicit subject; «مريضا» is its predicate, and «على سفر» coordinates as “or traveling.”
NAHHAS:v1p286/r16.anchor: اسم كان فيها مضمر ومريضا خبره أو على سفر عطف أي أو مسافرا

NAHHAS:v1p286/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r17.claim: The phrase states the number of replacement days for the sick or traveler.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r17.anchor: فعدة من أيام أخر يريد الله بكم اليسر

NAHHAS:v1p286/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r18.anchor: واليسر واليسر لغتان وكذا العسر والعسر

NAHHAS:v1p286/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r19.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p286/r19.claim: Al-Akhfash treats «ولتكمّلوا» as coordinated to “God wills,” supplying an implied conjunction of purpose.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r19.anchor: فيه خمسة أقوال قال الأخفش هو معطوف أي ويريد ولتكملوا العدة

NAHHAS:v1p286/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r20.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v1p286/r20.claim: Another analysis says God wills this easing so that you complete the count.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r20.anchor: وقال غيره يريد الله هذا التخفيف لتكملوا العدة

NAHHAS:v1p286/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r21.claim: A third analysis treats the wāw as extra.

NAHHAS:v1p286/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r22.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p286/r22.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the meaning to be that God did this so you complete the count; Abū Jaʿfar calls this a good analysis.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r22.anchor: وقال الفراء المعنى ولتكملوا العدة فعل هذا قال أبو جعفر وهذا قول حسن

NAHHAS:v1p286/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r23.speaker: إبراهيم بن السري
NAHHAS:v1p286/r23.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarīʾ links the phrase by meaning: God did this to make matters easy for you and so you complete the count.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r23.anchor: ذكره أبو إسحاق إبراهيم بن السري قال هو محمول على المعنى والتقدير فعل الله ذلك ليسهل عليكم ولتكملوا العدة

NAHHAS:v1p286/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p286/r24.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p286/r24.claim: The meaning-based construction is compared to God showing Abraham the dominion of the heavens and earth so he might be among the certain.
NAHHAS:v1p286/r24.anchor: ومثله ( وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين )

BAQILLANI:v1p32/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r1.claim: Arabic permits eloquent forms that cannot all be realized in Persian or other languages, supporting the Qur'an's distinctive form.
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r1.anchor: الشعر لا يتأتى في تلك الألسنة على ما قد اتفق في العربية وإن كان قد يتفق منها صنف أو أصناف ضيقة

BAQILLANI:v1p32/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r2.speaker: المجوس
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r2.claim: The Magians claim that the books of Zoroaster and Mani are inimitable.
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r2.anchor: فإن المجوس تزعم أن كتاب زرادشت وكتاب ماني معجزان

BAQILLANI:v1p32/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r3.claim: Mani's accounts of sorcery and magical tricks do not constitute inimitability.
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r3.anchor: الذي يتضمنه ماني من طرق النسيرنجات وضروب من الشعوذة ليس يقع فيها إعجاز

BAQILLANI:v1p32/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r4.claim: The wisdom sayings in Mani's book circulate across nations and are not the exclusive property of any community.
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r4.anchor: ويزعمون أن في الكتاب الحكم وهي حكم منقولة متداولة على الألسن لا تختص بها أمة دون أمة

BAQILLANI:v1p32/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r5.claim: The works cited as Ibn al-Muqaffa's Qur'anic counterwork are either collected common wisdom or a confused religious text, not an eloquent rival.
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r5.anchor: وقد ادعى قوم أن ابن المقفع عارض القرآن وإنما فزعوا إلى الدرة والتليمية وهما كتابان

BAQILLANI:v1p32/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r6.claim: No extant work is claimed as Ibn al-Muqaffa's Qur'anic rival; the author reports that he began one, destroyed it, and may have recognized his error and inability.
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r6.anchor: بل يزعمون أنه اشتغل بذلك مدة ثم مزق ما جمع واستحيا لنفسه من إظهاره

BAQILLANI:v1p32/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r7.claim: The wisdom book attributed to Ibn al-Muqaffa is copied from Burzumihr, so it earns him no distinction.
BAQILLANI:v1p32/r7.anchor: وكتابه الذي بيناه في الحكم منسوخ من كتاب بزرجمهر في الحكمة فأي صنع له في ذلك

BURHAN:v2p137/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p137/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p137/r1.claim: The Prophet’s reports that believers bear signs of ablution and its adornment reaching as far as it does fall within God’s completing His favor and prompting gratitude.
BURHAN:v2p137/r1.anchor: وهذا كله داخل فى قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v2p137/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p137/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p137/r2.claim: The purpose-lām signals a promise and glad tidings of further blessings through laws yet to come; the Farewell Pilgrimage announcement later declared the religion complete.
BURHAN:v2p137/r2.anchor: وجاءت لام كي ها هنا إشعارا ووعدا وبشارة لهم بنعم إخرى واردة عليهم من الشرائع لم تأت بعد

BURHAN:v2p137/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p137/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p137/r11.claim: The call’s repeated declaration that God is greatest is grounded in the command to magnify God for guiding the believers.
BURHAN:v2p137/r11.anchor: وقوله الله أكبر الله أكبر من قوله

ITQAN:v1p21/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p21/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p21/r1.claim: The author says he gathered neglected material into a Qur'anic-sciences book named al-Tahbir and lists its fields.
ITQAN:v1p21/r1.anchor: سميته التحبير في علوم التفسير وهذه فهرست الأنواع بعد المقدمة

ITQAN:v1p21/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p21/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p21/r2.claim: Its revelation topics include Meccan and Medinan, place and time of revelation, occasions, first and last revelations, repetition, piecemeal or complete descent, and manner of revelation.
ITQAN:v1p21/r2.anchor: النوع الأول والثاني المكي والمدني الثالث والرابع الحضري والسفري الخامس والسادس النهاري والليلي

ITQAN:v1p21/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p21/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p21/r3.claim: Its transmission topics include mutawatir, solitary and anomalous reports, Prophetic readings, transmitters, memorisers, modes of transmission, chain height, and musalsal reports.
ITQAN:v1p21/r3.anchor: الحادي والعشرون المتواتر الثاني والعشرون الآحاد الثالث والعشرون الشاذ الرابع والعشرون قراءات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v1p21/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p21/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p21/r4.claim: Its recitation-performance topics include beginnings, pauses, imala, lengthening, easing hamza, idgham, ikhfa, iqlab, and articulation points.

ITQAN:v1p21/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p21/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p21/r5.claim: Its language and interpretation topics include rare and foreign words, metaphor, homonyms, synonyms, and clear versus ambiguous verses.

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r1.claim: The author recommends frequent Qur'an recitation and supports it with reports of its merits.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r1.anchor: يستحب الإكثار من قراءة القرآن وتلاوته قال تعالى مثنيا على من كان ذلك دأبه

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r2.claim: In a report in both Sahih collections, Ibn Umar says the only envy allowed is for one given the Qur'an who recites and lives by it day and night.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r2.anchor: وفي الصحيحين من حديث ابن عمر لا حسد إلا في اثنتين رجل آتاه الله القرآن فهو يقوم به آناء الليل وآناء النهار

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Ibn Masud that each Qur'anic letter earns one good deed, multiplied tenfold.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r3.anchor: وروى الترمذي من حديث ابن مسعود من قرأ حرفا من كتاب الله فله به حسنة والحسنة بعشر أمثالها

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r4.claim: A report from Abu Sa'id says God gives the person occupied with Qur'an and remembrance more than those who ask, and God's speech surpasses all other speech as God surpasses creation.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r4.anchor: وأخرج من حديث أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الرب سبحانه وتعالى من شغله القرآن وذكري عن مسألتي

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r5.claim: Muslim reports from Abu Umama that the Qur'an will intercede for its companions on the Day of Resurrection.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r5.anchor: وأخرج مسلم من حديث أبي أمامة اقرؤوا القرآن فإنه يأتي يوم القيامة شفيعا لأصحابه

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r6.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reports from Aisha that a house where the Qur'an is recited appears to heaven's inhabitants like stars appear to earth's inhabitants.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r6.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي من حديث عائشة البيت الذي يقرأ فيه القرآن يتراءى لأهل السماء كما تتراءى النجوم لأهل الأرض

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r7.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r7.claim: A report from Anas urges people to illuminate their homes with prayer and Qur'an recitation.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r7.anchor: وأخرج من حديث أنس نوروا منازلكم بالصلاة وقراءة القرآن

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r8.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r8.claim: A report from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir calls Qur'an recitation the best worship of the Muslim community.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r8.anchor: وأخرج من حديث النعمان بن بشير أفضل عبادة أمتي قراءة القرآن

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r9.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r9.claim: A report from Samura ibn Jundub likens the Qur'an to God's banquet and warns its people not to abandon it.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r9.anchor: وأخرج من حديث سمرة بن جندب كل مؤدب يحب أن تؤتى مأدبته ومأدبة الله القرآن فلا تهجروه

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r10.speaker: عبيدة المكي
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r10.claim: A report attributed to Ubada al-Makki, both raised and stopped, urges Qur'an readers not to pillow on it, but to recite, share, and reflect on it day and night.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r10.anchor: وأخرج من حديث عبيدة المكي مرفوعا وموقوفا يا أهل القرآن لا تتوسدوا القرآن وأتلوه حق تلاوته

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r11.claim: Some early Muslims completed the Qur'an eight times per day and night, four times by day and four by night; others completed it four, three, two, or once daily.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r11.anchor: وقد كان للسلف في قدر القراءة عادات فأكثر ما ورد في كثرة القراءة من كان يختم في اليوم والليلة ثماني ختمات

ITQAN:v1p276#2/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r12.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r12.claim: Aisha criticized people who completed the Qur'an twice or thrice in one night, saying they recited without truly reciting; with the Prophet she heard al-Baqara, Al Imran, and al-Nisa, pausing at glad tidings to supplicate and at warnings to seek refuge.
ITQAN:v1p276#2/r12.anchor: وقد ذمت عائشة ذلك فأخرج ابن أبي داود عن مسلم بن مخراق قال قلت لعائشة إن رجالا يقرأ أحدهم القرآن في ليلة مرتين أو ثلاثا فقالت قرؤوا ولم يقرؤوا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r2.speaker: أبو قتادة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r2.claim: Abu Qatada reports that the Prophet said Quran revelation began for him on Monday and that Ramadan was the first month in which the Quran was sent down, citing this verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r2.anchor: عن أبي قتادة: أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله أرأيت صوم يوم الاثنين؟ قال: "فيه أنزل علي القرآن وأول شهر أنزل فيه القرآن شهر رمضان

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r3.speaker: واثلة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r3.claim: Wathila reports the Prophet's chronology of scripture revelation: the Suhuf of Abraham on Ramadan's first night, the Torah on day six, the Gospel on day thirteen, the Psalms on day eighteen, and the Quran on day twenty-four.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r3.anchor: عن واثلة أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: "نزلت صحف إبراهيم أول ليلة من رمضان، وأنزلت التوراة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p459#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p459#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p459#2/r1.claim: Furqān derives from tafrīq; farq is the splitting open of a thing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p459#2/r1.anchor: الفرقان : فعلان من التفريق . والفرق : الفلق من الشيء إذا انفلق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p459#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p459#2/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p459#2/r3.claim: Furqān can mean a way out in religion from error and doubt.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p459#2/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الفرقان في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r1.claim: In ordinary Arabic ṣawm is abstention in general; horses are called fasting when they stop moving, and wind when it stops blowing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r1.anchor: الصوم في اللغة : الامساك في الجملة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r2.claim: The cited line’s word ṣiyām describes horses that refrain from moving beneath the dust and chew their reins.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r2.anchor: خيل صيام وخيل غير صائمة … تحت العجاج وأخرى تعلك اللجما

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r3.speaker: author
