IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r3.claim: In religious law fasting is abstaining from food, drink, and sex together with the intention.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r3.anchor: والصوم في الشريعة : الإمساك عن الطعام والشراب ، والجماع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r4.claim: One Qur’anic sense of ṣawm is the legally prescribed fast.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p386/r4.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الصوم في القرآن على وجهين : -

THALABI:v2p74/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p74/r1.claim: The preceding clause says the purpose is that people give thanks for God's favors.

QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r4.claim: Ramadan burns sins for some and ego-forms for others: mercy burns the former’s sins, while reality burns the latter’s forms.
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r4.anchor: رمضان يرمض ذنوب قوم ويرمض رسوم قوم

QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r5.claim: Ramadan is the month of divine address and revelation, reward and nearness, eased burden and intimacy, mercy and blessing, rescue and intimate prayer.

QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r6.claim: God wills ease even when the servant thinks He wills hardship; a sign is that He has made the servant seek ease, as an anonymous poem says God taught the request only if He intended its fulfillment.
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r6.anchor: قال قائلهم : لو لم ترد نيل ما أرجو

QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r7.claim: The explicit denial of hardship confirms the divine specification and removes possibilities raised by conjecture.
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r7.anchor: حيث قال : { ولا يريد بكم العسر }

QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r8.claim: Outwardly, completing the count means completing the fasting period; inwardly, it means joining a pure state to a fulfilled final outcome.
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r8.anchor: على لسان العلم تكملوا مدة الصوم

QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r9.claim: The servant should magnify God and give thanks at the final breath, leaving life with sound faith; finishing the fast is great, but ending life in felicity is greater.
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r9.anchor: وتخرجوا من مدة عمركم بسلامة إيمانكم

BURHAN:v4p95/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p95/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p95/r6.claim: The source describes the first wording as particular and the repeated wording as general, while both retain the same genus, as with God’s custom and Ramadan/the month.
BURHAN:v4p95/r6.anchor: فهما وان اختلفا يكون الاول خاصا والثاني عاما متفقان بالجنس

BURHAN:v1p115/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p115/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p115/r7.claim: Al-Baqarah first says ومن كان مريضا in the fasting passage, then restates the condition as فمن كان منكم مريضا.
BURHAN:v1p115/r7.anchor: فى البقرة ﴿ فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه ومن كان مريضا ﴾ ثم قال ﴿ فمن كان منكم مريضا ﴾

BURHAN:v4p284/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p284/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p284/r1.claim: Here على means because of God's guidance; one scholar says blessings usually accompany praise without على, but this verse is answered as referring to raising the voice in takbīr.

BURHAN:v4p284/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p284/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v4p284/r2.claim: A scholar observes that blessings mentioned with praise usually lack على, unlike expressions of praise for a blessing; the cited verse is answered as loud takbīr.
BURHAN:v4p284/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم واذا ذكرت النعمة في الغالب مع الحمد لم تقترن بعلى

BURHAN:v2p183/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p183/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p183/r3.claim: The Qur'an leaves many practical details to explanation, including zakat amounts and conditions, prayer counts and times, and the rites and prohibitions of pilgrimage.
BURHAN:v2p183/r3.anchor: والثانى ككثير من أحكام الطهارة والصلاة والزكاة والصيام

BURHAN:v1p228/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p228/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p228/r1.claim: The first view says the Qur'an descended all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then gradually over twenty, twenty-three, or twenty-five years, according to the reported length of the Meccan period.
BURHAN:v1p228/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه نزل إلى سماء الدنيا ليلة القدر جملة واحدة ثم نزل بعد ذلك منجما

BURHAN:v1p228/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p228/r2.speaker: الحاكم
BURHAN:v1p228/r2.claim: Al-Hakim transmits from Ibn Abbas that the Qur'an descended at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree and then over twenty years; he grades the report sound by the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim.
BURHAN:v1p228/r2.anchor: قال الحاكم صحيح على شرط الشيخين

BURHAN:v1p228/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p228/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p228/r3.claim: A report in al-Nasaʾi says the Qur'an was placed in Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brought it down to the Prophet; its chain is sound and Hassan ibn Abi al-Ashras is trustworthy.
BURHAN:v1p228/r3.anchor: قال فصل القرآن من الذكر فوضع فى بيت العزة من السماء الدنياا

BURHAN:v1p228/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p228/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BURHAN:v1p228/r4.claim: The second view says revelation came to the lowest heaven on twenty, twenty-three, or twenty-five Nights of Decree across the corresponding years, with each year's portion then sent down gradually; Muqatil, al-Halimi, and al-Mawardi hold it.
BURHAN:v1p228/r4.anchor: وبالثانى قال مقاتل والإمام أبو عبد الله الحليمى فى المنهاج والماوردى

BURHAN:v1p228/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p228/r5.speaker: الشعبي
BURHAN:v1p228/r5.claim: The third view says revelation began on the Night of Decree and then came gradually at different times throughout the rest of the year; al-Shaʿbi and others hold it.
BURHAN:v1p228/r5.anchor: والقول الثالث أنه ابتدىء إنزاله فى ليلة القدر

BURHAN:v1p228/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p228/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p228/r6.claim: Sunni scholars agree that God's speech is sent down, but differ whether this means making the Qur'an manifest or teaching Gabriel its recitation in heaven for him to deliver on earth.
BURHAN:v1p228/r6.anchor: اتفق أهل السنة على أن كلام الله منزل واختلفوا فى معنى الإنزال

BURHAN:v1p228/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p228/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p228/r7.claim: Transmission has two forms: the Prophet leaves human form for angelic form to receive from Gabriel, or the angel assumes human form to deliver to the Prophet; the first is harder.
BURHAN:v1p228/r7.anchor: والتنزيل له طريقان أحدهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انخلع من صورة البشرية

ITQAN:v3p59/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p59/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p59/r3.claim: The compensation clause is said to be abrogated by the command to fast for those who witness the month; another view considers it operative with an implied negation.
ITQAN:v3p59/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية ﴾ قيل منسوخة بقوله ﴿ فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه ﴾ وقيل محكمة

ITQAN:v3p98/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p98/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p98/r2.claim: Linguistic metaphor uses a word outside its original assignment; one type names the whole for a part, such as 'fingers' for fingertips or 'bodies' for faces.
ITQAN:v3p98/r2.anchor: الثالث إطلاق إسم الكل على الجزء نحو

ITQAN:v3p98/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p98/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p98/r3.claim: Calling the witnessed month the whole month uses the whole for a part; al-Fakhr al-Razi explains that the command means whoever sees its beginning must fast all of it, even if later traveling.
ITQAN:v3p98/r3.anchor: أطلق الشهر وهو إسم لثلاثين ليلة وأراد جزء منه

DAMGHANI:v1p502/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r8.claim: Yusr means a concession or dispensation granted by God.
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r8.anchor: الرابع اليسر الرخصة قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r1.claim: God makes matters easier by exempting the sick and travelers from fasting.
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r1.anchor: أي أن ييسر عليكم بوضعه عنكم الصوم في السفر والمرض.

ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r2.claim: Both a doubled and a light lām form are read: litukammilū from kammala and litakmalū from kamula.
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r2.anchor: بالتشديد، ولتكملوا بالتخفيف. من كمل يكمل، وأكمل يكمل.

ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r3.claim: The conjunction continues according to the sense: God did this to ease matters and to let you complete the number; the poem coordinates mushajjaj with an implied baqiyat after bādat illā rawākid.
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r3.anchor: معطوف محمول على المعنى. (المعنى) فعل الله ذلك ليسهل عليكم ولتكملوا العدة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets “so that you may give thanks” as God’s intention, construing divine hope as will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ومعنى ولعلكم تشكرون وإرادة أن تشكروا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya assigns the hope to human beings, since literal hoping is impossible for God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r2.anchor: وجعل ابن عطية الترجي من المخلوق، إذ الترجي حقيقة يستحيل على الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r3.claim: He regards the two analyses as comparable and observes that hard duties such as fasting and retaliation end with hope of piety, while concessions such as breaking the fast end with hope of gratitude.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r3.anchor: والقولان متكافئان، وإذا كان التكليف شاقا ناسب أن يعقب بترجي التقوى،

BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r1.claim: After the earlier passage left the fasting days vague and optional for the able, naming Ramadan fixes the obligation and makes its specification more emphatic.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r1.anchor: ولما أبهم الأمر أولا في الأيام وجعله واجبا مخيرا على المطيق عين هنا وبت الأمر فيه بقوله تعالى : { شهر رمضان }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r2.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines a lunar month by the moon’s cycle from one appearance to the next; both twenty-nine and thirty days fit the name.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r2.anchor: والشهر هو الهلال الذي شأنه أن يدور دورة من حي أن يهل إلى أن يهل ثانيا سواء كانت عدة أيامه تسعا وعشرين أو ثلاثين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reports that Ramaḍān may be one of God’s names and derives it from ramḍāʾ, the intense midday heat that heats stones.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r3.anchor: يقال : هو اسم من أسماء الله سبحانه وتعالى , واشتقاقه من الرمضاء وهو اشتداد حر الحجارة من الهاجرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r4.claim: Al-Ḥarālī relates the month’s name and calendar to a year beginning with winter and the earth’s revival, placing the spring seasons in the earthly and celestial cycles.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r4.anchor: كأن هذا الشهر سمي بوقوعه زمن اشتداد الحر بترتيب أن يحسب المحرم من أول فصل الشتاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees the lunar month as the distinctive form of this community’s fast, replacing counted days with one unified month; he links its thirty nights to Muhammad’s community and the added ten nights to Moses and earlier peoples.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r5.anchor: فجعل صومهم لرؤية الشهر وجعل لهم الشهر يوما واحدا فكأنهم نقلوا من صوم أيام معدودات

BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r6.claim: God praised Ramaḍān by revealing the Qur’an in it, with its complete descent to the House of Might and the beginning of its descent to earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r6.anchor: ولما كان هذا خطاب إرقاء مدحه سبحانه وتعالى بإنزال الذكر فيه جملة إلى بيت العزة وابتدئ من إنزاله إلى الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says fasting prepares a receptive, eased understanding of the Qur’an and pairs daytime fasting with night vigil; Qur’an is an intensive form from qaraʾ, gathering books, pages, and tablets.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r7.anchor: وأظهر فيه وجه القصد في الصوم وحكمته الغيبية التي لم تجر في الكتب الأول الكتابي فقال : { الذي أنزل فيه القرآن }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r8.claim: The praise of the Qur’an’s descent in Ramaḍān also praises the month, since fasting chiefly purifies thought so people can understand the Qur’an.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p342/r8.anchor: وفي مدحه بإنزاله فيه مدح للقرآن به من حيث أشعر أن من أعظم المقاصد بمشروعيته تصفية الفكر لأجل فهم القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r2.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says fasting prepares people to reflect and understand, humbles the soul, and can raise them from ordinary belief toward the rank of the doers of good.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r2.anchor: فيه إشعار بأن طائفة الناس يعليهم الصوم أي بالتهيئة للتدبر والفهم وانكسار النفس إلى رتبة الذين آمنوا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī calls hunger a key to guidance: weakening the body for God lights the heart, purifies the soul, strengthens the body, and opens the good associated with fasting.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r3.anchor: أن مفتاح الهدى إنما هو الجوع وأن المعدة والأعضاء متى أوهنت لله نور الله سبحانه وتعالى القلب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r4.claim: Al-Ḥarālī links fasting to closed gates of Hell, opened gates of Paradise, and chained devils because fasting narrows their channels through the blood; guidance benefits all people and shines more brightly for believers and the devout.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r4.anchor: وفي إشارته لمح لما يعان به الصائم من سد أبواب النار وفتح أبواب الجنة وتصفيد الشياطين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r5.claim: The clear proofs include what the fasting person experiences: a lit heart, humbled soul, and prepared thought able to understand and witness the Qur’an’s signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r5.anchor: إعلان بذكر ما يجده الصائم من نور قلبه وانكسار نفسه وتهيئة فكره لفهمه ليشهد تلك البينات في نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī distinguishes universal, complete guidance from the Furqān, the fullest criterion that orders the ranks of reality; the unifying gathering follows only after distinction is realized.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r6.anchor: وفي حصول الفرقان عن بركة الصوم والذي هو بيان رتب ما أظهر الحق رتبه على وجهه إشعار بما يؤتاه الصائم من الجمع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī links fasting to taqwā and taqwā to discernment, citing the promise that God grants a furqān to those who are mindful of Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343/r7.anchor: فهو صوم ينبني عليه تقوى ينبني عليها فرقان كما قال تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r1.claim: Biqai prefers the literal sense of guidance, while al-Ḥarālī takes it causally as fasting that prepares understanding and produces light.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r1.anchor: فعلى ما قلته المراد بالهدى الحقيقة , وعلى ما قاله الحرالي هو مجاز علاقته السببية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r2.claim: Biqai allows guidance to mean revelation generally, including the Book and Sunna or the Mother of the Book; al-Ḥarālī’s reading can mean the Qur’an gathering all earlier scriptures.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r2.anchor: الهدى } المعرف الوحي أعم من الكتاب والسنة أو أم الكتاب أو غير ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r3.claim: Biqai explains the Furqān as the special revelation for the Arabs that also signifies the month’s unity.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r3.anchor: والفرقان هو الخاص بالعرب الذي أعرب عن وحدة الشهر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r4.claim: “Witnessing” means full presence through a clear sighting in fair weather or completing Shaʿbān when cloud hides the moon, provided one is neither ill nor travelling.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r4.anchor: أي حضر حضورا تاما برؤية بينة لوجود الصحو من غير غمام أو بإكمال عدة شعبان إن كان غيم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the wording obliges fasting even for a person who alone saw the crescent.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r5.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي شياعه إلزام لمن رأى الهلال وحده بالصوم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī calls “the month” an object by expanded syntax; the following command confirms that the month itself is fasted, rather than saying to fast within it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r6.anchor: الشهر } هو المشهود على حد ما تقول النحاة مفعول على السعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reads the wording as indicating the validity of fasting a night, transforming the earlier choice between fasting and breaking fast into a choice between fasting the night and breaking it for those given spiritual strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r7.anchor: ويظهر معناه قوله تعالى : { فليصمه } فجعله واقعا على الشهر لا واقعا على معنى : فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r8.claim: The exemption covers the sick whether they witnessed the month or not, and the traveller whether sick or healthy; witnessing here concerns residence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r8.anchor: أي سواء شهده أولا { أو على سفر } أي سواء كان مريضا أو صحيحا وهو بين بأن المراد شهوده في بلد الإقامة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥarālī understands the substitute as a counted fast; its days need not form a single lunar month, and the indefinite wording permits consecutive or separated makeup days.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r9.anchor: وفي إطلاقه إشعار بصحة وقوعه متتابعا وغير متتابع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r10.claim: Repeating the sick and traveller concession after the replacement rule prevents readers from thinking the concession was abrogated.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r10.anchor: ولما نسخ بهذا ما مر من التخيير أعاد ما للمريض والمسافر لئلا يظن نسخه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r11.claim: God intends ease by permitting the sick and traveller to break the fast and by limiting the obligatory fast to one month, rather than imposing it on everyone or extending it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p343#2/r11.anchor: أي شرع السهولة بالترخيص للمريض والمسافر وبقصر الصوم على شهر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r1.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines ease as an action that does not exhaust the soul or burden the body, and hardship as what exhausts the soul and harms the body.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r1.anchor: اليسر عمل لا يجهد النفس ولا يثقل الجسم , والعسر ما يجهد النفس ويضر الجسم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r2.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the outward ease is breaking the fast for weak bodies, while for the spiritually strong fasting itself is ease and breaking it is hardship; each verse has an outward and inward wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r2.anchor: وفي باطن هذا الظاهر إشعار لأهل القوة بأن اليسر في صومهم وأن العسر في فطر المفطر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r3.claim: Biqai says the Prophet fasted during travel and also instructed travellers to break the fast; strong scholars fasted without condemning those who broke it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r3.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصوم في رمضان في السفر ويأمر بالفطر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r4.speaker: الشعبي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says that when two options confront someone, the easier is nearer to the truth, citing this verse.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r4.anchor: قال الشعبي : إذا اختلف عليك أمران فإن أيسرهما أقربهما إلى الحق لهذه الآية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r5.claim: Completing the count means fasting through the crescent sighting, or through thirty days when clouds prevent sighting; a longer obligation could lead to days being lost or broken, as Biqai says Christians do.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r5.anchor: عدة أيام رمضان إلى رؤية الهلال إن رأيتموه وإلى انتهاء ثلاثين التي لا يمكن زيادة الشهر عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the command completes the fast by sighting when clear and by completing the count when obscured, balancing clear weather at the opening with clouds at the end.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r6.anchor: التقدير : لتوفوا الصوم بالرؤية ولتكملوا إن أغمي عليكم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r7.claim: Biqai identifies an ellipsis by reciprocal implication: the initial mention of witnessing implies no sighting at the end, while final completion for clouds implies clear weather at first.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r7.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى احتباك , فإن ذكر الشهود أولا يدل على عدمه ثانيا وذكر الإكمال لأجل الغمام ثانيا يدل على الصحو أولا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines takbīr as magnifying rank or measure, in either a physical or figurative sense.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r8.anchor: والتكبير إشراف القدر أو المقدار حسا أو معنى - قاله الحرالي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r9.claim: The name Allah the Greatest suits the occasion; people should inwardly recognize His greatness and remember it aloud on Eid and elsewhere so their hearts remain humble.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r9.anchor: لتعتقدوا عظمته بقلوبكم وتذكروها بألسنتكم في العيد وغيره ليكون ذلك أحرى بدوام الخضوع من القلوب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r10.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reads the opening crescent as an outward sign and the month's end as an inward moon of divine light revealed by fasting, expressed in the Eid prayer’s takbīr.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r10.anchor: فكما كبر في ابتداء الشهر لرؤية الهلال يكبر في انتهائه لرؤية باطنه مرأى من هلال نور ربه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r11.claim: The Sunnah’s Eid prayer in open space, with loud takbīr in both rakʿas, fits the public character of magnification and its association with God’s great creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p344/r11.anchor: وجعل في براح من متسع الأرض لمقصد التكبير لأن تكبير الله سبحانه وتعالى إنما هو بما جل من مخلوقاته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r1.claim: Since Eid brings joy and the soul may overstep from appetite or heedlessness, takbīr counters negligence and restrains its excess.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r1.anchor: لما كان العيد محل فرح وسرور وكان من طبع النفس تجاوز الحدود لما جبلت عليه من الشره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r2.claim: The seven takbīrs in the first rakʿa recall the seven rites of pilgrimage—ṭawāf, saʿy, and stoning—stirring longing for the greater Eid.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r2.anchor: وجعل سبعا في الأولى لذلك وتذكيرا بأعمال الحج السبعة من الطواف والسعي والجمار تشويقا إليها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r3.claim: Seven also recalls the seven heavens and earths, creation over six days, and Adam’s creation on Friday, the seventh day.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r3.anchor: وما فيهما في الأيام السبع لأنه خلقهما في ستة وخلق آدم في اليوم السابع يوم الجمعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r4.claim: The second rakʿa has five takbīrs as a merciful reduction and the nearest lower odd count to seven; five recalls Islam’s pillars, especially its five prayers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r4.anchor: وكانت الخمسة أقرب وترا إلى السبعة من دونها جعل تكبير الثانية خمسا لذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r5.claim: The first rakʿa signifies God’s singular greatness, dominion, and power; the second turns hearts toward worship through Islam’s five supports and especially prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r5.anchor: أشير بتكبير الثانية إلى عبادته بالإسلام المبني على الدعائم الخمس وخصوصا بأعظم دعائمه الصلوات الخمس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r6.claim: Biqai says people praise God for guiding them by making the religious laws easy, preparing them to keep and hold firmly to them; this explains the near-universal observance of fasting.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r6.anchor: يسر لكم من شرائع هذا الدين فهيأكم للزومها ودوام التمسك بعراها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī describes guidance as the fasting person’s inward illumination, including signs of Laylat al-Qadr disclosed differently to the secluded, contemplative, and watchful according to their spiritual state.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r7.anchor: إن الهداية إشارة إلى تلك الموجدة التي يجدها الصائم وما يشهده الله من بركاته من رؤية ليلة القدر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī calls the fullest guidance the fading of body and self in God; fasting is distinctive as renunciation, recalling the report that the faster leaves food and drink for God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p345/r8.anchor: فأعظم الهدى هدى المرء لأن يذبل جسمه ونفسه وتفنى ذاته في حق ربه , كما يقول : ( يدع طعامه وشرابه من أجلي )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r1.claim: Biqai explains gratitude here as being in a state from which obedience may be continued and sin avoided.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r1.anchor: أي ولتكونوا في حالة يرجى معها لزوم الطاعة واجتناب المعصية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r2.claim: Al-Ḥarālī presents gratitude as the final stage following taqwā, which is the beginning, linking this verse to the earlier hope that people become mindful.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r2.anchor: فيه تصنيف في الشكر نهاية كما كان فيه تصنيف للتقوى بداية , كما قال : { ولعلكم تتقون }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees zakāt al-fiṭr as gratitude made visible: it concludes fasting by feeding dependants and applies to the fasting person and those the person supports.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r3.anchor: وفي إشعاره إعلام بإظهار نعمة الله وشكر الإحسان الذي هو مضمون فرض زكاة الفطر عن كل صائم وعمن يطعمه الصائم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r1.claim: Shahr derives from public renown: Ramadan is a month so well known that anyone seeking it can identify it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r1.anchor: الشهر مشتق من الاشتهار لأنه مشتهر لا يتعذر علمه على أحد يريده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r2.claim: Ramadan was named for the period of intense heat and scorched ground in which it was named; it had previously been called Nāthir, as Rabīʿ and Jumādā were named for their seasons.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r2.anchor: ورمضان علقه الاسم من مدة كان فيها في الرمض وشدة الحر، وكان اسمه قبل ذلك ناثرا، كما سمي ربيع من مدة الربيع، وجمادى من مدة الجمود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r3.claim: Mujāhid disliked saying Ramadan without شهر, and suggested that Ramadan might be one of God’s names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r3.anchor: وكره مجاهد أن يقال رمضان دون أن يقال شهر رمضان كما قال الله تعالى، وقال: لعل رمضان اسم من أسماء الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r4.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r4.claim: The majority read شهر in the nominative; analyses include an understood predicate, apposition to الصيام, or an independent subject with one of several following predicates, with syntax depending on whether 2:183’s fasting means Ramadan or the earlier three days and ʿĀshūrāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r4.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «شهر» بالرفع، ووجهه خبر ابتداء أي ذلكم شهر، وقيل: بدل من الصيام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r5.speaker: مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r5.claim: Mujāhid and Shahr ibn Ḥawshab read شهر in the accusative; it is analyzed as an exhortation, as the object of تصوموا, or as an adverbial expression.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r5.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب «شهر» بالنصب، ورواها أبو عمارة عن حفص عن عاصم ورواها هارون عن أبي عمرو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r6.claim: A group assimilates the rāʾ of شهر into the rāʾ of رمضان, though Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is not required by the principles because two vowelless consonants meet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r6.anchor: وقرأت فرقة بإدغام الراء في الراء وذلك لا تقتضيه الأصول لاجتماع الساكنين فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the Qur’an was sent down in Ramadan in the sense that observance of the month was prescribed, honored, and urged.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r7.anchor: فقال الضحاك: أنزل في فرضه وتعظيمه والحض عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r8.claim: Another view says the Qur’an’s revelation to the Prophet began in Ramadan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r8.anchor: وقيل: بدىء بنزوله فيه على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qur’an descended all at once to the lowest heaven on Ramadan’s twenty-fourth night, then Gabriel delivered it in successive portions according to commands, prohibitions, and occasions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس فيما يؤثر: أنزل إلى السماء الدنيا جملة واحدة ليلة أربع وعشرين من رمضان ثم كان جبريل ينزله رسلا رسلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r10.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r10.claim: Wāthila ibn al-Asqaʿ transmits from the Prophet that Abraham’s scrolls came down on Ramadan’s first night, the Torah on the sixth, the Gospel on the thirteenth, and the Qur’an on the twenty-fourth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254/r10.anchor: وروى واثلة بن الأسقع عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «نزلت صحف إبراهيم أول ليلة من شهر رمضان والتوراة لست مضين منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir omits the hamza in al-Qurʾān whether definite or indefinite; deriving the reading from q-r-n is judged weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r1.anchor: وترك ابن كثير همزة القرآن مع التعريف والتنكير حيث وقع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r2.claim: Hudan is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the Qurʾān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r2.anchor: وهدى في موضع نصب على الحال من القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r3.claim: The whole Qurʾān, including clear and ambiguous, abrogating and abrogated passages, is guidance; bayyināt specifies lawful and unlawful rulings, admonitions, and decisive verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r3.anchor: فالمراد أن القرآن بجملته من محكم ومتشابه وناسخ ومنسوخ هدى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r4.claim: The definite article in al-hudā is anaphoric, referring back to earlier guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r4.anchor: فالألف واللام في الهدى للعهد والمراد الأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r5.claim: Al-furqān is that which distinguishes truth from falsehood.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r6.claim: Shahida means present; al-shahr is temporal, meaning presence in town during the month.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r6.anchor: وشهد بمعنى حضر، والشهر نصب على الظرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r7.speaker: الحسن وعيسى الثقفي والزهري وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وأبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r7.claim: These readers vocalize the lām of fal-yasumhu; they similarly read every imperative lām in the Qurʾān with its original kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى الثقفي والزهري وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وأبو حيوة «فليصمه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وعبيدة السلماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r8.claim: Whoever was resident when Ramadan began must complete the fast even if he later travels; only one already traveling when Ramadan begins may break it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r8.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وعبيدة السلماني: من شهد أي من حضر دخول الشهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r9.speaker: جمهور الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r9.claim: The majority require fasting while resident if one witnesses either the beginning or end of the month.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r9.anchor: وقال جمهور الأمة: من شهد أول الشهر أو آخره فليصم ما دام مقيما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions require legal capacity during the month; insanity throughout Ramadan entails no make-up, while insanity at its beginning or end requires making up those days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: من شهد الشهر بشروط التكليف غير مجنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r11.claim: On Abu Hanifa’s interpretation, al-shahr is the direct object of shahida.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r11.anchor: ونصب الشهر على هذا التأويل هو على المفعول الصريح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r12.claim: “Or on a journey” functions like “or traveling,” so it coordinates with a noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r12.anchor: وقوله تعالى: أو على سفر بمنزلة أو مسافرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع ويحيى بن وثاب وابن هرمز وعيسى بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r13.claim: These readers pronounce the sīn of al-yusr and al-ʿusr with ḍamma; the majority leave it quiescent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع ويحيى بن وثاب وابن هرمز وعيسى بن عمر «اليسر» و «العسر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r14.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك بن مزاحم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r14.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak identify ease with breaking the fast while traveling and hardship with fasting during travel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك بن مزاحم: اليسر الفطر في السفر والعسر الصوم في السفر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r15.claim: The wording should encompass ease and hardship throughout religious matters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r15.anchor: والوجه عموم اللفظ في جميع أمور الدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r16.claim: The Prophet described God’s religion as easy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r16.anchor: وقد فسر ذلك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «دين الله يسر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r17.claim: Those who missed days because of travel or illness are to complete the corresponding number of days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r17.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ولتكملوا العدة معناه وليكمل من أفطر في سفره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r18.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r18.claim: Abu Bakr from ʿĀṣim and some transmissions from Abu ʿAmr read litukammilū with a doubled mīm; a light mīm is also transmitted and is the majority reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r18.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو في بعض ما روي عنه «ولتكملوا» بتشديد الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r19.speaker: البصريون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r19.claim: The Basrans attach the lām to yurīdu as an object lām, with an implied an after the verb; Qays Kathīr ibn Ṣakhr’s line illustrates it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r19.anchor: هذه اللام متعلقة إما ب يريد فهي اللام الداخلة على المفعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r20.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r20.claim: Some Kufans connect the lām to an omitted following verb: the dispensation was granted so people could complete the number.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r20.anchor: وإما بفعل مضمر بعد، تقديره ولأن تكملوا العدة رخص لكم هذه الرخصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r21.claim: Alternatively, the lām may be imperative, with the wāw coordinating one sentence with another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p254#2/r21.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون هذه اللام لام الأمر والواو عاطفة جملة كلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r1.claim: The command to magnify God urges takbīr at the end of Ramadan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r1.anchor: وقوله: ولتكبروا الله حض على التكبير في آخر رمضان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says takbīr begins at crescent sighting and lasts until the sermon ends; one pauses when the imam goes out, then repeats his takbīr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: «يكبر المرء من رؤية الهلال إلى انقضاء الخطبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r3.claim: Another view starts takbīr at crescent sighting and continues until the imam leaves for prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: يكبر من رؤية الهلال إلى خروج الإمام إلى الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r4.speaker: سفيان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r4.claim: Sufyan takes the command to mean takbīr on Eid day.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r5.claim: Malik says takbīr runs from when a man leaves home until the imam comes out.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r5.anchor: وقال مالك: «هو من حين يخرج الرجل من منزله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r6.claim: Scholars use several formulas; all are acceptable, beginning with takbīr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r6.anchor: والجميع حسن واسع مع البدأة بالتكبير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r7.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r7.claim: Some take “He guided you” specifically as guidance away from Christians’ alteration of their fast.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد لما ضل فيه النصارى من تبديل صيامهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r8.claim: A general sense of guidance is better.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r9.claim: The expectation of gratitude is phrased in terms appropriate to human beings, for God’s gift of guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r9.anchor: ولعلكم تشكرون ترج في حق البشر، أي على نعمة الله في الهدى

JISHUMI:v1p766/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p766/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p766/r1.claim: The author reports disagreement over travel fasting: some treat breaking the fast as obligatory and others as a concession; most prefer fasting, while some prefer breaking it.

JISHUMI:v1p758/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p758/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p758/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa permits making the intention for Ramadan during the day; al-Shāfiʿī does not.
JISHUMI:v1p758/r8.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة تجوز بالنهار، وقال الشافعي لا تجوز،

RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r1.claim: A second interpretation takes magnifying God as glorifying Him in gratitude for enabling this act of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r1.anchor: القول الثاني : في تفسير قوله : { ولتكبروا الله } أن المراد منه التعظيم لله شكرا

RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r2.claim: Complete magnification comprises speech affirming God's attributes and names and denying unworthy comparisons, inward belief, and worship through acts such as prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r2.anchor: أن تمام هذا التكبير إنما يكون بالقول والاعتقاد والعمل أما القول : فالإقرار بصفاته العلي

RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r3.claim: Razi prefers the first interpretation: magnification is commanded at all times, so specifying this worship implies a special feature beyond ordinary magnification.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r3.anchor: واعلم أن القول الأول أقرب ، وذلك لأن تكبير الله تعالى بهذا التفسير واجب في جميع الأوقات

RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r4.claim: The guidance includes great worldly blessings: evidence, instruction, enabling, and protection.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r4.anchor: فإنه يتضمن الإنعام العظيم في الدنيا بالأدلة والتعريف والتوفيق والعصمة

RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r5.claim: Razi says his school's account also includes God's creating the act of obedience among the blessings of guidance.

RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r6.claim: Mentioning gratitude after magnification directs servants who recognize God's majesty and transcendence, and His special gift of guidance, to thank and praise Him as they can.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80/r6.anchor: ثم يعلم أنه سبحانه مع جلاله وعزته واستغنائه عن جميع المخلوقات ، فضلا عن هذا المسكين خصه الله بهذه الهداية العظيمة

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r1.claim: After the fasting rulings, magnification, and gratitude, God's nearness assures worshippers that He knows their remembrance, hears their call, answers prayer, and does not disappoint hope.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r1.anchor: بين أنه سبحانه بلطفه ورحمته قريب من العبد مطلع على ذكره وشكره فيسمع نداءه ، ويجيب دعاءه ، ولا يخيب رجاءه

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r2.claim: The order places praise before supplication, as Abraham first praised God and then prayed; Razi compares this sequence with Abraham's words.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r2.anchor: تنبيها على أن الدعاء لا بد وأن يكون مسبوقا بالثناء الجميل

BURHAN:v3p165/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p165/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p165/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats الشهر as an omitted object, understanding “whoever witnessed the month” as whoever was present in town during it.
BURHAN:v3p165/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري من حذف المفعول قوله

BURHAN:v3p165/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p165/r3.speaker: أبو علي
BURHAN:v3p165/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī instead takes الشهر as an adverbial expression, estimating “whoever witnessed the town during the month.”
BURHAN:v3p165/r3.anchor: وعند أبي على أن الشهر ظرف والتقدير فمن شهد منكم المصر في الشهر
